The plate rests on a light bamboo table surface, showcasing its natural texture. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, and the background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of natural elements or plants, creating an eco-conscious and serene dining ambiance.
instructions: Prepare zero-waste vegetable broth: Collect vegetable scraps (carrot peels, onion ends, mushroom stems). Place in a pot with 1 liter of water. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.

Prepare quick-pickled cabbage: Thinly shred cabbage. In a heatproof bowl, combine 250 ml water, white vinegar, sugar, a pinch of salt, and a few lemon slices. Heat until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over shredded cabbage. Let cool and marinate for at least 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Dice carrots into 2 cm chunks. Dice half of the onion into 2 cm chunks. Toss carrots and diced onion with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Chop remaining half onion. Mince garlic. Halve or quarter mushrooms depending on size.

Cook bulgur: In a medium saucepan, combine bulgur with 500 ml of the zero-waste vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and bulgur is tender. Fluff with a fork.

While bulgur cooks, heat 20 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chopped onion and sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes, until mushrooms are golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine roasted carrots, roasted onion, and sautéed mushrooms with the cooked bulgur. Stir gently to combine.
Serve the bulgur mixture in bowls. Top each portion with a generous spoonful of quick-pickled cabbage. Garnish with thinly sliced green onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork and Cabbage Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of the braised pork and cabbage is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The pork, cut into 3-4 cm cubes, is tender and coated in a rich, dark golden-brown sauce. The cabbage, appearing as 2-3 cm wide wedges and soft shreds, has absorbed the braising liquid. Components are naturally piled, touching and overlapping, reflecting a hearty, comforting meal. A few vibrant green specks of fresh chopped parsley are scattered on top. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. A single, sturdy metal fork is placed next to the bowl. Lighting is soft and warm, suggesting natural light, creating an inviting, unpretentious scene.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season pork generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown pork cubes on all sides in batches. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn.
Stir in smoked paprika and dried thyme. Cook for 30 seconds.
Deglaze the pan with apple cider vinegar, scraping up any browned bits.
Return pork to the skillet. Add broth and Dijon mustard. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until pork is very tender.
Add cored cabbage wedges or thick shreds to the skillet. Stir gently to submerge in liquid.
Cover and cook for another 20-30 minutes, or until cabbage is tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Velvet Coconut Tofu Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous slice of Velvet Coconut Tofu Cake rests on an off-white, simple round ceramic plate. The cake slice is golden-brown on the edges with a tender, moist crumb visible on the cut side. A thin, white coconut glaze softly drips down the sides of the slice, pooling slightly at the base. The texture of the cake is soft and slightly dense. The plate is casually placed on a rustic wooden dining table, showing natural grain and a lived-in feel. In the background, the remaining whole cake sits on a simple cooling rack or cake stand, also coated with the subtle white glaze. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. A casually draped, light-colored cloth napkin is visible nearby. The setting is a homely family kitchen, focusing on comfort and simplicity. The overall presentation is unpretentious, highlighting the cake as a comforting, homemade dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and flour a 15 cm (6-inch) round cake pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together gluten-free flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a blender, combine silken tofu, coconut milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently with a whisk or spatula until just combined. Do not overmix. A few small lumps are fine.
Pour batter into the prepared cake pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar and coconut cream until smooth. Add more coconut cream if needed for desired consistency.
Once cake is completely cool, drizzle glaze over the top. Let glaze set before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Dark Beer Braised Beef with Fermented Cabbage & Carrot Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Dark Beer Braised Beef is presented on a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate with a natural, unglazed rim. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface. Three substantial, irregularly shaped chunks of deeply browned, fork-tender beef are nestled centrally, partially submerged in a rich, dark, glossy braising sauce. Scattered among the beef are tender, rustic-cut carrot pieces from the braise. Alongside, a mound of fluffy, earthy brown rice provides a textural contrast. A vibrant, glistening spoonful of quick-fermented julienned cabbage and carrot relish, showcasing bright orange and pale green hues, is placed next to the beef, adding a fresh, acidic counterpoint. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing natural colors and textures to shine. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting its rustic elegance. A simple, undyed linen napkin is subtly placed to the side. The background is clean and unfussy, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Relish: Combine 400g shredded cabbage and 100g julienned carrot in a clean bowl. Add 10g non-iodized salt. Massage vigorously for 5-7 minutes until vegetables release liquid. Pack tightly into a clean 1-litre jar. Pour any released liquid over. If needed, add filtered water to cover vegetables completely. Place a small weight to keep vegetables submerged. Seal loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.

Sear Beef: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and 100g diced carrots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Deglaze and Build Braise: Pour dark beer into the pot. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer. Add diced tomatoes, vegetable stock, bay leaves, and thyme sprigs. Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged.
Braise: Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot tightly. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.

Cook Brown Rice: While beef braises, rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 400 ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Serve: Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs from the braise. Season braising liquid with salt and pepper to taste. Ladle braised beef and its rich sauce over individual portions of brown rice. Top each serving with a generous spoonful of the fermented cabbage and carrot relish.

recipes.recipe_name: Bulgur & Mushroom Patties with Quick-Pickled Red Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown, pan-seared bulgur and mushroom patties rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone. Two thick, round patties are centrally placed, showing their slightly crispy, earthy crust. A vibrant mound of thinly sliced, quick-pickled red onion in a rich purple hue is artfully arranged atop one patty, providing a striking color contrast. Alongside, a fresh salad of vibrant green spinach leaves and bright orange julienned carrots is casually mounded. The dish is garnished with a few fresh basil leaves, adding a pop of green. The overall plating is minimalistic, allowing ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting from the side. The background is clean and unobtrusive, hinting at natural elements.
instructions: Prepare quick-pickled red onion: Thinly slice red onion. Combine apple cider vinegar, water, 5 ml salt in a small pot. Bring to a boil. Pour over sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Cook bulgur: Rinse bulgur. Place in a bowl. Pour 400 ml boiling water over bulgur. Cover. Let stand 15 minutes until tender. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare patty mixture: Dice yellow onion and mushrooms. Mince garlic. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté yellow onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and garlic. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a large bowl.
Form patties: Add cooked bulgur, Dijon mustard, 15 ml chopped fresh basil to the mushroom mixture. Mix well. Form into 8 patties, about 2 cm thick.
Cook patties: Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook patties 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Prepare carrot-spinach salad: Wash spinach. Julienne carrots. In a bowl, combine spinach and carrots. Dress lightly with lemon juice, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Plate: Arrange two patties on each plate. Top with quick-pickled red onion. Serve alongside the carrot-spinach salad. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Potato and Kale Salad with Lemon-Herb Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Shredded dark green kale forms the bed, lightly tossed with dressing, peeking through the other components. Over this, golden-orange roasted sweet potato cubes, with their slightly caramelized edges, are artfully scattered. Interspersed are tender, off-white diced chicken pieces, ensuring they are distinct and not fanned. Bright red dried cranberries and delicate slivers of thinly sliced red onion add pops of contrasting color. Roughly chopped, toasted pecans provide a warm brown hue and a crunchy texture. Crumbled white feta cheese adds creamy contrast and a savory touch. The lemon-maple vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients, providing a subtle sheen without pooling. The arrangement is natural and flowing, allowing each component to be visible without overcrowding. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, set on a simple wooden surface, creating a casual yet refined bistro ambiance.

ingredients.name: Sweet potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approximately 400g total), peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).

In a bowl, toss chicken breasts with 15 ml olive oil, 15 ml lemon juice, oregano, garlic powder, 3 g salt, and 2 g pepper. Place on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Let rest 5 minutes. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes.

While chicken cooks, toss diced sweet potatoes with 15 ml olive oil, smoked paprika, 3 g salt, and 2 g pepper on a separate baking sheet. Roast in the same oven for 20-25 minutes, turning once, until tender and slightly caramelized.
In a large bowl, combine shredded kale with a drizzle of olive oil (about 5ml) and a pinch of salt. Massage kale with hands for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Add chopped pecans. Toast for 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant. Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together 80 ml olive oil, 45 ml lemon juice, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, chopped parsley, 2 g salt, and 1 g pepper until emulsified.

Add roasted sweet potatoes, diced chicken, thinly sliced red onion, dried cranberries, toasted pecans, and crumbled feta to the bowl with the massaged kale. Pour vinaigrette over salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Divide salad among four plates. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty beef stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The stew fills the bowl, showcasing tender, browned beef chunks, soft, chunky potatoes, and vibrant orange carrot pieces nestled in a rich, dark brown, slightly glossy gravy. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, unpretentious look. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a functional garnish and a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table with visible grain. Beside the bowl, a simple, off-white ceramic plate holds a slice of crusty bread. A plain, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone and a sturdy, everyday metal fork are casually placed. Warm, cozy lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the steam gently rising from the stew. The background hints at a lived-in kitchen, slightly blurred, maintaining focus on the food. Beef chuck is cut into 3-4 cm cubes, carrots into 2 cm chunks, and potatoes into 3 cm chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Serve with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to cook off raw flour taste.
Pour in red wine (if using) and beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add dried thyme and bay leaves.
Add potatoes. Ensure liquid covers most ingredients. Add more broth if needed.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Cook on low heat for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best flavor, brown the beef well in batches.
Stew can be made ahead and reheats well. Flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tofu Coconut Cream Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of the Fermented Tofu Coconut Cream Cake is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake slice is neat, showcasing distinct layers: a compact, golden-brown crust at the bottom, topped by a smooth, ivory-white, creamy tofu-coconut layer. A vibrant, deep ruby-red berry coulis is artfully spooned alongside, creating a natural, flowing pool. The surface of the cake is unadorned, highlighting its pure, clean texture. The plate is positioned on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige subtly folded beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the cake's subtle hues and delicate structure. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery for an eco-conscious feel, avoiding any clutter.
instructions: Press silken tofu to remove excess water. Crumble into a clean bowl. Stir in vegan yogurt. Cover loosely with a cloth. Let ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours, or until slightly tangy.

Combine bread crumbs, ground nuts, melted coconut oil, and date paste in a bowl. Mix until well combined. Press mixture firmly into the bottom of four small individual ramekins or a 15 cm springform pan lined with parchment paper. Chill while preparing the filling.
Blend fermented tofu, coconut cream, maple syrup, lemon juice, vanilla extract, and sea salt until completely smooth and creamy.
In a small saucepan, whisk agar-agar powder with 50ml of the tofu mixture until dissolved. Heat over medium heat, whisking constantly, until mixture boils for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Slowly whisk the hot agar-agar mixture into the remaining tofu blend. Pour the mixture evenly over the chilled crusts in the prepared ramekins/pan.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until fully set.

Combine berries, water, and maple syrup in a small saucepan. Simmer over low heat for 10-15 minutes, mashing berries. Add lemon zest. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds and pulp, pressing to extract all liquid. Let cool.
Carefully unmold the cakes. Spoon berry coulis over each cake before serving.
notes: Fermentation time for tofu may vary based on ambient temperature and desired tanginess. Taste periodically.
The leftover berry pulp from the coulis can be incorporated into smoothies or baked goods to minimize waste.
Use gluten-free bread crumbs for a fully gluten-free cake.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Turkey Meatball Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Turkey Meatball Pasta Bake is presented in a well-used, rustic ceramic baking dish, hinting at family comfort. Modest portions of baked penne pasta are coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce, interspersed with generously sized, browned turkey meatballs. The meatballs are whole and round, not cut. Melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese forms a golden-brown crust over the top, with some strands stretching invitingly. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered casually on top for color and aroma. The dish sits on a warm, worn wooden dining table. A simple ceramic plate, a metal fork, and a folded cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish at the table.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese as an optional topping.
Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, finely diced onion, minced garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, milk, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Mix gently until just combined.
Form the mixture into 2.5 cm diameter meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear meatballs in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Pour crushed tomatoes over the browned meatballs. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10 minutes, ensuring meatballs are cooked through.
Stir the cooked pasta into the sauce with the meatballs.
Evenly top the pasta and meatballs with shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure turkey meatballs reach an internal temperature of 74°C (165°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Shakshuka
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hearty Shakshuka is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The vibrant, reddish-orange tomato sauce, rich with diced red bell pepper and onion, cradles two perfectly poached eggs. The egg whites are fully set and bright white, contrasting with the glistening, soft orange yolks. The sauce has a slightly chunky texture from the vegetables and a subtle sheen from the olive oil. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley covers the top, adding a fresh burst of color. The dish is presented on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, off-white ceramic plate with minor imperfections sits underneath the bowl. A plain, loosely folded cloth napkin and a metal fork are casually placed beside it. The lighting is warm and natural, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Serve with a side of plain yogurt or labneh.
Serve with a simple green salad.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and diced red bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Make 8 small indentations in the sauce. Carefully crack one egg into each indentation.
Cover the skillet. Cook for 7-10 minutes, or until egg whites are set and yolks are still runny.
Remove from heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro.
Serve hot directly from the skillet or spoon individual portions into bowls.

recipes.recipe_name: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelette)
recipes.visual_description: A single, round Tortilla Española is presented as the centerpiece on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A generous wedge is cut from the tortilla and rests slightly askew beside the main piece, revealing the soft, pale yellow interior studded with tender white potato slices and translucent, caramelized onion pieces. The tortilla's exterior boasts a beautiful, even golden-brown crust. The overall appearance is hearty and comforting, with a natural, home-cooked feel. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, lightly textured. A simple, dark-handled fork rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, soft lighting, emanating from a kitchen fixture, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen environment. A piece of crusty rustic bread or a small bowl of olives could be subtly placed in the background to enhance the Spanish authenticity without distracting from the dish.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into thin, even slices or small cubes (about 3-4 mm thick).
Peel and thinly slice the onion.
Heat olive oil in a 24-26 cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Add potatoes and onion to the pan. Ensure they are submerged in oil. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes. Potatoes should become very tender, not browned. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Once tender, remove potatoes and onion from the oil using a slotted spoon. Drain well. Reserve the oil for other uses or discard.
Crack eggs into a large bowl. Whisk lightly with salt.
Add the drained potatoes and onion to the egg mixture. Stir gently to combine. Let sit for 5 minutes so eggs absorb flavor.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the reserved olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Ensure pan is hot.
Pour the egg and potato mixture into the hot pan. Spread evenly. Cook for 5-7 minutes. Edges should set and turn golden brown.
Place a large, flat plate over the pan. Invert the pan quickly to flip the tortilla onto the plate.
Slide the tortilla carefully back into the pan, uncooked side down. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until golden brown and set in the center.
Slide the finished tortilla onto a clean serving plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Shakshuka with Bell Pepper
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Shakshuka is presented in a small, rustic ceramic dish with a slightly uneven, natural finish. The vibrant red tomato and bell pepper sauce fills the dish, with small, evenly diced red bell pepper and onion visible throughout. Two perfectly poached eggs are nestled into shallow wells within the sauce, their whites set firm but still tender, encasing bright, slightly runny golden yolks. A generous sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped parsley and cilantro leaves covers the surface, adding bursts of green color and fresh aroma. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a torn piece of warm pita bread, ready for dipping. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, illuminated by warm, inviting light, with minimal, unobtrusive background elements. The focus is entirely on the hearty, comforting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with warm pita bread for scooping
Offer a side of labneh or crumbled feta cheese
Accompany with a simple cucumber and tomato salad
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and diced red bell pepper. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, cumin powder, smoked paprika, chili flakes, salt, and black pepper.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce slightly thickens.
Using a spoon, create 4 small wells in the simmering sauce.
Carefully crack one egg into each well.
Cover the skillet. Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until egg whites are set and yolks reach desired consistency.
Remove from heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and coriander.
Serve hot, directly from the skillet or portion into individual bowls.
notes: Adjust chili flakes for desired spice level
Ensure sauce is simmering gently before adding eggs for even poaching
traditional_techniques: Sautéing aromatics to build flavor base
Poaching eggs directly in simmering sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Coconut Tofu Cheesecake
recipes.visual_description: An elegant single slice of Baked Coconut Tofu Cheesecake sits on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The crust is a golden-brown, firm layer at the base. The cheesecake filling is smooth, creamy, and off-white, with a soft, uniform texture. Lightly toasted coconut flakes are sprinkled gracefully over the top surface. A few vibrant fresh raspberries are placed artfully beside the slice for a pop of color. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. In the soft-focused background, the whole round cheesecake rests on a simple cake stand. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a clean, inviting bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a 20 cm springform pan with parchment paper.
Crush digestive biscuits finely. Melt dairy-free butter. Combine biscuits and butter. Press mixture firmly into the bottom of the prepared pan.
Bake crust for 10 minutes. Remove from oven. Let cool.
Combine silken tofu, coconut milk, coconut cream, sugar, cornstarch, vanilla extract, and lemon juice in a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
Pour tofu mixture over the cooled crust in the springform pan.
Place the springform pan in a larger roasting pan. Pour hot water into the roasting pan, reaching halfway up the side of the springform pan.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center still has a slight wobble.
Turn off the oven. Leave the cheesecake in the oven with the door ajar for 30 minutes. Remove from water bath.
Cool completely on a wire rack. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
Before serving, sprinkle toasted coconut flakes on top. Garnish with fresh berries.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Bolognese with Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of golden tagliatelle pasta, expertly swirled into a neat mound, is centered on a clean white round porcelain plate. Rich, deep red turkey bolognese sauce, abundant with tender ground turkey and finely diced soffritto vegetables, is generously spooned over the pasta. The sauce glistens invitingly. Rustic shavings of aged Pecorino Romano cheese are scattered liberally over the top, adding contrasting texture and a pale ivory hue. A few vibrant green fresh basil leaves are placed artfully for a pop of color and aromatic freshness. The composition is balanced, showcasing warmth and heartiness. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table. A neatly folded light cotton napkin and a silver fork are positioned beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the dish's colors and textures, creating an appealing casual dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Dice onion, carrots, and celery into small, uniform pieces.
Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add ground turkey to the pot. Break apart with a spoon. Cook until turkey is browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine mostly evaporates.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken broth to the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sauce will thicken.
Season sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with generous shavings of Pecorino Romano cheese and fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Mushroom-Mustard Cream Sauce
recipes.special_requests: Кухня для спорта без свиной вырезки
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Mushroom-Mustard Cream Sauce is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Two thick, seared pork loin medallions, golden-brown from pan-searing, are nestled in a rich, creamy, light-brown mushroom-mustard sauce. The sauce, speckled with tender, sautéed cremini mushroom slices and finely minced shallots, generously coats the pork. Beside the pork, a portion of roasted potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes, display a golden-crisp exterior and a fluffy interior. A sprinkle of vibrant chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. Standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate on the light wooden surface. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and warm tones.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cube potatoes into 2 cm pieces. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 25-30 minutes until golden and tender.
Pat pork loin dry. Cut into 4 medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 63°C internal temperature. Remove pork from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallot and cook 2 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the skillet. Simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in Dijon mustard and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add shredded Gruyère cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return pork medallions to the skillet with the sauce. Simmer 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Serve pork and sauce immediately with roasted potatoes. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Garlic-Chili Glaze & Charred Corn
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-on, exhibits a deep golden-brown, crispy skin, resting beside a modest mound of vibrant yellow charred corn kernels. The chicken is generously coated with a glossy, rich reddish-brown fermented garlic-chili glaze. A subtle pool of pale golden corn husk broth reduction lightly frames the chicken and corn. The plating is minimalistic, utilizing ample white space on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The chicken is presented as a whole, substantial piece, not sliced. The charred corn kernels are loosely arranged, showcasing their natural texture and slightly browned edges. A few small, fresh green micro herb leaves are sparingly scattered for a hint of contrasting color. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, and soft, diffused natural light from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of blurred natural greenery.
instructions: Separate husks and cobs from corn. Place corn husks and cobs in a saucepan with 750 ml water and optional bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Strain the liquid, discard solids. Return liquid to pan. Reduce liquid by half over medium-high heat. Set aside.

Brush corn cobs with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Season with salt. Char corn cobs directly over a high flame or in a hot cast-iron pan until kernels are lightly browned and slightly softened. Cut kernels from cobs using a sharp knife. Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together fermented garlic paste, hot sauce, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup (if using), and 2 tablespoons water or chicken broth. This is your glaze.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear undisturbed for 8-10 minutes, until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.
Continue cooking chicken for 6-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at its thickest part. Remove chicken from pan and let it rest on a cutting board.

If pan is dry, add a splash of water or broth to deglaze. Pour the prepared glaze mixture into the hot skillet. Bring to a simmer and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until glaze slightly thickens and becomes glossy.

To plate, spoon charred corn kernels onto each plate. Place one seared chicken thigh next to the corn. Drizzle chicken generously with the fermented garlic-chili glaze. Spoon a small amount of the corn husk broth reduction around the chicken and corn.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Cherry Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh is placed slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes, thick wedges of caramelized red onion, and plump, dark Kalamata olives. Smashed roasted garlic cloves are nestled among the vegetables. Fresh green oregano and thyme sprigs are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color. The natural pan juices and olive oil sheen glisten on the ingredients. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing for negative space. A rustic wooden table surface serves as the background. Beside the plate, a neatly folded off-white cotton napkin and a simple fork and knife are placed. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread like ciabatta to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Accompany with a simple side salad of mixed greens with a lemon-oregano vinaigrette.
Enjoy with a glass of crisp white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large roasting pan, combine cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, smashed garlic cloves, pitted Kalamata olives, oregano, and thyme.
Drizzle vegetables and herbs with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Nestle chicken thighs among the vegetables in the roasting pan. Drizzle chicken with remaining 30ml olive oil.
Arrange lemon slices around the chicken.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and skin is golden and crispy.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the roasted chicken and vegetables before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through for food safety.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage Stuffed Conchiglie with Mornay Sauce and Citrus Cherry Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate on a simple wooden table. Three golden-brown, baked pasta shells are neatly arranged, showcasing their generous sausage and tomato filling. The shells are slightly bubbling with melted Gruyère cheese from the rich Mornay sauce that pools beneath and around them. The sausage filling is visible, a deep reddish-brown. Beside the pasta, a vibrant, fresh salad is mounded. It features ruby red cherry halves, glistening pink and yellow grapefruit segments, and translucent, thinly sliced cucumber rounds. A scattering of fresh green mint or basil leaves brightens the salad. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and colors. A simple fork and knife are placed to the right, and a folded white cotton napkin to the left, completing a casual bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook pasta shells according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper into the sausage. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine cooked sausage mixture, egg, Parmesan cheese, and breadcrumbs. Mix well.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the sausage mixture. Do not overfill. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer in a large baking dish.
Prepare Mornay sauce: Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute, forming a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. This takes 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded Gruyère cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour Mornay sauce evenly over the stuffed pasta shells in the baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until sauce is bubbly and shells are golden brown.
While shells bake, prepare the salad: In a medium bowl, combine halved cherries, grapefruit segments, and thinly sliced cucumber.
Whisk together olive oil, white wine vinegar, salt, and pepper for dressing. Pour over salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat. Stir in chopped mint or basil.
Remove baked shells from oven. Let rest for a few minutes.
Serve 2-3 stuffed shells per plate with a generous spoonful of Mornay sauce. Place a portion of the Citrus Cherry Salad alongside. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown seared pork chop rests prominently on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chop exhibits a beautifully caramelized crust, indicating a perfect sear, and appears juicy. A rich, velvety cream sauce, studded with tender, earthy brown mushroom slices and flecks of fresh parsley, is elegantly spooned over and around the pork. Beside the chop, a neat bundle of vibrant green, tender-crisp roasted asparagus spears adds a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro setting. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting presentation. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and professional single serving.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer chops to a plate. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add finely diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Return pork chops to skillet with sauce. Spoon sauce over chops. Cook 2-3 minutes or until heated through.
Meanwhile, toss asparagus with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a preheated 200°C oven for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Garnish sauce with fresh chopped parsley. Serve pork chops immediately with mushroom cream sauce and roasted asparagus.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Pilaf is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pilaf forms a natural mound in the center, allowing the individual grains of rice to be visible. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among the fluffy, yellow-tinted basmati rice. Visible specks of vibrant red diced bell pepper and green chopped parsley are interspersed throughout the rice. The chicken exhibits a slightly crisp exterior, contrasting with its tender interior. The rice is light and separate, with a soft texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley covers the top. One or two vibrant yellow lemon wedges are placed neatly beside the pilaf. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded, light-colored cotton napkin to the side. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background is slightly blurred, focusing attention on the dish while hinting at a casual restaurant environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain Greek yogurt.
Accompany with warm pita bread.
Serve with a simple cucumber and tomato salad.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Drain well.
Pat chicken chunks dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, diced red bell pepper, cumin, coriander, paprika, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the drained rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat rice with spices and oil.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly.
Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during simmering.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Stir in half of the fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Cheesy Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Cheesy Potato Gratin is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three thick, golden-brown pan-seared pork medallions, cooked to a tender finish, are neatly arranged on one side of the plate. A rich, creamy mushroom-Dijon cream sauce is generously drizzled over the pork, pooling slightly around its base. Adjacent to the pork, a substantial, rectangular portion of golden-crusted Cheesy Potato Gratin sits, its top a deep, inviting golden-brown from melted Gruyère, revealing layers of thinly sliced, tender potatoes beneath. Freshly chopped bright green chives are lightly sprinkled over the pork and sauce, adding a vibrant color contrast. The composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, textured wooden table, accompanied by polished silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, set in natural, even lighting to highlight the dish's appealing textures and colors, creating a refined bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty baguette slices on the side for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a gratin dish.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes (2-3 mm thick). Pat dry.
Arrange a layer of sliced potatoes in the gratin dish. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with grated Gruyère.
Repeat layering potatoes and cheese until all are used. Pour heavy cream evenly over potatoes.
Bake gratin for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbling. Let rest 10 minutes.
While gratin bakes, cut pork tenderloin into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season pork with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 63°C). Remove pork from pan. Keep warm.
Add butter to the same pan. Add chopped shallot and cook 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Bring to a simmer. Stir in Dijon mustard and remaining heavy cream. Cook 3-5 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Return pork medallions to the pan briefly to coat in sauce.
Serve pork medallions immediately alongside a generous portion of potato gratin. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.
notes: For the gratin, ensure potatoes are sliced uniformly thin for even cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing pork; cook in batches if necessary to ensure a good sear.
traditional_techniques: Gratin (baking in layers with cheese and cream)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken Breast and Creamy Potato Gratin is elegantly plated on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, seared to a golden-brown crust, is cut into thick, succulent pieces, arranged naturally beside a substantial, golden-brown square of potato gratin. The gratin displays visible layers of thinly sliced, roasted potatoes beneath a rich, bubbly, caramelized cheese crust. A glossy, amber-hued thyme pan sauce is spooned over the chicken and around the plate. Fresh thyme sprigs provide a vibrant green accent. The color palette features warm browns, creamy whites, and rich amber tones. Moderate negative space frames the professional yet approachable plating. The plate rests on a simple dark wooden table, with a white cotton napkin and classic flatware nearby, under natural, even lighting, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a crisp white wine like Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc.
Offer crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Rub a 20x20 cm baking dish with a cut garlic clove.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly, 2-3 mm thick. Use a mandoline if possible.
Combine cream, minced garlic, a few thyme sprigs, salt, and pepper in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Remove from heat.
Layer half the sliced potatoes in the prepared dish. Pour half the cream mixture over. Sprinkle with half the grated Parmesan.
Repeat with remaining potatoes, cream, and Parmesan.
Bake 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. Let gratin rest 10 minutes before serving.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken breasts. Sear 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crusty.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven (180°C) for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, return skillet to stovetop over medium heat.
Add minced shallot to skillet. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Deglaze skillet with chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified. Stir in a few fresh thyme leaves. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick pieces. Do not fan out slices.
Place a portion of potato gratin on each plate. Arrange chicken pieces beside the gratin.
Spoon thyme pan sauce over chicken and around the plate. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure potatoes are very thinly sliced for best gratin texture.
Do not overcrowd the skillet when searing chicken to ensure proper browning.
Resting the chicken is crucial for juiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Chicken and Tomato Pasta is presented on a modest, everyday ceramic plate. The dish features chunky, cooked chicken pieces, mixed with penne pasta coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. Vibrant green spinach leaves are visible throughout, along with earthy brown mushroom slices and tender diced onion. The ingredients are naturally mixed, forming a hearty, comforting mound in the center of the plate, with some sauce and pasta spilling gently to the edges. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, under warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware are casually placed nearby, suggesting a relaxed, family meal setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Set aside.
Cut chicken breasts into 2.5 cm cubes.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Slice mushrooms.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried basil, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in fresh spinach until wilted.
Add cooked pasta to the pot. Stir to combine all ingredients.
Transfer mixture to a 3-liter baking dish if not using an oven-safe pot.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until bubbling and heated through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Shakshuka
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Shakshuka served in a small, seasoned black cast-iron skillet. The base consists of a thick, chunky sauce made of deep-red tomatoes and softened diced red peppers. Four whole poached eggs are nestled into the sauce. The egg whites are solid and opaque white, while the yolks remain bright yellow and liquid. Small white crumbles of feta cheese and bright green chopped parsley are scattered across the surface. The skillet sits on a rustic dark wooden table. A side of warm, charred pita bread batons rests on a simple ceramic plate nearby. Lighting is warm and natural, evoking a cozy home kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or challah
Accompany with a side of labneh or hummus
Pair with a simple Israeli salad of cucumber and tomato
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chili flakes.
Cook spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Season sauce with salt and black pepper.
Use a spoon to create 4 small wells in the sauce.
Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the skillet with a tight-fitting lid.
Cook for 5 to 8 minutes until egg whites are set and yolks are runny.
Remove skillet from heat.
Garnish with crumbled feta and chopped parsley.
notes: Watch the eggs closely to ensure yolks do not overcook.
Add a splash of water to the sauce if it becomes too thick before adding eggs.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Stuffed Pork Loin with Dijon Glaze and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Herb-Stuffed Pork Loin with Dijon Glaze and Rosemary Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork loin, seared golden-brown and roasted tender, is cut into three substantial 2-3 cm thick chunks, revealing the creamy mushroom and herb cheese stuffing. Chunks are arranged centrally. Beside the pork, roasted Yukon Gold potato wedges, with crisp, golden-brown skins and fluffy interiors, are neatly piled. A glossy Dijon glaze is drizzled over the pork. The dish is garnished with vibrant, freshly chopped parsley. The presentation is clean, professional, and inviting. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with standard silver flatware and a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights food textures and colors. The background is minimal, creating a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed green beans or a light mixed green salad with vinaigrette for a balanced meal.
Offer crusty bread to sop up any remaining glaze.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).

Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges or cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, 1 sprig chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until golden and tender. Flip halfway.
While potatoes roast, butterfly the pork loin. Slice lengthwise almost through, then open flat. Cover with plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness.

Clean and thinly slice mushrooms. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms and minced garlic. Sauté until mushrooms are softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine sautéed mushrooms, herb cream cheese, and half of the chopped fresh parsley. Mix well.
Spread the mushroom-cheese mixture evenly over the pounded pork loin. Roll the pork tightly. Secure with kitchen twine at 3 cm intervals.
Season the outside of the rolled pork with salt and pepper.

Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add 15 ml olive oil. Sear the pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven with the potatoes.
Roast pork for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Use a meat thermometer.
Remove pork from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.

While pork rests, make the glaze. Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth to deglaze, scraping up browned bits. Stir in Dijon mustard. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove twine from pork. Cut pork into thick 2-3 cm chunks. Do not slice thinly or fan out.
Arrange pork chunks and roasted potatoes on plates. Drizzle with Dijon glaze. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure pork reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
Tying the pork loin helps it maintain its shape during cooking and keeps the stuffing secure.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Mushroom Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous scoop of the Homestyle Chicken and Mushroom Rice Bake rests on a simple, everyday ceramic plate. The dish presents as a hearty, comforting casserole, brimming with distinct textures and natural colors. Diced chicken chunks, sautéed sliced mushrooms, and bright green peas are visibly nestled within fluffy rice grains. The top boasts a bubbly, golden-orange layer of melted cheddar cheese, creating an inviting, slightly creamy texture. The plate is casually positioned on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a lived-in, family kitchen setting. A simple, slightly wrinkled cloth napkin and a standard fork are placed nearby. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the dish's comforting appeal. This is a modest, satisfying individual portion, perfectly embodying homely comfort food.
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Slice mushrooms. Finely chop onion. Mince garlic.
Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add chopped onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Return chicken to skillet with mushrooms. Stir in cooked rice, green peas, 150g shredded cheddar cheese, plain yogurt, chicken broth, salt, black pepper, and dried thyme. Mix well.
Transfer mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet. Top with remaining 50g shredded cheddar cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and dish is heated through.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Paprika Chicken Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty paprika chicken stew rests in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The stew is a rich reddish-brown, with tender chicken chunks, soft 2 cm potato cubes, and vibrant green beans nestled within the thick, savory sauce. The chicken pieces are substantial, natural cuts, not fanned. A few fresh basil leaves are torn casually over the top, adding a pop of green. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, emphasizing comfort and approachable home cooking.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Trim chicken thighs. Cut into 4 cm chunks.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Brown on all sides. This takes about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at end of cooking.
Stir in sweet paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add potato cubes. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Trim green beans. Add to the pot. Cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and green beans are cooked through.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: This dish can be made ahead and reheats well.
Adjust paprika amount for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken with Cherry Tomato Confit and Spaghetti
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Chicken with Cherry Tomato Confit and Spaghetti is presented on a round white porcelain plate on a rustic wooden table. Spaghetti is neatly coiled, forming a modest mound. Golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions, about 2 cm thick, are arranged atop the pasta, showcasing their seared crust. Vibrant, soft-burst cherry tomatoes from the confit are scattered around, some whole, some split. A light, glossy sauce coats the al dente spaghetti. Fresh green basil leaves and chopped flat-leaf parsley are sprinkled over, adding vibrant color. Fine lemon zest provides a bright finish. The presentation is clean, organized, and inviting. A silver fork and spoon rest on a white cotton napkin beside the plate. The background hints at a casual bistro with warm, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer a small bowl of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Confit: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a small baking dish, combine cherry tomatoes, 4 sliced garlic cloves, 80 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss gently. Roast for 30-40 minutes, or until tomatoes are soft and slightly burst.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 20 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions or chunks.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water before draining.

Build Sauce: While pasta cooks, return pan used for chicken to medium heat. Add remaining 2 sliced garlic cloves. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Deglaze with chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add roasted cherry tomatoes with their oil. Stir gently to combine.
Combine Dish: Add drained spaghetti to the pan with the sauce. Add lemon juice and most of the fresh basil leaves. Toss well. Add reserved pasta water as needed to create a light sauce.

Serve: Divide spaghetti among four plates. Arrange sliced chicken pieces on top of each pasta portion. Garnish with remaining fresh basil, chopped parsley, and lemon zest. Serve immediately, with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano on the side if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C internal temperature.
Do not overcook spaghetti; it should be al dente.
The tomato confit can be prepared in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Shrimp with Mozzarella Polenta and Glazed Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pan-Seared Shrimp with Mozzarella Polenta and Glazed Onions is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, fluid mound of creamy, golden-yellow mozzarella polenta forms the base. Four to five pan-seared shrimp, vibrant pink-orange with subtle browned edges, are arranged on top of the polenta, showcasing their plump, whole forms. A small, neat pile of deeply caramelized onion strands gleams with an inviting amber-brown hue. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with balanced colors and textures and moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting. A subtly blurred modern bistro background suggests a relaxed dining atmosphere.
instructions: Thinly slice onions. In a large pan, heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Bring broth to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until creamy and thick. Stir in shredded mozzarella until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat shrimp dry with paper towels. Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using).

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add shrimp in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
If desired, after searing shrimp, add white wine to the hot skillet. Scrape up any browned bits. Cook for 1 minute until reduced slightly.

Ladle creamy mozzarella polenta onto serving plates. Arrange seared shrimp over the polenta. Spoon caramelized onions next to or over the shrimp. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Tofu Bolognese with Gluten-Free Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty tofu bolognese is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Gluten-free pasta forms a loose base on the plate. A generous, rustic portion of rich red tofu ragu is spooned over the pasta, allowing some pasta to peek through. The ragu features finely diced onions, carrots, and celery, along with crumbled, lightly browned tofu pieces, all coated in a thick, vibrant tomato sauce. Specks of dried oregano and basil are visible throughout the sauce. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are casually placed on top as a garnish. The dish is arranged naturally, with components touching and overlapping. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork are casually placed beside the plate, creating a lived-in, homely atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a comforting, approachable meal.
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes to remove excess water. Crumble tofu into small pieces with your hands.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crumbled tofu to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, dried oregano, and dried basil.
Bring the ragu to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce will thicken.
Season the ragu with salt and black pepper to taste.
While the ragu simmers, cook gluten-free pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Drain the cooked pasta.
Serve the tofu ragu generously spooned over the gluten-free pasta. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Katsu Curry with Japanese Potato Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Japanese Pork Katsu Curry is presented on a clean, off-white ceramic dinner plate, reflecting a simple restaurant style. The main dish features a bed of fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice on one side, with a rich, dark golden-brown Japanese curry sauce generously ladled beside it, pooling slightly. Sliced, golden-crisp pork katsu, cut into thick chunks, is arranged neatly on top of the curry, showcasing its perfectly fried, craggy panko coating. The katsu is not fanned out. Visible within the curry sauce are tender, soft chunks of potato, carrot, and sliced mushrooms, adding color and texture. A small, neat scoop of Japanese potato salad, creamy white with visible flecks of orange carrot and tiny green onion slivers, rests on the plate next to the main components. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with the deep brown of the curry, the golden katsu, and the white rice. The table surface is a simple, natural wood, complemented by a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. The lighting is natural and even, creating soft shadows that highlight the textures. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a small ceramic rice bowl are subtly placed in the background, reinforcing the authentic Japanese dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fukujinzuke (pickled daikon and lotus root) or rakkyo (pickled scallions).
Offer a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven-spice blend) for those who prefer more heat.
Serve in traditional Japanese ceramic bowls for rice and curry, with a small side plate for the potato salad.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.quantity: 1 small (80g), finely diced or 1 tbsp tomato paste

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (300g), peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes (for salad)

instructions: Wash rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Combine rice and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 10 minutes.

Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté diced onion, carrot, and diced potato for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened. Add sliced mushrooms, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Cook for another 3 minutes. Add diced tomato (or tomato paste), cook for 2 minutes. Pour in water or dashi. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cook until vegetables are tender, about 15-20 minutes. Turn off heat. Break curry roux blocks into pieces and add to the pot, stirring until fully dissolved. Return to low heat, stir occasionally until sauce thickens. Stir in soy sauce and honey/sugar (if using). Keep warm.

Pat pork loin cutlets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Set up a breading station: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten egg, one plate with panko breadcrumbs. Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, ensuring full coverage. Finally, coat thoroughly with panko, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 170°C. Carefully lower one or two katsu cutlets into the hot oil. Fry for 4-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove and place on a wire rack to drain excess oil. Repeat with remaining katsu. Let rest briefly, then slice each katsu into 2 cm thick strips.

While katsu is cooking, boil diced potatoes and carrots in salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well. In a bowl, combine warm potatoes and carrots. Add mayonnaise, rice vinegar, salt, pepper, and thinly sliced onion (if using). Gently mash some of the potato cubes for a creamier texture while leaving some chunks. Stir in chopped hard-boiled egg (if using).

Serve a portion of steamed rice on one side of a plate. Ladle a generous amount of hot curry sauce next to the rice. Arrange the sliced pork katsu on top of the curry sauce or alongside it. Place a scoop of Japanese potato salad on the side.
notes: Japanese Kewpie mayonnaise is recommended for the potato salad for its distinct umami flavor.
Adjust the spiciness of the curry by choosing different curry roux brands or adding a pinch of cayenne pepper.
Ensure the oil temperature for frying katsu is maintained to achieve a crispy exterior and fully cooked interior.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo y Arroz con Pimientos y Queso
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo y Arroz con Pimientos y Queso is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice is centrally mounded, showcasing its golden-yellow hue from saffron and paprika. Interspersed throughout the rice are vibrant 2 cm squares of red and yellow bell pepper, adding bursts of color. Succulent, browned 3-4 cm chicken cubes are naturally nestled within the rice, prominent and uncut. A delicate melt of grated Manchego cheese lightly coats the top of the dish, adding a subtle creamy sheen. The textures are varied: tender, slightly al dente rice, tender-crisp bell peppers, and juicy chicken. A small sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley is placed on top for a vibrant green garnish. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded natural-colored cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a clean, professional, and inviting presentation with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices
Offer lemon wedges for a squeeze of fresh acidity
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion finely. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm squares. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or paella pan over medium-high heat.
Add chicken pieces. Sear until browned on all sides. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add bell pepper squares. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes (undrained). Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice with the sofrito. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads if using. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Distribute evenly in the rice. Do not stir extensively after this point.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pan tightly. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Manchego cheese until melted and incorporated. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Spicy Dijon Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of pan-seared pork medallions on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned on a simple wooden table surface. Two thick, golden-brown seared pork medallions, cooked to a tender finish, rest atop a creamy mound of smooth mashed potatoes. A glossy, rich Dijon-chili glaze is generously spooned over the pork, catching the natural light. Beside the pork, a thoughtful arrangement of deeply caramelized, golden-brown onion strands and earthy sautéed mushroom caps adds contrasting color and texture.
