Do not overcook the pasta; it should be al dente.
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts better and provides superior flavor compared to pre-grated.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Chicken Adobo with Garlic Rice
recipes.visual_description: Place two whole, bone-in chicken thighs and three golden potato cubes on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken and potatoes are coated in a dark, glossy mahogany glaze. Position a mound of white rice, flecked with crispy golden garlic bits, next to the meat. Top the rice with a single sunny-side up egg featuring a bright yellow runny yolk and lacy edges. Garnish with cracked black peppercorns. The arrangement is clean and organized on a dark wood bistro table. Natural light emphasizes the sauce's texture. Include a traditional stainless steel spoon and fork on a folded white napkin. The entire plate is visible against a soft-focus restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally eaten using a spoon and fork simultaneously
Serve with a side of pickled green papaya or Atchara
Provide extra adobo sauce in a small side dish
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice with 600ml water in a pot.
Boil then simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Marinate chicken in soy sauce, half the garlic, and black pepper for 20 minutes.
Heat 30ml oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until browned on both sides.
Remove chicken from pan.
Fry potato cubes in the remaining oil until edges are golden.
Return chicken to the pan.
Add marinade, paprika, and 200ml water.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Remove lid and increase heat to reduce liquid to a thick, glossy glaze.
Sauté remaining garlic in 15ml oil until golden brown.
Fold fried garlic and salt into the cooked rice.
Fry eggs sunny-side up in a separate non-stick pan.
Place chicken and potatoes over garlic rice and top with the egg.
notes: Ensure the sauce is reduced until it coats the back of a spoon
Use bone-in thighs to prevent the meat from drying out during braising
Monitor chicken internal temperature to hit exactly 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Potato Mayonnaise Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of Hearty Chicken and Potato Mayonnaise Bake rests on an off-white, slightly imperfect ceramic plate. The top crust is a rich golden-brown, with visible edges of tender, slightly charred tomato slices peeking through the creamy, baked mayonnaise. Beneath, layers of thinly sliced, soft yellow potato rounds are visible, interspersed with succulent, thick-cut chicken chunks and translucent, caramelized onion rings. The dish exudes warmth and comfort. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green dill adds a touch of color. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed casually to the side, beside a folded, natural linen napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers or sauerkraut.
Offer a simple fresh salad of tomatoes and cucumbers with a light dressing.
Accompany with slices of rye bread.

ingredients.name: fresh dill or parsley, for garnish (optional)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a 25x35 cm baking dish with olive oil.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick cubes. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and dried dill.
Slice peeled potatoes into 3 mm thin rounds. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice onions into thin rings.
Slice tomatoes into 5 mm thick rounds.
Arrange a single layer of half the potato slices in the prepared baking dish.
Spread all the seasoned chicken cubes evenly over the potatoes.
Scatter sliced onions and minced garlic over the chicken.
Layer the remaining potato slices over the chicken and onions.
Arrange tomato slices evenly over the top potato layer.
Spread mayonnaise evenly over the tomatoes, covering completely.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). The top should be golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh dill or parsley if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
The mayonnaise creates a flavorful, moist crust, preventing the dish from drying out.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Chicken and Bell Pepper Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente fettuccine, coated in a creamy, off-white sauce, forms the base. Succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks are arranged naturally on top and mixed throughout. Vibrant red and yellow bell pepper dice, bright yellow corn kernels, and tender orange squash cubes are interspersed, adding pops of color and textural contrast. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. On the side, a portion of vibrant green, tender-crisp steamed green beans is neatly placed, alongside a slice of golden-brown garlic bread. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, with standard flatware and a cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty garlic bread for dipping into the creamy sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes 4-5 minutes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Dice bell peppers into 2 cm pieces. Peel and dice butternut squash into 1.5 cm cubes. Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté diced onion 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced bell peppers and squash to the pan. Sauté 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp. Add frozen corn kernels. Cook 2 minutes. Remove vegetables from pan. Set aside.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Meanwhile, melt butter in the pan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in softened cream cheese, sugar, and soy sauce until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked chicken and sautéed vegetables to the sauce. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Steam or blanch green beans 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with salt.
Toast bread slices. Rub with a cut garlic clove, then spread with a thin layer of butter for garlic bread.
Toss cooked pasta with the creamy chicken and vegetable mixture. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with green beans and garlic bread.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency by adding more reserved pasta water if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thai Basil Chicken Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant individual portion of Spicy Thai Basil Chicken Fried Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The stir-fried jasmine rice, mixed with tender diced chicken, finely minced bird's eye chilies, diced onion, and glossy dark green Thai basil leaves, forms a natural mound in the center. The chicken pieces are golden-brown and visually distinct. A perfectly fried sunny-side-up egg with a crisp, lacy edge and a bright yellow, runny yolk rests gently atop the rice. The dish showcases a balance of earthy browns from the chicken, vivid greens from the basil, red flecks from the chili, and the clean white of the rice. Three thin, fresh cucumber slices are neatly fanned beside the rice, with a bright green lime wedge completing the garnish. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A set of elegant dark wood chopsticks lies to the right, and a small white ceramic sauce dish containing prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) is placed to the left. A folded white cotton napkin is beside the chopsticks. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors of the dish, creating a professional and inviting image.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies and lime juice) for an optional spicy and tangy condiment.
Traditionally eaten with a spoon and fork, or chopsticks.
Often accompanied by a small bowl of clear broth on the side.

ingredients.name: Chicken breast or thigh, diced into 2 cm pieces
Bird's eye chilies, minced (adjust to taste)

instructions: Prepare sauce: In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat. Add minced chilies, minced garlic, and diced onion. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add cooked day-old jasmine rice to the wok. Break up any clumps with a spatula. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, mixing well with chicken and aromatics.
Pour the prepared sauce over the rice and chicken. Continue to stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, ensuring all ingredients are evenly coated and heated through.
Add fresh Thai basil leaves. Stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds until basil wilts. Remove from heat.
In a separate small frying pan, heat remaining 30 ml vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Fry each egg individually, sunny-side up, until whites are set and edges are crispy, with yolk still runny.
Serve individual portions of fried rice on plates. Top each portion with a fried egg. Garnish with thin cucumber slices and a lime wedge.
notes: Using day-old cooked jasmine rice is crucial for optimal fried rice texture; fresh rice tends to clump and become mushy.
Adjust the amount of bird's eye chilies to suit your preferred spice level.
Ensure your wok or pan is very hot before adding ingredients to achieve a good 'wok hei' (breath of the wok) for authentic flavor.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: sweet, sour, salty, and spicy

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Herbs and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests on an everyday off-white ceramic dinner plate. Beside it, a generous, natural mound of roasted potato chunks, their skins lightly browned and interiors tender, intermingle with soft, caramelized onion wedges and roasted garlic cloves. A few roasted sprigs of thyme and rosemary are visible amongst the vegetables. The components are arranged casually, touching and slightly overlapping, reflecting a comforting, home-cooked meal. The overall palette is warm with golden browns, earthy potato tones, and subtle green from the herbs. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family dinner. A casually placed cloth napkin or paper towel might be nearby.

ingredients.name: Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks
Large yellow onion, peeled, cut into 8 thick wedges

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, onion wedges, smashed garlic, 15ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread the seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs among the vegetables.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Rub chicken with remaining 15ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 3g black pepper.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up on the baking tray with the vegetables. Ensure chicken skin is not touching.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden brown and crispy. Potatoes should be tender.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C (167°F). Continue roasting if needed.
Remove tray from oven. Let chicken rest on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.
If making a pan sauce: Carefully pour chicken broth into the hot baking tray. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the tray.
Serve one chicken thigh per plate, surrounded by roasted potatoes and onions. Spoon pan sauce over chicken and potatoes if made. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Polenta with Seared Sausage and Roasted Corn & Peppers
recipes.visual_description: Creamy, golden polenta forms the base, generously ladled onto an off-white ceramic plate. Piled centrally are irregularly shaped, seared chunks of sausage, interspersed with vibrant roasted corn kernels, diced red and yellow bell peppers, and softened onion pieces. The colors are rich: deep yellow polenta, browned sausage, bright corn, and colorful peppers, all accented by a sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley. Textures are a mix of smooth polenta, slightly crisp sausage, and tender vegetables. The plate rests on a well-worn, rustic wooden dining table. A simple, casually crumpled beige linen napkin and a fork are beside the plate. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a cozy, lived-in kitchen. This is a single, modest, home-style portion.
instructions: Bring chicken broth and milk to a boil in a large saucepan.

Gradually whisk in the polenta. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until polenta is creamy and thick. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Remove sausage from casings. Break into irregular small chunks.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Sear until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove sausage from skillet. Drain excess fat.

Add diced red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, diced onion, and corn kernels to the same skillet. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften and lightly char. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Return cooked sausage chunks to the skillet with the vegetables. Stir to combine all ingredients.
Ladle creamy polenta onto individual serving plates. Spoon the sausage and roasted vegetable mixture generously over the polenta. Garnish each serving with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust polenta consistency by adding more broth or milk if it becomes too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Macaroni Bake
recipes.special_requests: Not spicy, only baked or stewed
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Macaroni Bake is presented in a pristine white porcelain oval gratin dish. The dish showcases a perfectly golden-brown, crispy breadcrumb and cheese crust across its surface. Below the crust, a rich, creamy, pale yellow sauce is visible, with tender, irregularly shaped chunks of seared chicken, soft diced potatoes (1.5-2 cm cubes), and al dente elbow macaroni peeking through. The textures are varied: crunchy topping, smooth sauce, and tender ingredients. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top as a final garnish. The gratin dish is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A polished silver fork and knife rest beside the dish on a crisp white cotton napkin. The setting evokes a clean, modern bistro, with soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's comforting appeal. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance, keeping the focus entirely on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.
Dice potatoes into 1.5-2 cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Melt butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Add finely diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk and chicken broth. Cook, stirring, until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in 150 g of the mixed cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Add cooked potatoes and macaroni. Stir gently to combine.
Transfer mixture to individual oven-safe gratin dishes or a single large baking dish. Ensure chicken is fully submerged in the sauce.
In a small bowl, whisk the egg. Combine breadcrumbs with the remaining 50 g mixed cheese. Stir in the whisked egg to form a coarse topping.
Sprinkle the breadcrumb mixture evenly over the top of the bake.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the sauce is bubbling. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For a richer flavor, use heavy cream instead of whole milk.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Hearty Beef and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew features tender, irregular chunks of browned beef, approximately 3-4 cm, nestled amongst soft, diced carrots (1.5 cm cubes) and creamy, diced potatoes (2 cm cubes). The rich, dark brown gravy, thickened slightly, coats all ingredients, with a gentle sheen from slow cooking. A few vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley leaves are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. The overall presentation is homely, comforting, and unpretentious, reflecting a satisfying family meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 150g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in beef broth, stirring to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5 hours, or until beef is tender.
Add diced potatoes and carrots to the pot. Stir well.
Cover and continue to cook for 30-40 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. The stew should be thick.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Sourdough Tagliatelle with Chicken Ragu and Fresh Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in a warm off-white tone, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A single individual portion of al dente sourdough tagliatelle, with its subtle golden hue and irregular, rustic texture, forms the base. It is generously coated in a rich, deeply savory chicken ragu, showcasing tender, irregular chunks of chicken and vibrant, crushed red tomatoes. The sauce glistens with olive oil, highlighting the natural imperfections of the hand-cut pasta. Fresh mozzarella pieces, some halved, some quartered, are thoughtfully placed on top, their pristine white contrasting with the ragu's depth. A scattering of verdant, torn basil leaves adds a pop of natural green, providing a fresh aroma and visual lift. The composition is clean, with ample negative space on the plate, emphasizing the pure beauty of each ingredient. A simple, undyed linen napkin in beige rests beside the plate, and soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the food's natural colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the ragu.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine.
instructions: Prepare Sourdough Tagliatelle:
Combine flour, sourdough starter, egg, and salt in a bowl.
Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Turn onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Wrap in cling film or a damp cloth. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes, or refrigerate for 1-2 hours.
Divide dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion very thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin.
Cut into tagliatelle strips (approx. 6-7mm wide). Dust with semolina to prevent sticking.
Prepare Chicken Ragu:
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Brown chicken in batches until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return browned chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and sauce has thickened. Stir occasionally. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook Pasta:
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add sourdough tagliatelle. Cook for 2-4 minutes until al dente. Fresh pasta cooks quickly.
Drain pasta, reserving 100ml of pasta water.
Combine and Serve:
Add drained pasta to the chicken ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing pasta to absorb flavors.
Portion pasta and ragu onto individual plates.
Arrange fresh mozzarella halves/quarters artfully on top of the pasta.
Garnish generously with torn fresh basil leaves. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil. Serve immediately.
notes: For zero-waste, save chicken trimmings (bones, skin, small bits) to make homemade chicken stock for the ragu or for future use.
Tomato ends and cores can be used to infuse olive oil or added to a vegetable stock.
Sourdough discard can be used to make the pasta, reducing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Chopped Cucumber and Chicken Garden Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of a vibrant, fresh garden salad is presented on a simple, everyday ceramic plate, possibly with a subtle floral pattern or a solid, earthy tone. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures. The salad features a base of roughly chopped romaine lettuce, creating a bed of deep green. Scattered throughout are bright red halved cherry tomatoes, crisp diced green bell pepper, refreshing diced cucumber, and finely diced red onion, adding pops of purple. Small, irregular chunks of pan-fried chicken are nestled among the vegetables, showing a lightly browned, savory exterior. A simple, golden lemon-herb vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients, creating a moist, appetizing sheen. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a homely, unpretentious feel. A standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. A crumpled paper napkin might be nearby. The background is a relaxed family dining area, possibly with a hint of natural clutter like a salt shaker or a water glass.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Wash and chop romaine lettuce into 2 cm pieces.
Dice cucumber into 1.5 cm cubes.
Halve cherry tomatoes.
Dice bell pepper into 1.5 cm cubes.
Finely dice red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, oregano, salt, and pepper for the dressing.
In a large serving bowl, combine chopped lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, bell pepper, and red onion.
Add diced chicken to the vegetables.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Chicken and Shrimp Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cajun Chicken and Shrimp Jambalaya fills a deep, matte white ceramic bowl. The dish presents a rich, cohesive blend of textures and colors. Fluffy, reddish-orange long-grain rice forms the base, speckled with vibrant green diced bell pepper, translucent onion, and bright red tomato pieces. Prominently placed are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks and plump, pink-orange cooked shrimp. Slices of dark, caramelized Andouille sausage are interspersed throughout. The surface is lightly garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and a sturdy, traditional metal spoon, with soft, natural lighting highlighting the dish's warmth and depth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional hot sauce on the side for those who prefer more heat.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add sausage slices. Cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove sausage and set aside.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear until golden brown on all sides, about 6-8 minutes. Chicken should reach 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cayenne pepper, dried sage, and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice, rice, chicken stock, and hot sauce. Bring to a boil. Scrape bottom of pot to release any browned bits.
Return cooked sausage and chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is nearly tender.
Stir in shrimp. Re-cover and cook for another 5-7 minutes, or until shrimp are pink and cooked through.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
traditional_techniques: Holy Trinity (sautéing onion, celery, bell pepper)

recipes.recipe_name: Potato, Tomato, and Basil Salad
recipes.visual_description: A homely, comforting salad presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden dining table. The base consists of irregularly diced, roasted potato pieces, their skins slightly crisped and interiors tender, showing a light golden hue. Interspersed among the potatoes are vibrant red cherry tomatoes, halved to reveal their juicy interiors. Fresh, whole green basil leaves are generously scattered throughout, adding bright pops of color and aromatic contrast. A small amount of finely shredded, pale chicken breast is lightly distributed, blending subtly with the vegetables. The salad is lightly coated in a glistening, simple vinaigrette, which clings to the ingredients. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a casually folded cloth napkin. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen setting.
instructions: Wash and dice potatoes into irregular pieces. Boil or roast potatoes until tender. Ensure internal temperature of any chicken used reaches 75°C (167°F) if cooking from raw.
Shred or finely dice cooked chicken breast.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Pick fresh basil leaves.
For the dressing, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, gently combine the warm potatoes, halved cherry tomatoes, basil leaves, and shredded chicken.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Gently toss to coat all ingredients.
Serve immediately or at room temperature. This recipe serves 4 people.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on an off-white ceramic plate with a rustic, uneven rim. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken pieces (thigh and drumstick), skin crisp from roasting, are centered. Substantial potato wedges, deeply caramelized and tender, are scattered around the chicken, some overlapping. Thick wedges of roasted onion, softened and sweet, are interspersed. Bright yellow lemon slices, slightly charred, peek out. The dish is garnished with fresh chopped parsley and small rosemary sprigs. The arrangement is casual, asymmetrical, filling the plate adequately. The scene is on a well-used wooden dining table, lit by warm kitchen light. A folded linen napkin and basic silver flatware rest beside the plate. A small, rustic bowl of olive oil and crusty bread sit nearby, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up the pan juices.
Enjoy family-style, with dishes passed around the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potato wedges, and onion wedges.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme leaves, salt, and pepper.
Squeeze juice from one lemon over the ingredients. Toss well to coat everything evenly.
Arrange chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place lemon slices among the chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 45-55 minutes.
Turn chicken and vegetables halfway through cooking.
Chicken is cooked when internal temperature reaches 75°C and juices run clear. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For extra crispiness, broil for the last 5 minutes.
Adjust herbs based on preference; oregano also works well.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Roasted Carrots, Onions, and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, whole roasted chicken breast rests as the focal point. Adjacent to the chicken is a neat, fluffy mound of earthy brown rice. Around the chicken and rice, a vibrant array of roasted vegetables is thoughtfully arranged: thick, tender carrot batons with slightly caramelized edges and tender red onion wedges, displaying their beautiful roasted color. Bright green, crisp-tender steamed broccoli florets add a pop of contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished simply with a fresh sprig of rosemary and a bright yellow lemon wedge, adding a touch of freshness. The overall presentation is balanced and organized, showcasing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A folded white cotton napkin and classic flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred restaurant background suggesting a casual yet refined atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with half of the chopped rosemary, thyme, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil.
Peel carrots. Cut into thick batons (approx. 5cm long, 1.5cm thick).
Peel red onion. Cut into 8 thick wedges.
In a large bowl, toss carrot batons and onion wedges with remaining rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt, pepper, and 30ml olive oil.
Arrange seasoned chicken, carrots, and onions in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 25-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized.
While chicken roasts, combine brown rice, chicken broth or water, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Cut broccoli into large florets. Steam broccoli for 5-7 minutes, until crisp-tender and vibrant green.
Slice lemon into wedges for garnish.

To serve, place a portion of brown rice on each plate. Arrange one roasted chicken breast beside the rice. Artfully arrange roasted carrot batons and onion wedges around the chicken. Add steamed broccoli florets to the plate. Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting portion of Homestyle Chicken and Rice Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a rustic edge. A generous mound of moist white rice, studded with tender, diced red bell pepper and bright red diced tomatoes, forms the base. Resting atop the rice is a single, perfectly cooked, golden-brown chicken thigh. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds color. The plating is natural and unforced, as if served directly from a family meal. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and spoon are casually placed beside it, alongside a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a comfortable kitchen environment with a softly blurred background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into 1cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in rice, oregano, and basil. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes with their juice and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Nestle seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Marsala with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: The Pan-Seared Chicken Marsala is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of golden, creamy polenta forms a smooth, fluid base on one side of the plate. Resting elegantly atop the polenta, or nestled beside it, is a whole, pan-seared chicken breast, its surface a rich, golden-brown with visible sear marks. The chicken is not sliced. Cascading over the chicken and pooling around the polenta is a glossy, deep amber Marsala sauce, studded with tender, earthy brown cremini mushroom slices and flecks of bright green chopped Italian parsley. The colors are warm and inviting: golden chicken, creamy yellow polenta, rich brown sauce, and vibrant green herbs. The textures are varied, from the smooth polenta and tender chicken to the soft mushrooms. A simple white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate on a light wooden table surface, under natural, even lighting, completing a refined casual dining presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette can accompany the dish.

ingredients.name: Water or chicken broth for polenta

instructions: Pound chicken breasts to even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken to a plate. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned.
Add minced shallots and garlic to skillet. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 2 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 1 minute to heat through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
For polenta: Bring water/broth and milk to a boil in a medium saucepan. Season with salt.
Slowly whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until polenta thickens and is creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken and Potato Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of the Savory Chicken and Potato Cake is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The slice reveals distinct, well-defined layers: golden-brown roasted potato slices forming the top and bottom, encasing creamy shredded chicken mixed with caramelized onions and vibrant red tomato slices. The chicken layer shows subtle hints of green from fresh herbs. The textures are varied: tender potatoes, succulent chicken, and soft tomatoes, all bound by a rich, savory mayonnaise-based sauce that subtly oozes from the layers. The top potato layer is lightly browned and crisp at the edges. A delicate sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives garnishes the top of the slice. The plate features moderate negative space, highlighting the layered structure. In the background, the remaining whole cake, still in its mold or on a simple wooden cutting board, suggests its full form. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table and natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and line a 20x10 cm loaf pan with baking paper, leaving overhang.
Poach chicken breasts. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred chicken finely.
Thinly slice potatoes, 2-3 mm thick. Do not peel. Boil potato slices in salted water for 5 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain well.
Thinly slice tomatoes, 2-3 mm thick.
Finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan. Add diced onion. Cook on medium-low heat until deeply caramelized, about 20-25 minutes. Add minced garlic in the last 5 minutes. Set aside.
In a bowl, combine mayonnaise, chicken broth, shredded chicken, caramelized onion, minced garlic, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Arrange a single layer of potato slices on the bottom of the prepared loaf pan. Overlap slightly.
Spread one-third of the chicken mixture evenly over the potatoes.
Arrange a layer of tomato slices over the chicken mixture.
Repeat layers: potato, chicken mixture, tomato. Finish with a final layer of potato slices on top.
Cover the loaf pan with foil. Bake for 40 minutes.
Remove foil. Bake for another 20-25 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and potatoes are very tender.
Let the cake cool in the pan for at least 30 minutes. Then refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, to firm up.
To serve, carefully invert the cake onto a cutting board. Slice into thick pieces. Garnish with fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Root Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: European cuisine, non-alcohol, have a chicken fillet, don't have cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single braised chicken fillet is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Rustic large chunks of fork-tender potatoes and thick slices of vibrant orange carrots are artfully arranged around the chicken. The chicken and vegetables are generously coated in a rich, rustic red tomato and oregano sauce, with visible pieces of caramelized onion and minced garlic. The chicken boasts a golden-brown exterior from initial searing, contrasting with its tender interior. Vegetables retain their shape and bright color. A fresh sprig of oregano rests atop the chicken, with a slight drizzle of golden olive oil enhancing the sheen. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and natural, even lighting from the side, creating a warm bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread to soak up the rich sauce.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken fillets with salt and pepper. Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken fillets to the pot. Add potato chunks and carrot slices around the chicken.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with a fresh oregano sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Braised Greens and Preserved Lemon
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown seared chicken thigh, presented whole, rests slightly off-center on a handcrafted, natural beige ceramic plate. Beside it, a vibrant mound of braised green vegetables, showcasing their tender texture and natural color, is artfully arranged. Finely diced preserved lemon pieces are scattered over the greens and chicken, adding bright yellow accents. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface. An undyed natural linen napkin is casually draped beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. A subtle green plant in a simple terracotta pot provides a hint of natural background, emphasizing the eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: seasonal greens (e.g., kale, chard), tough stems removed, roughly chopped
fresh parsley or chives, roughly chopped

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot pan. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board.
Add sliced garlic and onion to the same pan. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add chopped greens to the pan. Cook, stirring, until wilted.
Pour in chicken stock. Stir in diced preserved lemon. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise greens for 5-7 minutes, or until tender. Season with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve each chicken thigh alongside a generous portion of braised greens. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.
notes: Use chicken bones and vegetable scraps to make homemade stock, reducing food waste.
Embrace seasonal variations for greens based on local availability.
Preserved lemon utilizes a traditional preservation technique, extending shelf life and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Burst Cherry Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, cut into two thick medallions, rests slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken boasts a golden-brown, crisp exterior and a tender, juicy interior. It is generously spooned with a vibrant sauce made from burst red and orange cherry tomatoes, which create a rustic yet elegant pool around the chicken. Thinly sliced garlic and delicate basil leaves are visible within the sauce, adding specks of green and white. A sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped basil leaves garnishes the dish, providing a pop of fresh green color and aromatic appeal. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside it, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are arranged. The background features a softly blurred, modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining atmosphere. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a simple side of pasta or roasted potatoes
Accompany with a light green salad
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallots to the skillet. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened. Add sliced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon. Let wine reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Add cherry tomatoes and chicken stock to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, gently pressing on tomatoes with the back of a spoon to help them burst, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to warm through.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in butter and half of the fresh basil until butter is melted and sauce is glossy. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chicken immediately, spooning generous amounts of the burst tomato sauce over each piece. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken with lemon-garlic pasta on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown seared chicken breast, or two thick diagonal pieces, rests beside a mound of loosely twirled, glistening lemon-garlic pasta. The pasta shows visible flecks of minced garlic, bright yellow lemon zest, and chopped green parsley. A light dusting of grated Parmesan covers the dish. The presentation is organized yet natural. Garnish with fresh parsley sprigs and thin lemon slices. The setting is a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Sauté minced garlic 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth, lemon juice, and lemon zest. Bring to a simmer.
Add cooked pasta to skillet. Toss to coat.
Stir in grated Parmesan and chopped parsley. Add reserved pasta water gradually until sauce reaches desired consistency.
Slice chicken breasts diagonally into two thick pieces or serve whole.
Plate pasta. Top with chicken. Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon slices.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Turkey Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single whole, deeply browned braised turkey thigh rests on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The turkey is generously coated and surrounded by a rich, rustic tomato and onion sauce. The sauce, a deep reddish-orange, is thick and glossy, with visible soft, diced onion pieces. A vibrant scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves provides a fresh contrast on top of the turkey and sauce. The turkey itself appears incredibly tender, hinting at its long braise. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's comforting textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, evoking a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (e.g., Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat turkey thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear turkey thighs until deep golden brown on all sides. Remove turkey from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pot. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to release any browned bits. Cook 2 minutes until reduced slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, and chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return seared turkey thighs to the pot. Ensure turkey is mostly submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Braise for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until turkey is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove turkey from pot. Tent with foil. Let rest 5 minutes.
If sauce is too thin, simmer on stovetop over medium-high heat until desired consistency is reached.
Serve turkey with the rich tomato sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil.
notes: Ensure turkey reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust braising time based on the thickness of the turkey thighs.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a deep, white ceramic bowl, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features golden-brown chicken chunks, roasted to perfection, nestled among tender, rustic potato cubes. Bright orange carrot rounds and softened onion pieces are visible throughout. A rich, savory broth coats all components, reflecting the warm kitchen light. The chicken is cooked until juicy, with slightly browned edges, while the potato cubes hold their shape, offering a soft texture. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley scattered over the top. The background includes a casual cloth napkin and a metal fork, emphasizing a cozy, home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
Ideal for a family dinner.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt, pepper, and half the thyme.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and chop onion into 1 cm pieces.
Peel and slice carrots into 0.5 cm thick rounds.
Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 3-4 minutes until lightly golden. Remove chicken.
Add onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and remaining thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add diced potatoes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover the pot. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Check seasoning. Adjust as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: This dish is excellent for meal prepping.
Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, golden-brown Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a well-loved, rustic ceramic baking dish, slightly off-center on a warm, worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features tender, cubed chicken breast chunks and soft potato cubes, generously coated in a creamy, savory sauce, with vibrant green peas interspersed throughout. A thick, bubbly layer of golden-brown melted cheddar cheese forms a crisp crust over the top. The sauce peeks through in places, showing its rich, creamy texture. The overall appearance is hearty and inviting, with natural, modest portions. The setting is a homely family kitchen, bathed in warm, soft light from an overhead fixture. A simple, everyday ceramic plate with minor imperfections is placed nearby, ready for serving. A casually folded cloth napkin and basic flatware rest beside the dish. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere with a natural, unpretentious feel, emphasizing the dish as the centerpiece of a satisfying home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot of salted cold water. Bring to a boil. Cook 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain thoroughly.
Dice chicken breasts into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat an oven-safe baking dish or large skillet over medium heat. Melt butter. Add diced chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from dish.
Add chopped onion to the same dish. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Remove dish from heat.
Stir mayonnaise into the sauce until well combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add seared chicken, drained potatoes, and frozen peas to the dish. Pour the creamy sauce over. Stir gently to coat all ingredients.
Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage & Pickled Root Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a round, matte cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate, centered with a natural mound of vibrant vegetables. Thinly shredded green cabbage forms the base, interspersed with bright orange julienned carrots and translucent crimson slices of quick-pickled radishes. Freshly chopped dill and parsley are generously mixed in, providing pops of verdant green and aromatic texture. A light, emulsified vinaigrette coats each component, creating a subtle sheen. The salad is topped with a scattering of golden-brown toasted pumpkin seeds, adding a textural contrast. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed, natural linen napkin is loosely draped beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh, crisp textures. The background is clean and simple, featuring a hint of blurred green foliage, underscoring the dish's natural and sustainable essence.
instructions: Shred 500 grams of green cabbage very thinly. Place in a large mixing bowl.
Julienne 2 medium carrots. Thinly slice 6-8 small radishes.
Prepare quick pickle brine: Combine 120 ml apple cider vinegar, 120 ml water, 5 grams sugar, and 5 grams salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Cool slightly.
Add julienned carrots and sliced radishes to the cooled brine. Let sit for at least 30 minutes to quick pickle.
Finely chop 15 grams fresh dill and 15 grams fresh parsley.
For the dressing: Whisk 60 ml olive oil, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 5 grams Dijon mustard, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper in a small bowl until emulsified.
Drain the quick-pickled carrots and radishes, reserving the brine if desired for other uses.
Add drained pickled carrots and radishes, along with chopped dill and parsley, to the shredded cabbage in the large mixing bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all components evenly.
Plate the salad immediately. Garnish each serving with a scattering of toasted pumpkin seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Potato Smash and Pickled Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single portion presented on a light, natural-textured ceramic plate in an earthy tone. An irregularly shaped, rustic mound of 'Fermented Potato Smash' occupies one side, showcasing visible potato chunks and flecks of fermented vegetables. Adjacent, a whole, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh rests, its surface crisp and inviting, unsliced. Vibrant green clusters of 'Quick-Pickled Greens,' with their slightly blanched texture, are neatly arranged, providing a fresh contrast around the main components. A subtle drizzle of clear olive oil glistens over the dish. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and textures with ample white space, creating a clean, uncluttered visual. The setup features a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. A minimalist background includes subtle green plant elements, reinforcing the sustainable theme.

ingredients.name: Mixed greens (e.g., radish greens, carrot tops, kale leaves)
Finely chopped fermented vegetables (e.g., sauerkraut, kimchi)

instructions: Wash mixed greens thoroughly. Blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds. Drain immediately and shock in ice water. Drain again; squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop.
In a small pot, combine 100ml water, 50ml apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of sugar. Bring to a simmer. Pour hot liquid over greens. Let cool and marinate.
Wash potatoes. Boil whole in salted water until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain. Let cool slightly.

Roughly smash potatoes in a bowl; do not mash smooth. Add 50ml fermented vegetable brine and 30g finely chopped fermented vegetables. Season with salt and pepper. Adjust brine/vegetable quantity to taste.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken presentation-side down.
Sear chicken for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Flip. Cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest 5 minutes.

Spoon a generous portion of Fermented Potato Smash onto each plate. Place a seared chicken thigh next to it. Drain Quick-Pickled Greens and arrange them around the chicken and potatoes. Drizzle with remaining 15ml olive oil. Garnish with fresh herbs.
notes: This recipe emphasizes using vegetable parts often discarded for pickling, contributing to zero-waste cooking.
The fermented brine and vegetables add a complex depth of flavor and beneficial probiotics to the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sirloin with Rosemary Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A robust pan-seared sirloin steak, presented as a thick, whole piece, commands the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The steak features a deep, caramelized crust on its exterior, contrasting with its juicy, medium-rare interior. Beside the steak, a generous portion of roasted Yukon Gold potato cubes, golden-brown and slightly crisp on the edges, are artfully arranged. Their irregular, rustic shapes provide texture. Vibrant green beans, blanched to tender-crisp perfection, add a pop of color and freshness. A rich, glossy pan sauce, subtly spooned over a portion of the steak, catches the light. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware accompany the dish. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, emphasizing its inviting textures and rich colors, creating a professional yet approachable presentation typical of a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, 1 sprig chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 30-35 minutes. Turn halfway. Roast until golden and tender.
Pat sirloin steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Add 30ml olive oil. Heat until shimmering.
Carefully place steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter, 2 sprigs rosemary, and crushed garlic cloves to the pan. Tilt pan. Baste steaks with melted butter and aromatics for 1-2 minutes.
Remove steaks from pan. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.
While steaks rest, trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain. Alternatively, sauté in a separate pan with a knob of butter until tender-crisp.
For the pan sauce: Pour off excess fat from the skillet, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Return pan to medium heat. Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add beef stock to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Strain sauce if desired for a smoother consistency.
Slice rested steaks against the grain into thick pieces or serve whole. Plate with roasted potatoes and green beans. Spoon pan sauce over the steak.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Chicken and Potato Bake sits on a matte cream ceramic plate. The dish consists of oven-roasted, golden-brown potato cubes and seared chicken chunks arranged in a natural, overlapping heap. Melted sharp cheddar cheese drapes over the components, showing bubbly textures and toasted edges. Vibrant green chopped chives are sprinkled evenly over the cheese. The arrangement is asymmetrical and casual, filling the center of the plate while leaving clean margins. The plate rests on a dark, textured wooden table next to a stainless steel fork and a neutral linen napkin. Warm, directional kitchen lighting enhances the crispy potato skins and the glossy, melted cheese. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of sour cream
Pair with a fresh green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Toss potatoes with 15ml oil, half the salt, and half the paprika.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Season chicken with remaining oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper.
Add chicken to the baking sheet with potatoes.
Roast for 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar over the chicken and potatoes.
Bake 3 minutes until cheese melts and bubbles.
Garnish with finely chopped chives.
notes: Cut potatoes into uniform cubes to ensure even roasting
Use sharp cheddar for the best flavor profile
Ensure chicken chunks are not touching to allow browning

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: Tagliatelle is coiled neatly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta is evenly coated in a creamy, rich sauce. Seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled among the pasta. Sliced cremini mushrooms are integrated throughout the dish. Fresh chopped parsley and a light grating of Parmesan cheese provide vibrant green and pale yellow accents. The dish displays warm golden, earthy brown, and creamy white tones. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A single refined restaurant portion is presented.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Slice 300g cremini mushrooms. Mince 3 garlic cloves. Dice 1 medium onion. Cut 500g chicken breast into 3cm thick chunks.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the pan. Sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Pour in 250ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in 200ml heavy cream. Simmer gently for 2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook 400g tagliatelle in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.

Return cooked chicken to the pan with the sauce. Add drained tagliatelle. Add 50g grated Parmesan cheese and 15g chopped fresh parsley. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Mushroom with Creamy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Savory Beef and Mushroom with Creamy Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, off-white Arborio rice forms a soft, free-flowing bed in the center of the plate, its smooth texture visible. Piled generously atop the rice are thick, roasted beef chunks, their surfaces seared to a rich dark brown, contrasting with the tender, juicy interior. Interspersed among the beef are earthy brown, sautéed cremini mushroom slices and translucent, caramelized onion pieces, all coated in a glossy, deep brown, savory sauce. The dish is vibrant with warm tones of brown and cream, accented by the bright green of fresh chopped parsley sprinkled over the top. The beef pieces are presented as substantial, irregular chunks, not sliced. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional but approachable presentation.

ingredients.name: Beef (e.g., sirloin or tenderloin, cut into 2.5 cm chunks)

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat half of olive oil in a large pan over high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining olive oil and butter to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce. Pour in 750 ml beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Return seared beef to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until beef is tender.
While ragout simmers, prepare rice. In a separate saucepan, melt 15g butter over medium heat. Add Arborio rice. Stir for 1 minute until translucent.

Add 250 ml beef broth to rice. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding remaining 500 ml beef broth, 125 ml at a time, stirring constantly until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Cook until rice is creamy and al dente, about 18-20 minutes.
Stir heavy cream into the beef and mushroom ragout. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle creamy rice onto plates. Top with generous portions of beef and mushroom ragout. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust beef cooking time based on cut and desired tenderness.
Ensure rice is stirred constantly for optimal creaminess.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Two thick, pan-seared beef medallions, exhibiting a rich, caramelized crust, are presented on a clean white porcelain plate. A generous quantity of creamy, light brown mushroom sauce, featuring tender, browned mushroom slices and finely diced shallots, is spooned over the beef and cascades around its base. A vibrant scattering of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a verdant contrast. The plate is arranged on a simple wooden table, flanked by a neatly folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its appealing textures and colors against a subtle, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside roasted potatoes, mashed potatoes, or crusty bread.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil.
Add butter to the same pan. Add finely diced shallot. Sauté until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and fresh thyme leaves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with brandy or white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce liquid by half.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Plate beef medallions. Spoon creamy mushroom sauce generously over beef.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, allow beef to rest for 5 minutes after searing.
Adjust cooking time for beef to achieve desired doneness.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken is presented in a shallow, rustic terracotta-style bowl on a light wooden table.
