Two golden-brown chicken thighs, seared to a crisp exterior, are nestled within a vibrant, rich tomato and bell pepper sauce. The bell peppers are cut into thick, rustic chunks, showcasing shades of red and yellow, contrasting with the deep red of the tomato sauce. Diced onions and garlic are visible within the sauce, contributing to its texture. Freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley is generously sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of green. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, a crisp, white linen napkin and a slice of crusty artisan bread complete the authentic casual dining setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread to dip into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper chunks. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in smoked paprika and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Remove from oven. Discard bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best flavor, use high-quality smoked paprika.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Beef with Tomato & Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Beer-Braised Beef with Tomato & Onion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. The rich, dark reddish-brown beef stew, featuring tender 4cm beef cubes and softened diced onions and tomatoes in a thick, glossy sauce, is ladled on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the stew, a neat mound of fluffy white basmati rice sits, its individual grains distinct. The stew exhibits visual depth with hints of dark beer and caramelized vegetables. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top of the stew, providing a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is professional yet inviting, with moderate negative space around the elements. A simple, folded white cotton napkin and a polished fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4cm cubes. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and black pepper. Dredge beef lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Sauté onions for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and sugar. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in dark beer. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, beef stock, dried thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring the stew to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
While stew simmers, prepare rice. Rinse basmati rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rinsed rice with 600 ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Remove bay leaves from the stew. Stir in red wine vinegar. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle beef stew onto plates. Serve alongside or over fluffed basmati rice. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: Tagliatelle is coiled neatly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta is evenly coated in a creamy, rich sauce. Seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled among the pasta. Sliced cremini mushrooms are integrated throughout the dish. Fresh chopped parsley and a light grating of Parmesan cheese provide vibrant green and pale yellow accents. The dish displays warm golden, earthy brown, and creamy white tones. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. A single refined restaurant portion is presented.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Slice 300g cremini mushrooms. Mince 3 garlic cloves. Dice 1 medium onion. Cut 500g chicken breast into 3cm thick chunks.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the pan. Sauté diced onion for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Pour in 250ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in 200ml heavy cream. Simmer gently for 2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook 400g tagliatelle in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120ml pasta water.

Return cooked chicken to the pan with the sauce. Add drained tagliatelle. Add 50g grated Parmesan cheese and 15g chopped fresh parsley. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Medley with Cheesy Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. A portion of fluffy brown rice, generously mixed with melted golden cheddar cheese, forms the base on one side of the plate. Beside the rice, a whole roasted chicken thigh, with a crisp, golden-brown skin, is prominently placed. Around the chicken and rice, an artful medley of roasted vegetables is arranged. This includes tender-crisp broccoli florets, some with slightly charred edges, alongside creamy 2cm potato cubes with a hint of golden-brown crispness. Vibrant red onion wedges, softened and slightly caramelized, add depth of color. Bursting, sweet cherry tomato halves and bright yellow corn kernels complete the colorful arrangement. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate, emphasizing a casual yet refined dining experience.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, cubed potatoes, broccoli florets, onion wedges, and halved cherry tomatoes.
Drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with smoked paprika, garlic powder, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread seasoned chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Add corn kernels to the baking tray. Toss gently with other vegetables.
Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
While chicken and vegetables roast, stir shredded cheddar cheese into the hot cooked brown rice until melted and well combined.
To serve, spoon a portion of cheesy brown rice onto each plate.
Arrange roasted chicken and vegetable medley beside the rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Braised Chicken with Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Braised Chicken is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. One tender, bone-in chicken thigh, its skin a rich golden-brown, rests partially submerged in a vibrant, rustic red tomato and onion sauce. The sauce is thick with visible pieces of diced onion and crushed tomato, creating a rich texture. Fresh green basil leaves, torn, are scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. Beside the plate, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish's warmth and comforting appeal, set against a subtle, blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread (pane) to soak up the sauce
Creamy polenta or pasta (e.g., pappardelle, rigatoni)
A sprinkle of grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese
A glass of robust red wine
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Discard rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf sprigs.
If sauce is too thin, increase heat and simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes until desired consistency.
Return chicken to sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The Thai Basil Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, alongside a mound of fluffy white jasmine rice. The chicken mince, cooked to a rich brown, is mixed with vibrant green wilted basil leaves and flecks of red chili. A perfectly fried egg with a crisp edge and a glossy, runny yolk rests atop the rice. The dish displays a balanced composition of textures and colors: the tender chicken, fresh basil, and the golden egg. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing each element to stand out. A set of chopsticks rests beside the plate, on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting with an authentic Thai culinary touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) for extra seasoning.
Traditionally eaten with jasmine rice as a staple accompaniment.
A fried egg (kai dao) is a common and essential topping.
instructions: Prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Mix well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat until smoking.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince to the wok. Break up the chicken with a spatula. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the prepared sauce over the chicken. Stir quickly to coat all ingredients.
Add the basil leaves. Stir-fry for 30-60 seconds until basil wilts but retains vibrant green color.
Remove from heat immediately.
While chicken cooks, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Serve the Thai Basil Chicken stir-fry immediately over individual portions of cooked jasmine rice, topped with a fried egg.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Garlic-Herb Sauce and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its golden-brown crust hints at crispness. Adjacent, roasted broccoli florets, some with slightly charred edges, provide vibrant green and textural contrast. A light, glistening garlic-herb sauce is spooned elegantly over the chicken, pooling subtly at its base. A fresh lemon wedge accompanies the dish. The chicken is a central focal point, with broccoli arranged organically. The sauce adds a fluid element. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting, clean and uncluttered.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast broccoli for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken, let rest on a cutting board.
While chicken rests, finely chop garlic, parsley, and thyme.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add butter and chopped garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and juice from half a lemon. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in chopped parsley and thyme. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice remaining lemon into wedges for garnish.
Serve chicken breasts whole or cut into thick chunks. Spoon garlic-herb sauce over chicken. Serve with roasted broccoli.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Cheesy Tomato-Garlic Relish
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is golden-brown, with a slightly crisp exterior, presented as a whole, un-sliced piece. A generous spoonful of vibrant red and orange cheesy tomato-garlic relish, featuring softened cherry tomato halves and melted, slightly browned cheese, is spooned over the top of the chicken. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of creamy white cannellini beans, braised in beer, is arranged. The beans are plump and intact. A thin, pale yellow drizzle of mustard-mayo sauce artfully streaks across the plate, creating visual interest. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley over the chicken and beans. The overall color palette is inviting, with golden brown chicken, red and orange relish, white beans, and green parsley, offering varied textures from seared crispness to creamy softness. Appropriate negative space surrounds the components, ensuring a clean and professional appearance. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtle, blurred background suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere. This is a single individual portion.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board.

In the same pan, add a splash more olive oil if needed. Add halved cherry tomatoes and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and bubbly. Keep warm.
In a separate medium pot, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until fragrant and softened.

Add drained and rinsed cannellini beans and lager beer to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid slightly reduces and beans are heated through. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise and Dijon mustard until smooth.
To plate, place one pan-seared chicken breast centrally on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the cheesy tomato-garlic relish over the chicken.
Arrange a mound of beer-braised cannellini beans alongside the chicken.
Drizzle the mustard-mayo sauce artistically around the plate or over the chicken and beans.
Garnish the dish with freshly chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Soy-Ginger Chicken and Shrimp Noodles
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant medley of colors and textures. Steaming egg noodles form a generous base, loosely coiled. Cubes of seared chicken, cooked to a golden-brown, are interspersed with plump, pink shrimp. Bright red and yellow julienned bell peppers, thinly sliced onions, and earthy brown mushroom slices are tossed throughout, offering a lively contrast. Halved baby corn adds a touch of yellow. The noodles and ingredients are coated in a glossy, light brown soy-ginger sauce, reflecting the light. A sprinkle of fresh, thinly sliced green spring onions provides a final pop of color. The arrangement is organic yet inviting, with distinct components visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer small individual ceramic bowls for serving.
Serve with a side of chili garlic sauce or sriracha for those desiring extra heat.
instructions: Cook noodles according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat. Add chicken cubes. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through to 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to wok. Add shrimp. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until pink and opaque. Remove shrimp from wok.
Add sliced onion, julienned bell peppers, sliced mushrooms, and baby corn to the wok. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to vegetables. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, chicken stock, and sesame oil.
Pour sauce mixture into the wok with vegetables. Bring to a simmer.
In a separate small bowl, whisk cornstarch with water to create a slurry. Stir slurry into simmering sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return cooked chicken and shrimp to the wok. Add cooked noodles. Toss everything to combine and coat evenly with the sauce.
Serve immediately. Garnish with sliced spring onions.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not overcrowd the wok when stir-frying to ensure ingredients brown properly and cook evenly. Cook in batches if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Potato Bake is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, roasted chicken thighs, cooked whole, are nestled amongst a generous pile of tender potato wedges. The chicken has a slight crisp, showcasing a warm brown hue. The potato wedges, cut into thick chunks, are golden-brown with soft interiors. Melted, bubbly cheddar cheese forms a comforting blanket over the chicken and potatoes. Vibrant green chopped green onions are scattered across the dish. The plate sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table, indicative of a cozy family kitchen. Warm, soft lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comforting textures. A casually placed linen napkin and a simple fork complete the homely scene. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a modest, satisfying portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread on the side for soaking up juices.

ingredients.name: potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Russet), cut into 2-3 cm wedges or large chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, chicken thighs, smashed garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper, paprika, and dried oregano. Toss well to coat.
Spread the mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken and potatoes are not overcrowded.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with chopped green onions before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For crispier potatoes, ensure they are spread in a single layer without overcrowding the pan. Use two pans if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Birria de Res
recipes.visual_description: The Birria de Res is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, reddish-brown hue. Tender, shredded beef chunks are generously bathed in the glossy, thick chili-tomato broth. A small, separate mound of fluffy white basmati rice sits beside the bowl on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Alongside the rice are a few golden-brown, soft potato cubes, some slightly caramelized. The birria is garnished with a sprinkle of finely diced white onion and fresh, vibrant green chopped cilantro, providing a striking color contrast. A lime wedge rests on the plate's rim. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting textures and warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping and making tacos.
Offer additional garnishes like finely diced white onion, fresh cilantro, and lime wedges.
Serve with a side of frijoles charros (charro beans) or a simple avocado salad.

ingredients.name: Russet potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Rehydrate chilies. Place deseeded guajillo and ancho chilies in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Soak for 20 minutes until softened.
Prepare sauce base. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium-high heat. Add roughly chopped onion, garlic, and halved tomatoes. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Blend sauce. Drain rehydrated chilies. Add chilies, sautéed vegetables, cumin seeds, Mexican oregano, bay leaves, apple cider vinegar, and 250 ml of beef broth to a blender. Blend until very smooth.

Sear beef. Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper. In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, sear beef chunks in batches over high heat until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Cook birria. Pour blended sauce into the Dutch oven. Bring to a simmer. Return seared beef to the pot. Add remaining 750 ml beef broth. Ensure beef is mostly submerged.
Simmer birria. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 3-4 hours, or until beef is very tender and easily shredded with a fork.
Prepare rice. While birria simmers, rinse basmati rice. Cook according to package directions.
Cook potatoes. Boil potato cubes in salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well.
Shred beef. Remove beef from the pot. Shred beef into smaller pieces using two forks. Return shredded beef to the sauce.
Adjust seasoning. Taste birria and adjust salt and pepper as needed. Remove bay leaves before serving.
Warm tortillas. Warm corn tortillas on a comal or dry skillet until pliable.
notes: For extra flavor, toast the dried chilies lightly in a dry pan before rehydrating.
The birria sauce can be made a day in advance for deeper flavor.
Leftover birria is excellent for quesadillas or mulitas.
Chicken can be substituted for beef; adjust cooking time accordingly to 75°C internal temperature.
traditional_techniques: Soaking and blending dried chilies for a rich sauce.
Slow braising (estofado) of meat until fork-tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Quick-Pickled Cucumber & Tomato Salad with Roasted Potato and Crispy Sourdough Crumbs
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earth-toned glaze, showcasing a natural, unforced arrangement. Roasted potato cubes, with their golden-brown edges, form the base. Vibrant quick-pickled cucumber half-moons and translucent, thinly sliced red onion are artfully scattered amongst the potatoes. Bright red halved tomatoes add pops of color. The elements are lightly coated in a glistening, pale yellow dressing, allowing their natural textures and colors to shine. Hard-boiled egg quarters, with their creamy white and yellow, are placed strategically. A generous sprinkle of rustic, crispy sourdough crumbs, with hints of golden-brown from toasting, provides a textural contrast. The composition is clean and mindful, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting, emphasizing the dish's sustainable ethos.
instructions: Prepare quick pickle brine: Combine 120 ml water, 60 ml white wine vinegar, 10 g sugar, and 5 g salt in a bowl. Whisk until sugar and salt dissolve.
Slice cucumber into thin half-moons. Thinly slice red onion. Add cucumber and onion to the brine. Let marinate for at least 15 minutes.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss potatoes with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly golden. Set aside to cool.
Hard boil eggs: Place eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water. Bring to a rolling boil, then remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 10 minutes. Drain, cool in ice water, peel, and quarter.

Prepare crispy sourdough crumbs: Tear day-old sourdough bread into small, irregular pieces. Mince garlic clove. In a small pan, heat 15 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add bread pieces and minced garlic. Toast, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy. Set aside.
Halve or quarter small tomatoes. Set aside.

Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, combine 30 ml lemon juice, 15 ml olive oil, 5 ml Dijon mustard, 5 ml honey, and 2 g black pepper. Whisk well. Add 1-2 tablespoons of the quick pickle brine from the cucumber and onion mixture for extra flavor. Whisk again.

Drain quick-pickled cucumber and red onion, reserving the brine. In a large bowl, combine roasted potato cubes, quick-pickled cucumber, quick-pickled red onion, and halved/quartered tomatoes. Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat.
Divide salad between two plates. Arrange the hard-boiled egg quarters on top. Sprinkle generously with crispy sourdough crumbs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, hearty portion of Classic Beef Shepherd's Pie is presented in a deep, oval ceramic baking dish, slightly browned on top. The golden-brown mashed potato crust, with its characteristic fork-tined peaks, forms a comforting, textured surface. Beneath, the rich, savory ground beef and vegetable filling is visible where a scoop has been taken out, revealing diced carrots, peas, and corn in a thick, dark brown gravy. The dish is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, off-white ceramic plate beside it, ready for serving. A basic silver fork and knife are placed casually. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene from above, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation emphasizes a satisfying, home-cooked meal, with natural colors and textures, and a generous, comforting portion.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (Russet or similar, peeled and quartered)

instructions: Prepare Potatoes: Place quartered potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain Potatoes: Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot to dry for 1 minute.
Mash Potatoes: Add milk, butter, and a pinch of salt to potatoes. Mash until smooth and creamy. Beat in the egg until combined. Set aside.

Brown Beef: Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Sauté Vegetables: Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the skillet with the beef. Cook until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Thicken Sauce: Stir in flour and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.

Add Liquids and Seasoning: Gradually pour in beef broth, stirring to prevent lumps. Add Worcestershire sauce and dried thyme. Bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Frozen Vegetables: Stir in frozen peas and corn. Cook for 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble Pie: Spoon the beef mixture evenly into a 23x33 cm (9x13 inch) baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet. Top with the mashed potatoes. Spread potatoes evenly, creating peaks with a fork for texture.
Bake Pie: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the filling is bubbling and the potato topping is golden brown.
Rest and Serve: Let the pie rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.
notes: For extra browning on the mashed potato, you can place the pie under a broiler for 2-3 minutes at the end, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Ensure the beef is cooked to 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, dark red-brown ragu, forming an appealing mound. Tender, large chunks of braised beef are visibly nestled within the sauce and pasta, showcasing their fork-shredded texture. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped Italian parsley adds a vibrant color contrast, along with a generous dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, providing a touch of white and a slightly coarser texture. The plating is organized yet retains a natural, flowing quality, with moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, illuminated by natural, even light, capturing the warmth and richness of the dish. Traditional flatware is placed beside the plate, and a crisp cotton napkin completes the modern bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, highlighting the professional, approachable presentation. The beef is presented as large chunks, while the vegetables in the soffritto are finely diced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.
instructions: Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine has mostly evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, bay leaf, and thyme.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F) or continue simmering on stovetop over very low heat. Cook for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef into smaller pieces using two forks. Discard bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cook pappardelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each plate with grated Pecorino Romano cheese and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Soy Garlic Chicken and Potato with Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, individual portion of Spicy Soy Garlic Chicken and Potato with Cheese is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features tender, succulent chicken thigh chunks (3-4 cm) coated in a rich, glossy, reddish-brown gochujang-soy sauce, nestled among soft, 2 cm potato cubes. A generous layer of melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese blankets the top, creating a tempting contrast. Bright green, thinly sliced green onions are scattered across the cheese, providing a fresh pop of color and herbaceous aroma. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a set of traditional Korean metal chopsticks and a small white rice bowl, alongside a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and vibrant colors. A subtle, blurred bistro-style background suggests a casual dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of kimchi.
Include various banchan (small side dishes) such as pickled radishes or seasoned spinach.
Eat with metal chopsticks and a spoon.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, boneless, skinless, cut into 3-4 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, peeled, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.quantity: 4, sliced, white and green parts separated

instructions: Prepare chicken: In a bowl, combine chicken chunks, 30 ml soy sauce, 30 g gochujang, 10 g gochugaru, 3 minced garlic cloves, 10 ml sesame oil, 10 g sugar, and black pepper. Mix well. Marinate 30 minutes.

Cook potatoes: Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add potato cubes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Remove potatoes, set aside.
Cook chicken: Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry until browned on all sides, about 8-10 minutes.

Combine: Add cooked potatoes back to the pan with the chicken. Add remaining 30 ml soy sauce, 30 g gochujang, 5 g gochugaru, 3 minced garlic cloves, and white parts of green onions. Pour in water or stock. Bring to a simmer.
Braise: Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (75°C internal temperature) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Finish with cheese: Uncover. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese evenly over the chicken and potatoes. Cover again for 2-3 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish: Remove from heat. Sprinkle with remaining green onion greens and 5 ml sesame oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust gochujang and gochugaru to your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For extra flavor, you can add a drizzle of sesame oil just before serving.
traditional_techniques: Layering of savory, sweet, and spicy flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Rustic Chicken and Potato Stew is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly uneven, natural glaze. The stew features hearty chunks of seared chicken, tender 2 cm potato cubes, diced tomatoes, and vibrant green peas, all coated in a rich, savory broth. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, unpretentious mound in the bowl. Fresh, chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, adding a pop of green. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, everyday metal spoon rests beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and cozy, emanating from kitchen fixtures, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is visible in the background, out of focus. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the homely, comforting presentation without overcrowding.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Russet)
ingredients.quantity: 500 grams, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Add chicken to pot. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced potatoes and canned diced tomatoes with their juices.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.

Return seared chicken to the pot. Cover. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75 0C (167 0F).
Stir in frozen green peas. Cook for 3-5 minutes, until peas are heated through.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Bake
recipes.visual_description: Diced chicken pieces and bright green broccoli florets are nestled within a rich, creamy, off-white sauce. The dish is topped with a generous layer of melted, golden-brown cheddar cheese, showing bubbly, slightly crisped edges. The texture is hearty, with tender chicken, slightly firm broccoli, and a smooth, thick sauce beneath a savory cheese crust. Presented as a generous, natural portion scooped into a deep, off-white ceramic bowl. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin and a metal fork rest beside the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the comforting appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain white rice or egg noodles to soak up the creamy sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken breast into 2 cm diced pieces. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Steam broccoli florets for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain well.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in plain flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in sour cream until well combined. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked chicken and steamed broccoli to the sauce. Stir gently to coat.
Pour mixture into a 2-liter baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for a few minutes before serving.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to your preference, adding more salt or pepper as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Garlic Parmesan Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual serving of One-Pan Garlic Parmesan Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. Two succulent bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, roasted to a golden-brown crisp, are placed centrally. Around them, generous chunks of roasted potatoes, some halved and some quartered, exhibit a beautiful golden-brown crust and tender interior. Scattered among the potatoes are soft, caramelized whole garlic cloves. Melted, bubbly Parmesan cheese lightly coats the chicken skin and potato surfaces, showing slight browning in spots. A sprinkle of vibrant green, chopped fresh parsley adds a touch of color. The arrangement is casual and natural, with components touching and overlapping. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, alongside a simple silver fork and knife. A casually folded plain cloth napkin rests nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting light, typical of a cozy family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut larger potatoes into halves or quarters. Keep small potatoes whole.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, potatoes, peeled garlic cloves, olive oil, oregano, thyme, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread chicken and potatoes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip potatoes and chicken. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese over chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh parsley if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chocolate Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A warm, golden-brown bread pudding, baked in a rustic ceramic dish. The top surface features toasted, slightly crisped bread cubes, with melted dark chocolate chips forming glossy pools and streaks, contrasting with the lighter custardy bread. The edges are caramelized. The interior is soft and moist. Scooped onto a simple, everyday ceramic plate, the 2cm irregular bread cubes showcase a homely cut. Served on a warm-toned wooden kitchen table, the plate holds a generous, natural scoop. A plain fabric napkin is casually placed. Warm, inviting kitchen light casts soft shadows. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen. A single, ample individual portion is naturally presented, highlighting the bread and melted chocolate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream.

ingredients.name: Stale white bread or challah, cut into 2cm cubes
Dark chocolate chips or chopped dark chocolate

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Lightly butter a 1.5 litre baking dish.
Place bread cubes into the prepared dish.
In a bowl, whisk milk, sugar, eggs, melted butter, vanilla extract, and salt.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the bread cubes.
Gently press bread down to absorb liquid.
Scatter chocolate chips over the bread.
Let stand 10 minutes for bread to soak.
Bake for 30-35 minutes.
Pudding is done when golden brown and set in the center.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Milk Pudding with Candied Tomato & Pasta Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chocolate Milk Pudding is elegantly presented in a clean, white porcelain dessert bowl, set on a simple wooden table surface. The pudding itself is a rich, glossy dark brown, its creamy texture visible. A generous dollop of fluffy, pale yellow lemon yogurt foam rests slightly off-center on the pudding, offering a soft contrast. Around the foam, a scattering of vibrant red, translucent candied cherry tomato halves provides bursts of color and a hint of sweetness. Interspersed among these are delicate, golden-brown shards of crisp, sweetened angel hair pasta, adding a textural crunch. A fresh, bright green mint leaf and a whisper of finely grated lemon zest serve as a final, fresh garnish. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, featuring natural, even lighting. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl. The overall presentation is professional yet inviting, emphasizing the dessert's refined simplicity and appealing textures.
instructions: Boil chicken breast until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Cool completely. Shred chicken extremely finely, almost to a paste. Set aside.

Rinse rice. In a large saucepan, combine rice, milk, and finely shredded chicken. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring frequently, until rice is tender and mixture thickens.
Stir in 150g granulated sugar and chopped dark chocolate until melted and well combined. Add vanilla extract. Cook for 5 more minutes, stirring, until pudding is creamy and thick. Remove from heat.

Halve cherry tomatoes. In a small saucepan, combine 50g granulated sugar and 50ml water. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add halved tomatoes. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until tomatoes are slightly softened and translucent. Remove tomatoes from syrup and let cool.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Break angel hair pasta into small pieces. Toss with melted butter, powdered sugar, and a pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool.
In a bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt, lemon juice, 5g lemon zest, and honey until smooth and slightly aerated.

Spoon warm chocolate milk pudding into individual serving bowls. Top with a dollop of lemon yogurt foam. Arrange a few candied tomato halves and a sprinkle of pasta crisp pieces on top. Garnish with a fresh mint leaf and a little extra lemon zest.
notes: The chicken breast is prepared in a traditional Turkish pudding style, shredded extremely finely to become imperceptible in texture, contributing only a unique creaminess and subtle body to the pudding without a savory chicken flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna with Warm Tomato Vinaigrette and Soft-Boiled Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single seared tuna steak, cooked to a rosy medium-rare, anchors the center of a clean white porcelain plate. Its exterior shows a distinct golden-brown crust. Around the tuna, a vibrant medley of warm, slightly burst cherry tomatoes, some gently mashed, forms a rustic, glossy vinaigrette. Thick slices of creamy green avocado are artfully placed beside the tuna. Two halves of a soft-boiled egg, revealing a rich yellow yolk, rest near the avocado. The dish is subtly garnished with fresh green basil leaves and chopped parsley, providing a pop of color. The composition is balanced, leaving appropriate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the flavorful tomato vinaigrette.
A simple side salad of mixed greens with a light lemon vinaigrette complements the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a baking dish, combine cherry tomatoes, 30ml olive oil, sliced garlic, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly burst. Remove from oven.

Bring a small pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for exactly 6 minutes for soft-boiled. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel gently under cold running water once cooled. Halve each egg lengthwise.
Halve avocados, remove pit. Scoop out flesh. Cut into thick slices or wedges.

To the warm roasted tomatoes, add remaining 30ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, capers (if using), and half of the torn basil and chopped parsley. Gently stir to combine, slightly mashing some tomatoes to create a rustic sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Pat tuna steaks very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Add a thin layer of olive oil. Carefully place tuna steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 1.5-2 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness.

Place one seared tuna steak on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of the warm tomato vinaigrette around and over the tuna. Arrange avocado slices beside the tuna. Place two egg halves on the plate. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust tuna searing time to achieve desired doneness; 1.5-2 minutes per side typically yields a good medium-rare for a 2.5 cm thick steak.
Quality of ingredients, especially tuna and olive oil, significantly impacts the final flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Clásico
recipes.visual_description: The Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous single portion. Golden-orange, moist medium-grain rice forms the base, studded with vibrant, uniformly diced red and yellow bell peppers, bright orange diced carrots, and soft, creamy diced butternut squash. Large, succulent chunks of seared chicken are nestled throughout the rice, displaying a rich, caramelized exterior. A scattering of bright green peas adds pops of color. The dish is garnished with freshly chopped green cilantro, providing a contrasting verdant hue. The composition is organic and flowing, not overly structured, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin, and a traditional, simple fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh citrus squeeze.
Traditionally accompanied by warm, crusty bread.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion, red and yellow bell peppers, carrot, and butternut squash to the pan. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, and bay leaf. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes to coat rice in aromatics.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking, if using.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Discard bay leaf.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
For best results, use a heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven to prevent sticking.
Avoid over-stirring the rice to prevent it from becoming gummy.
traditional_techniques: Sofrito preparation for the aromatic base

recipes.recipe_name: Homely Chicken & Potato Curry with Basmati Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Homely Chicken & Potato Curry is presented on a rustic, earthy-toned ceramic plate. The rich, reddish-orange curry with tender chicken chunks and soft diced potatoes fills one side of the plate. The chicken pieces are natural, un-sliced, and coated in the savory sauce. Fluffy, white basmati rice is piled neatly on the other side. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh coriander garnishes the curry. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, everyday fork and spoon are casually placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comfortable, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Naan bread or Chapati.
A small bowl of plain yogurt or Raita on the side.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add chopped onions. Cook until softened and golden, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, and turmeric powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes. Cook, mashing with a spoon, until tomatoes break down and oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add chicken chunks and diced potatoes to the pot. Stir to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in water or broth. Add salt. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
While curry cooks, rinse basmati rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions.
Stir in garam masala into the curry.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Vegetable Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Chicken and Vegetable Skillet on a simple, round ceramic plate. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Large, irregular chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are nestled among quartered, tender potatoes and softened, rustic-cut pieces of red bell pepper, sautéed mushrooms, and caramelized onion. A light, savory pan sauce coats the ingredients. The colors are natural and inviting: warm browns from the chicken and mushrooms, vibrant red from the bell pepper, and creamy white from the potatoes. A few fresh green basil leaves are scattered on top for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is casual and natural, typical of a home-cooked meal, with components slightly overlapping. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin and everyday flatware are casually placed next to the plate.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large, irregular chunks. Quarter the small potatoes. Slice mushrooms. Roughly chop onion and bell pepper. Mince garlic.
Season chicken chunks generously with salt and black pepper. Lightly dust chicken with flour.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add chopped onion, bell pepper, and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a gentle simmer.
Add quartered potatoes to the skillet. Stir gently to combine. Cover skillet with a lid.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken is cooked through.
Remove lid. Increase heat slightly if needed to reduce sauce to desired consistency. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato and Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Roasted Potato and Rice Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of textures and colors. Diced potatoes, roasted to a golden-brown with a crisp exterior and fluffy interior, are prominently visible alongside halved, tender roasted cherry tomatoes. Fluffy white cooked rice intersperses with thinly sliced crimson red onion and flecks of bright green minced chili. The salad is casually mounded in the center of the plate, allowing for moderate negative space around the edges. A light, glossy chili-lime vinaigrette subtly coats the ingredients, reflecting the natural light. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered generously over the top, adding a final touch of color and freshness. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin positioned to the side, under soft, even natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice potatoes into 1.5-2 cm cubes. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Toss diced potatoes and halved cherry tomatoes with 45ml olive oil, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until potatoes are tender and lightly browned. Let cool slightly.
Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic cloves. Seed and finely mince green chili.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled roasted potatoes and tomatoes with the cooked rice and finely diced red onion.
For the dressing, whisk together 15ml olive oil, lime juice, minced garlic, minced green chili, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Pour dressing over the potato mixture. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Chop fresh cilantro. Fold cilantro into the salad.
Serve immediately or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Root Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty chicken and root vegetable stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled amongst tender, thick-cut potato wedges and vibrant orange braised carrot rounds, all bathed in a rich, savory brown gravy. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, showcasing their comforting textures and inviting colors. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley adds a touch of green. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casually placed, simple cloth napkin and a plain water glass are visible in the soft, warm light of a homely kitchen setting, emphasizing a relaxed, comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich gravy
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large 4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into large 4 cm wedges.
Peel carrots. Cut into thick 2 cm rounds.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Slowly pour in chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Add seared chicken, potato wedges, carrot rounds, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf to the pot.
Bring stew to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes.
Cook until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use chicken thighs with bone and skin removed after searing.
Adjust thickness of gravy by simmering longer or adding a cornstarch slurry if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Tomatoes and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of braised beef with potatoes and tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The beef, cut into substantial 4-5 cm chunks, is dark, fork-tender, and coated in a rich, glossy, deep reddish-brown tomato-based sauce. Quartered potatoes, tender and slightly yielding, are nestled among the beef, absorbing the sauce's flavors. Vibrant green chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the dish, providing a fresh color contrast. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and deep colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and appealing presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the rich sauce.
instructions: Cut beef into 4-5 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add diced onions, chopped carrots, and chopped celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Return seared beef to the pot. Add bay leaves and thyme sprigs.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer the covered pot to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2 hours.
Peel and quarter potatoes. Add them to the pot with the beef. Gently stir to submerge potatoes.
Continue braising for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is very tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Ladle braised beef and potatoes onto plates. Garnish generously with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Garlic Honey and Root Vegetable Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening from a fermented garlic honey glaze, rests centrally on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The chicken skin is crisp. Rustic 3 cm chunks of roasted carrots, parsnips, and potatoes, along with vibrant green broccoli florets, 2 cm broccoli stem discs, and tender cauliflower florets and leaves, are arranged naturally around the chicken. Vegetables show slight caramelization. A scattering of delicate, golden-brown root vegetable crisps adds texture. The minimalistic plating leaves ample white space, highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. The scene is set on a light, natural wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in beige is subtly placed. Soft, natural lighting creates a clean ambiance. Simple, elegant flatware rests beside the plate. The background is uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash carrots, parsnips, and potatoes thoroughly. Peel all three vegetables, reserving all peels.
Cut peeled carrots, parsnips, and potatoes into rustic 3 cm chunks. Set aside.
Trim broccoli and cauliflower. Separate florets. Cut broccoli stems into 2 cm discs. Tear cauliflower leaves into large pieces. Set all aside.

For crisps: Toss reserved vegetable peels with 15 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Bake 10-15 minutes until crispy and golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove and set aside.
Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides.

Heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or roasting pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.

Add chunked carrots, parsnips, potatoes, broccoli florets and stems, cauliflower florets and leaves, onion quarters, rosemary, and thyme to the skillet around the chicken. Toss vegetables with pan drippings and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 25 minutes. Internal temperature of chicken should reach 75°C (167°F).
Brush chicken generously with fermented garlic honey during the last 10 minutes of roasting. Ensure chicken reaches safe internal temperature.
Remove skillet from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve chicken with roasted vegetables. Garnish each plate with a scattering of root vegetable crisps.
notes: For zero-waste, chicken bones and vegetable scraps can be used to make a nutritious stock.
Fermented garlic honey can be made at home by submerging peeled garlic cloves in honey and letting it ferment for several weeks at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Chicken with Fermented Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, placed on a light bamboo table surface. A single portion of whole wheat penne pasta forms a natural mound in the center. Draped over the pasta are tender, slow-cooked chicken pieces, still retaining their natural shape. A rich, deep red fermented tomato sauce generously coats the pasta and chicken, showcasing its rustic texture. Scattered around are vibrant, lightly cooked seasonal vegetable pieces, such as small zucchini half-moons and red bell pepper strips, adding pops of natural color. Crispy, golden-brown chicken skin shards are strategically placed atop the chicken, providing a textural contrast. A few fresh basil leaves are sparingly placed for a touch of green. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space on the plate. The textures are natural and inviting. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its organic beauty. A simple undyed linen napkin and perhaps a small, unglazed ceramic bowl for a side are visible in the background, maintaining an eco-conscious, uncluttered aesthetic. Chicken is presented in natural chunks, never fanned.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Sauce: Roughly chop tomatoes, garlic, and onion. Place in a clean 2-liter glass jar. Dissolve 20g sea salt in 500ml filtered water to make a brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Add bay leaf. Cover loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Blend contents of jar until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve if a smoother sauce is desired. Set aside.

Make Chicken Stock (Optional Zero-Waste Step): If using chicken bones, place them in a pot, cover with 2 liters of water. Bring to a simmer, skim foam. Add any vegetable scraps. Simmer gently for 1-2 hours. Strain and set aside. Use water or store-bought stock if bones are unavailable.
Prepare Chicken: Carefully remove skin from chicken thighs. Reserve skin. Season chicken thighs with salt and black pepper.

Cook Chicken: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown. Pour in enough chicken stock (or water) to partially cover chicken (approx. 500ml). Bring to a simmer, reduce heat to low, cover, and slow-cook for 45-60 minutes. Cook until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot, set aside. Reserve cooking liquid.

Crisp Chicken Skin: While chicken cooks, preheat a dry pan over medium heat. Lay reserved chicken skins flat. Press down with a spatula. Cook until deeply golden brown and very crispy, about 5-8 minutes per side. Remove, drain on paper towels, season with a pinch of salt. Break into shards.

Finish Sauce: Add fermented tomato sauce to the pot with reserved chicken cooking liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook Pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add penne pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.

Combine and Serve: Gently shred or chunk the slow-cooked chicken meat. Add cooked pasta, chicken pieces, zucchini half-moons, and bell pepper strips to the sauce. Toss gently to combine. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until vegetables are lightly cooked but still have a bite.
Plate: Serve individual portions of pasta and chicken on ceramic plates. Garnish with crispy chicken skin shards and fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Italian Sausage and Crab Orecchiette
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of vibrant Spicy Italian Sausage and Crab Orecchiette is presented in a shallow, matte white porcelain pasta bowl. The orecchiette, perfectly al dente, is generously coated in a rich, rustic tomato-cream sauce with a subtle orange hue. Crumbled, browned Italian sausage chunks are interspersed throughout, alongside tender, golden-brown sliced cremini mushrooms. Bright, sweet crab meat pieces are gently folded in, adding delicate white and pink accents. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley and grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese garnishes the top. The dish is naturally arranged, allowing the textures and colors of the ingredients to shine. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface, beside a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese at the table.
instructions: Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook orecchiette according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage. Break sausage into small pieces with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the same skillet. Cook until softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms. Set aside with sausage.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallot to the skillet. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in cooked sausage and mushrooms. Add heavy cream. Simmer 2 minutes.
Add cooked orecchiette to the sauce. Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water gradually, 60 ml at a time, until sauce coats pasta well.
Gently fold in fresh crab meat and half of the chopped parsley. Heat through 1-2 minutes. Do not overcook crab.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and extra Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes for desired spice level.
Fresh crab meat is recommended for best flavor. Canned crab can be used if fresh is unavailable, but drain very well.
Do not overcook the crab meat; add it at the very end to warm through.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Potato & Kohlrabi Gratin with Smoked Tempeh and Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of gratin is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl, its cream-colored glaze reflecting natural light. Layers of tender, thinly sliced potato and kohlrabi are visible, baked to a golden-brown on top with a slightly crisp edge. Dark brown, firm chunks of smoked tempeh are interspersed within the layers, offering visual contrast. Scattered across the gratin's surface are small, irregular pieces of crispy, reddish-brown bacon, providing texture. A few fresh green thyme leaves are placed sparingly on top. The gratin occupies the center of the bowl, leaving ample white space around the edges. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its natural textures and earthy colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green foliage from a plant, emphasizing the dish's connection to nature and sustainability.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Render diced bacon in a cold oven-safe skillet or baking dish until crispy. Remove bacon. Reserve rendered fat.
Add olive oil and a portion of the reserved bacon fat to the skillet. Sauté tempeh cubes until golden. Set aside.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in milk, cream, and vegetable broth. Add thyme, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Layer thinly sliced potatoes and kohlrabi in the skillet. Distribute tempeh cubes, finely chopped lacto-fermented kohlrabi, and grated cheddar between layers.
Pour the hot cream mixture over the layers. Ensure liquid almost covers the top layer.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly.
Sprinkle crispy bacon on top during the last 10 minutes of baking, or after baking.
Let gratin rest 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Sausage Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty portion of baked chicken and sausage pasta is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic baking dish, slightly overflowing onto a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features al dente penne pasta coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, interspersed with tender, diced chicken chunks and savory, crumbled Italian sausage. A thick, bubbly layer of golden-brown melted mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese forms the top, with some crispy, golden breadcrumbs scattered across. The sauce peeks through, revealing flecks of green herbs. The overall appearance is warm and inviting, showcasing comforting textures and rich colors. The dish sits on a worn wooden kitchen table, accompanied by a casually folded linen napkin and a sturdy fork, under warm, ambient kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Accompany with warm, crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Boil 200g penne pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add 200g Italian sausage, crumbled. Cook until browned. Remove sausage and drain excess fat. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same pan. Add 300g chicken breast, diced into 2cm cubes. Sear until lightly browned. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 chopped medium onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add 3 minced garlic cloves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in 400g crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Return cooked sausage and chicken to the sauce. Stir in the cooked pasta.
If not using an oven-safe pan, transfer the mixture to a 20x20cm baking dish. Top evenly with 100g shredded mozzarella and 50g grated Parmesan.
In a small bowl, melt 20g butter. Toss with 50g fresh breadcrumbs until coated. Sprinkle the breadcrumbs over the cheese layer.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato, Rice and Roasted Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, homely salad presented in a rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The base consists of fluffy white rice, generously mixed with beautifully roasted vegetables. Diced potatoes exhibit tender, slightly browned edges. Halved cherry tomatoes are softened and burst with color. Red onion wedges show caramelization, and whole roasted garlic cloves are golden and sweet. Finely shredded chicken is subtly integrated, providing a small protein accent without dominating the dish. The salad is casually tossed, allowing the components to overlap naturally. A simple vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients. Fresh, chopped parsley is sprinkled over, adding a vibrant green contrast. The overall palette is warm and earthy, reflecting the roasted elements. The scene is lit by warm, natural kitchen light, conveying a relaxed, family meal atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and basic cutlery complete the unpretentious setting.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

Toss diced potatoes, halved cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, and whole garlic cloves with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on the baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized. Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
While vegetables roast, cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cook chicken breast: Season chicken with salt and pepper. Pan-fry or bake until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred the cooked chicken finely. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the roasted vegetables, cooked rice, and shredded chicken. Add the finely minced red chili.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Add chopped fresh parsley. Toss gently to combine. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked thoroughly to 75°C internal temperature.
Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Picante
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo Picante is presented in a deep, round white porcelain bowl. The dish features vibrant, reddish-orange rice, cooked to a tender yet distinct grain, interspersed with succulent, irregularly shaped 3 cm chunks of pan-seared chicken, exhibiting a golden-brown crust. Diced white onion and flecks of fresh green cilantro are visible throughout the rice, adding color and texture. A small cluster of fresh cilantro sprigs garnishes the center, alongside a bright green lime wedge placed on the rim of the bowl. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space around the food. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed neatly beside the bowl. In the background, slightly out of focus, a small, rustic Mexican ceramic dish holds a dollop of vibrant red salsa, and a stack of warm, neatly folded corn tortillas rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style presentation.
