cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of fresh salsa or extra hot sauce for additional spice.
Accompany with a simple green salad or sliced avocado.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Add diced white onion to the same pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked long-grain rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly translucent.
Pour in diced tomatoes, hot sauce, chicken broth, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Stir to combine. Bring the liquid to a rolling boil.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Stir gently to submerge. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly.
Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove the pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes to allow the rice to finish steaming.
Fluff the rice and chicken gently with a fork. Stir in fresh chopped cilantro.
Serve hot with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Chicken Garden Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the Fermented Tomato & Chicken Garden Soup is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a warm cream hue, centered on a light, naturally textured bamboo table. The deep, earthy red-orange broth is rich and inviting, with clearly visible, tender 1.5 cm diced chicken chunks, 1 cm diced potatoes, and vibrant green swiss chard leaves. Scattered throughout are smaller pieces of red bell pepper and sliced mushrooms, adding textural variety. The soup's surface is lightly garnished with a few crisp, golden-brown potato peels and a scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves. The setting features an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone, subtly enhancing the organic feel. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting its natural colors and clean composition against a minimalist background with a hint of green foliage.

ingredients.name: Chicken Thighs (boneless, skinless, diced 1.5 cm cubes)
Bell Pepper (any color, diced 1 cm cubes)
Canned Beans (e.g., cannellini or kidney, rinsed)
Chicken Broth (from scraps/bones, or low-sodium store-bought)

instructions: Prepare broth: Simmer chicken bones/carcass, onion peels, garlic skins, bell pepper cores, mushroom stems, basil stems, and chard stems in 2 liters of water for at least 1 hour. Strain. (Assume 1.5L ready broth for this recipe).
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced bell pepper. Cook for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add diced chicken. Cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Stir in sliced mushrooms, diced potatoes, and dried oregano. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the fermented tomato & chili paste and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in rinsed beans and thinly sliced swiss chard stems. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add swiss chard leaves. Cook until just wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
For garnishes: Toss potato peels and a few small swiss chard leaves with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt. Roast or air-fry until crispy.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish with crispy potato peels, crispy chard leaves, fresh basil leaves, and optional fermented garlic slices.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste cooking by utilizing vegetable scraps for broth and incorporating fermented ingredients for enhanced flavor and preservation. Pre-prepare fermented tomato & chili paste and fermented garlic slices for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Quinoa-Stuffed Tomatoes
recipes.special_requests: для пп и похудения без мяса и рыбы
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly baked, plump red tomato is the centerpiece on a clean white round porcelain plate. The tomato is gently cooked, its skin holding its shape, with a slightly golden-brown top from the oven. The quinoa filling, visible from the top, is mounded generously, showcasing a vibrant mix of white quinoa, green herbs, and small, distinct orange and green diced vegetables. A single, fresh sprig of bright green basil leaves rests delicately on top of the filling. A subtle sheen of olive oil glistens around the base of the tomato. The plate is set on a light-colored wooden table in a modern bistro style. A folded white cotton napkin and polished simple flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh colors and textures against a softly blurred, neutral background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon-herb vinaigrette
Offer crusty whole-grain bread on the side
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.

Rinse quinoa thoroughly. Combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Set aside.
Carefully cut the top off each tomato. Scoop out the pulp and seeds with a spoon, leaving a sturdy shell. Discard seeds. Finely chop the tomato pulp.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, diced zucchini, and diced red bell pepper. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, sautéed vegetables, chopped tomato pulp, fresh basil, fresh parsley, nutritional yeast (if using), salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Evenly fill each hollowed tomato with the quinoa mixture. Place stuffed tomatoes in a baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until tomatoes are tender and filling is heated through.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Lemon Herb Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests on a simple white ceramic plate. Alongside are hearty portions of rustic potato wedges, roasted to a tender interior and a crisp, golden exterior. Scattered among the chicken and potatoes are bright green sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme, and a few caramelized lemon slices. The chicken is whole, not sliced. The potato wedges are irregularly cut, showing their homely appeal. The dish is presented on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the plate, with a casually folded cloth napkin. The scene is uncluttered, focusing on the comforting appeal of the meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut potatoes into 2 cm rustic wedges.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towel.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potato wedges, olive oil, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, smashed garlic cloves, salt, paprika, and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients to coat evenly.
Spread chicken and potatoes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Arrange lemon slices among the ingredients.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For crispier potatoes, ensure they are spread in a single layer without overcrowding the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Tuna Niçoise Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate set on a light oak bistro table. The focal point is a thick, whole rectangular block of seared tuna, showing a thin grey seared edge and a vibrant deep pink center. Beside the tuna, two halves of a soft-boiled egg reveal jammy, translucent orange yolks. The salad consists of vibrant red cherry tomato halves, thick cucumber medallions, and delicate purple red onion rounds. The vegetables are lightly coated in a pale, creamy lemon-mayonnaise dressing. Fresh green parsley is scattered naturally across the plate. The lighting is bright and natural, coming from the side to highlight the textures of the seared fish and glossy egg yolks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices
Pair with a chilled dry Rosé from Provence
Provide a small bowl of Niçoise olives on the side
instructions: Boil water in a small pot. Add eggs and cook for 6 minutes and 30 seconds. Transfer eggs to ice water immediately. Peel and set aside.
Cut tuna loin into four thick 150g rectangular blocks.
Season tuna with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear tuna for 45 seconds per side until a crust forms but the center remains rare.
Slice cucumber into 2cm thick medallions. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice the red onion into rounds.
Whisk mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth.
Arrange cucumber medallions, tomatoes, and red onion on four plates.
Place one whole seared tuna block on each plate. Do not slice.
Halve the soft-boiled eggs and place next to the tuna.
Drizzle the mayonnaise dressing over the vegetables. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure the tuna is sushi-grade for the best flavor and safety.
Dry the tuna loin thoroughly with paper towels before searing to achieve a better crust.
The eggs should be at room temperature before boiling to prevent cracking.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken Provençal
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Chicken Provençal is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned bone-in chicken thigh is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are roasted potato quarters, some with lightly crisped edges and a tender interior, showcasing their golden-brown hue. Interspersed among the potatoes are soft, burst cherry tomatoes, vibrant red and slightly collapsed from roasting, alongside caramelized, translucent red onion wedges. A few dark, pitted Kalamata olives add depth of color. Fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are placed artfully for garnish. A light drizzle of the pan juices glistens over the dish. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with natural color balance. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, complemented by a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. Traditional flatware is placed alongside the plate, creating an authentic, approachable bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh crusty baguette to soak up the delicious pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Quarter small potatoes. Peel and quarter red onion. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, toss quartered potatoes, onion wedges, and smashed garlic with 2 tablespoons of olive oil, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Spread potato mixture in the skillet. Place seared chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the potatoes.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Remove skillet from oven. Add cherry tomatoes and olives around the chicken and potatoes. Pour white wine and chicken stock into the skillet.
Return to oven. Roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, use a cast-iron skillet or other oven-safe pan that can go from stovetop to oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mexican Chicken & Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Spicy Mexican Chicken & Rice Soup is presented in a clean, round white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The rich, clear red-orange broth is filled with tender 3 cm chicken chunks, soft 2 cm potato dice, distinct grains of white rice, and diced tomatoes. Fresh green cilantro leaves are generously scattered over the surface, with a few thin, bright green serrano chili slices providing a contrasting pop of color and subtle heat. A fresh lime wedge rests on the bowl's rim, ready to be squeezed. Beside the bowl, a small stack of warm corn tortillas, neatly wrapped in a beige cotton napkin, and a rustic ceramic dish holding creamy avocado slices complete the authentic Mexican casual dining experience. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping or making small tacos.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh citrusy finish.
Serve sliced avocado as a cooling accompaniment.
Provide additional hot sauce on the side for those who prefer more heat.

ingredients.name: Jalapeño or serrano chili, thinly sliced

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add minced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Brown lightly on all sides for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in diced Roma tomatoes, ground cumin, and dried Mexican oregano. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and washed rice to the pot. Stir well.
Continue to simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F), potatoes are tender, and rice is cooked.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls.
Garnish each serving with fresh chopped cilantro, extra chili slices if desired, and a lime wedge.
Serve immediately with warm corn tortillas and sliced avocado on the side.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.
For a richer flavor, brown chicken chunks more deeply before adding liquids.

recipes.recipe_name: Salade Niçoise
recipes.visual_description: The Salade Niçoise is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing vibrant natural colors and fresh textures. Thick, seared tuna medallions, with a pink interior and golden-brown crust, are thoughtfully arranged. Halved jammy-yolk eggs are placed, their creamy centers contrasting with the white. Bright red cherry tomatoes, some halved, are scattered alongside crisp-tender green bean batons and halved new potatoes. Dark Niçoise olives and thin red onion slices add depth. The dish is lightly dressed with a golden vinaigrette, glistening on the fresh mixed salad greens forming a base. The plating is organized yet organic, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin rests beside the plate on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh baguette.
Offer additional vinaigrette on the side.
Enjoy with a glass of chilled rosé wine.
instructions: Boil potatoes. Cook until tender. Drain and halve.
Steam green beans. Cook until crisp-tender. Plunge into ice water. Drain.
Hard boil eggs. Cook for 7-9 minutes. Peel and halve.
Prepare vinaigrette. Whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pat tuna steaks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add a touch of olive oil.
Sear tuna steaks. Cook 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest tuna 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.
Wash and dry salad greens. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion.
Assemble salads. Arrange salad greens on four plates.
Artfully place potatoes, green beans, halved tomatoes, sliced red onion, olives, and capers on each plate.
Add sliced tuna medallions and halved hard-boiled eggs to each salad.
Drizzle generously with vinaigrette. Serve immediately.
notes: Fresh tuna is preferred for authentic restaurant quality. If using canned tuna, use oil-packed and flake it generously over the salad.
Adjust tuna cooking time to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Quinoa and Turkey Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: Two vibrant bell pepper halves, filled with a hearty quinoa and ground turkey mixture, are perfectly arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The peppers, roasted to a tender-crisp, exhibit rich red and yellow hues. The filling is a harmonious blend of fluffy quinoa, finely crumbled lean ground turkey, diced red tomatoes, and wilted green spinach, all lightly seasoned. A delicate sprinkle of fresh green parsley garnishes the top of each pepper, adding a pop of fresh color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver cutlery and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting textures and colors. The scene is uncluttered, focusing entirely on the balanced, healthy main course.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Cook quinoa according to package directions. Use 300 ml water for 150g quinoa. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground turkey to skillet. Cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, oregano, and basil. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add cooked quinoa and fresh spinach to the turkey mixture. Stir until spinach wilts. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the turkey and quinoa mixture evenly into each bell pepper half.
Pour vegetable broth into the bottom of the baking dish. This creates steam.
Bake 30-35 minutes, or until peppers are tender-crisp and internal temperature of turkey reaches 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: This recipe is designed for healthy eating and weight management. It is high in protein and fiber.
Ensure ground turkey reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a rich, caramelized crust. A generous portion of creamy, savory mushroom sauce is spooned artfully over and around the chicken. The sauce is off-white with varying shades of earthy brown from the sliced mushrooms. The mushrooms are tender, with some retaining a slight chew. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its succulent texture. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface beside a folded cotton napkin. Standard European flatware is neatly placed. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour if using.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in white wine if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer 1 minute until reduced.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 2 minutes to heat through.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Spanish Chicken and Rice with Potatoes is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, resting on a rustic wooden table. Golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are placed atop a bed of saffron-infused short-grain rice. The rice is studded with diced ripe red tomatoes, small diced white potatoes, and bright green peas, creating a mosaic of colors and textures. Minced garlic and finely diced onions are subtly integrated into the rice. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, adding a pop of verdant green. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the rich colors and inviting textures. A simple white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, with a small, culturally authentic Spanish ceramic olive dish nearby, adding to the bistro-style setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan in the center of the table.
Offer with crusty bread to soak up the juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of dry Spanish red wine or sangria.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: a pinch (approx. 0.1g), steeped in 60ml warm water

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Red Bliss)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide, shallow pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking them down with a spoon.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to coat rice grains with the mixture.
Pour in warm chicken broth and saffron liquid. Stir well. Add diced potatoes.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid. Stir in frozen green peas. If rice is too dry, add a little more broth.
Cook uncovered for another 5 minutes, allowing any excess liquid to evaporate and peas to warm through.
Remove from heat. Let the dish rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Using a short-grain rice like Bomba rice will yield the best texture for absorbing flavors.
Adjust chili (bell pepper) for heat preference; a pinch of red pepper flakes can be added for more spice.
Ensure the pan is wide enough for the rice to cook evenly in a thin layer.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Garden Chicken with Savory Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, showcasing a single, artfully arranged individual portion. At the center, a bed of fluffy, light brown rice forms the foundation. Spooned generously over the rice are substantial chunks of golden-seared chicken, interspersed with vibrant, rustic cuts of fermented red and green bell peppers, diced tomatoes, and tender onion. The sauce offers a rich reddish-brown hue with flecks of bright vegetable colors, highlighting the natural textures. A scattering of finely grated Pecorino cheese lightly dusts the top, adding a subtle visual contrast. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space around the food, emphasizing its organic beauty. The scene is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin and a single piece of traditional flatware. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, enhancing its wholesome and inviting appearance.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3cm chunks
hard cheese (e.g., Pecorino or Parmesan), finely grated
Trimmings from onions, bell peppers, tomato ends, garlic skins (for optional broth)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Vegetables (3-5 days in advance): In a clean 1-liter jar, combine diced tomatoes, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, chopped small onion, and minced garlic. Dissolve sea salt in filtered water to create a brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small plate to keep vegetables under brine. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tangy flavor is achieved. Burp daily if not using an airlock. Store in refrigerator after fermentation.

Make Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth (optional): Combine all vegetable trimmings with 1 litre water in a pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes. Strain and discard solids.

Cook Rice: Rinse brown rice. In a medium pot, combine rice and 450ml vegetable broth (or water). Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Cook Chicken: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken in a single layer. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Prepare Sauce: Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced large onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Combine Dish: Add the fermented vegetables (drained, reserve brine) to the skillet with onions and garlic. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing some of the tomatoes slightly to create a rustic sauce. Add 60ml of the reserved fermentation brine for extra tang and depth. Stir in cooked chicken. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat through.
Serve: Divide cooked brown rice among 4 plates. Spoon chicken and fermented vegetable sauce over rice. Garnish each serving with finely grated hard cheese.
notes: Fermentation time for vegetables can vary based on temperature and desired tanginess; taste daily. Ensure vegetables remain submerged to prevent mold.
To maximize zero-waste, save all vegetable trimmings (onion skins, garlic peels, bell pepper cores, tomato ends) to create a flavorful vegetable broth for cooking the rice or sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Banana, Apple, and Blueberry Salad with Cacao-Lime Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. Cooked green banana rounds, crisp apple cubes, and vibrant blueberries are generously scattered among fresh, dark green mixed greens. Thin slices of red onion and toasted pecan pieces add pops of color and texture. A light, glistening coating of cacao-lime vinaigrette unifies the components. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, with ingredients casually overlapping, creating an inviting, homely appearance. The plate is adequately filled, leaving some comfortable negative space. Warm, diffused light illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural colors and textures, reflecting a cozy, family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Peel green bananas. Slice into 5mm thick rounds.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add banana slices in a single layer. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden and tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool.
Core apples. Dice into 1cm cubes.
Toast pecans in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant. Chop coarsely.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45ml olive oil, lime juice, crushed cacao nibs, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using).
In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, cooked banana slices, diced apples, blueberries, thinly sliced red onion, and toasted pecans.
Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic beef and potato stew is presented in a deep, earthenware bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features generous chunks of tender, dark brown beef, nestled among soft, golden-yellow potato cubes, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and earthy brown quartered mushrooms. A rich, thick reddish-brown gravy coats all ingredients, with visible flecks of dried herbs. A light scattering of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The stew has a comforting, slightly irregular texture, reflecting home cooking. The bowl sits on a simple ceramic plate. A linen napkin and a sturdy spoon are casually placed beside it. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread.
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onion and carrots to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually stir in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add potato cubes and quartered mushrooms. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-40 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Zero-Waste Fermented Garlic Chicken Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of clear, golden chicken broth is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl of light cream or beige on a light bamboo surface. Tender, poached chicken chunks, 2 cm in size, are nestled among thinly sliced rounds of vibrant orange carrot, pale green celery, and white leek, visible through the translucent liquid. Thinly sliced fermented garlic pieces are subtly present. A delicate swirl of bright green herb oil, made from parsley stems, floats on the surface. A few fresh parsley leaves provide minimalist garnish. The composition is clean, with ample white space around the bowl. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a clean, uncluttered background and a hint of natural plant greenery.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Garlic: Ensure garlic is fermented. If not, ferment 1 whole head of peeled garlic cloves in a jar with 250 ml non-chlorinated water and 5 g non-iodized salt for 7-10 days at room temperature.

Make Chicken Broth: Place chicken carcass/bones, chopped carrot end, celery end, and green leek part in a large pot. Add 3 litres water, bay leaf, and peppercorns. Bring to a simmer. Skim foam. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 2-3 hours.
Strain Broth: Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Reserve broth.

Poach Chicken: Add chicken breasts to the hot strained broth. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let cool slightly. Shred or cut into 2 cm chunks.
Prepare Vegetables: Peel remaining carrot. Cut into thin 0.5 cm rounds. Cut remaining celery into thin 0.5 cm slices. Slice white leek part into thin 0.5 cm rounds.
Simmer Vegetables: Add prepared carrot, celery, and leek to the broth. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Add Fermented Garlic: Slice fermented garlic cloves thinly. Add to the simmering broth. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Make Herb Oil: Wash parsley or chives. Reserve a few leaves for garnish. Blend remaining herbs, including stems, with 50 ml olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil.
Season Soup: Season broth with sea salt to taste.
Assemble: Ladle hot broth and vegetables into bowls. Add shredded chicken chunks. Drizzle with herb oil. Garnish with reserved fresh herb leaves.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste. Use vegetable scraps for broth. Herb stems are repurposed for herb oil.
Fermentation adds complex flavor and aids preservation.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Raspberry Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single wedge of Lemon Raspberry Layer Cake is centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The slice reveals distinct layers: a light yellow, tender cake, a vibrant, glossy pink raspberry filling, and a creamy white lemon cream cheese frosting. The cake slice is tall and holds its shape, showcasing a moist crumb. A few fresh, plump red raspberries are artfully placed on top of the slice and beside it on the plate, along with a delicate sprinkle of finely grated lemon zest. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. In the background, the remaining whole cake, fully frosted and garnished with a few fresh raspberries, sits elegantly on a simple cake stand on a rustic wooden table. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver dessert fork are positioned beside the plate, completing the sophisticated yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 18 cm round cake pans. Line bottoms with parchment paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, and salt into a bowl. Whisk to combine.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in vanilla extract and lemon zest.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans.
Bake 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack. Cool completely.
Combine raspberries, sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, mashing berries, until mixture simmers.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 1 tablespoon water to form a slurry.
Stir cornstarch slurry into simmering raspberry mixture. Cook, stirring, until thickened, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Cool completely.
In a large bowl, beat softened cream cheese and softened butter until smooth.
Gradually add powdered sugar, beating until combined.
Mix in lemon zest, lemon juice, and vanilla extract. Beat until frosting is light and fluffy.
Place one cooled cake layer on a serving plate or cake stand.
Spread raspberry filling evenly over the first cake layer.
Place the second cake layer on top.
Frost the top and sides of the cake with lemon cream cheese frosting.
Chill cake for at least 30 minutes to set frosting before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Smoked Sausage Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cajun Smoked Sausage Jambalaya is presented in a white porcelain shallow bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The dish features fluffy, reddish-brown long-grain rice, generously interspersed with substantial chunks of browned smoked sausage, vibrant diced green, red, and yellow bell peppers, and tender diced onions and celery. The rich color comes from the seasoned tomatoes and browned ingredients. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley and sliced green onions provides a contrasting garnish, adding freshness and visual appeal. The jambalaya is moist and cohesive, not dry or clumpy. A cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, with a standard fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's hearty texture and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bottle of hot sauce on the side for individual customization.
Offer cornbread or French bread as an accompaniment.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add smoked sausage slices. Brown until crispy. Remove sausage from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Cajun seasoning. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes with their liquid and chicken broth. Add bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Stir in rice. Return browned sausage to the pot. Ensure sausage is submerged.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook 20-25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Discard bay leaf. Fluff jambalaya with a fork.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure the internal temperature of the smoked sausage reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety, though it is typically pre-cooked.
Adjust the amount of Cajun seasoning to achieve desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Spaghetti Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of spaghetti carbonara is presented in a deep, slightly imperfect, off-white ceramic bowl. The golden-yellow spaghetti is loosely coiled, coated generously with a creamy, rich, and emulsified sauce. Small, irregularly diced, crispy pieces of rendered guanciale are scattered throughout the pasta, providing a textural contrast. Specks of freshly ground black pepper are visible on the sauce and pasta. The dish is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple silver fork rests beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and natural, typical of a cozy kitchen. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a casual cloth napkin, emphasizing a homely family meal setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Pecorino Romano at the table for individual preference.
Enjoy as a hearty 'primo piatto' (first course) or a complete main course.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Dice the guanciale into small cubes.
Place guanciale in a cold large skillet. Cook over medium heat. Render fat until guanciale is crispy.
Remove crispy guanciale from skillet. Leave rendered fat in skillet.
In a medium bowl, whisk whole eggs, egg yolks, grated Pecorino Romano, and a generous amount of black pepper. Set aside.
Add spaghetti to boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 200ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain spaghetti. Immediately transfer spaghetti to the skillet with the guanciale fat.
Add a splash of reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss well to coat pasta.
Remove skillet from heat. Quickly pour the egg mixture over the pasta.
Toss vigorously and continuously. Add more reserved pasta water gradually until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms.
Stir in the crispy guanciale.
Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use authentic guanciale. If unavailable, high-quality pancetta can be used as a substitute.
Ensure the skillet is off the heat when adding the egg mixture to prevent the eggs from scrambling. The residual heat from the pasta and skillet will cook the sauce to a creamy consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper & Herb Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Bell Pepper & Herb Rice Salad is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl, typical of Italian home cooking. Vibrant diced yellow and red bell peppers are scattered among fluffy, white long-grain rice. Halved cherry tomatoes add bursts of deep red. Small, golden-brown diced chicken pieces are interspersed throughout. Finely diced red onion and fresh green basil and oregano leaves are visible, adding herbaceous freshness. The salad is casually mounded, with ingredients naturally overlapping and touching, creating an abundant, unpretentious feel. A light sheen from the olive oil dressing coats the ingredients. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple cloth napkin and unadorned flatware complete the homely scene. Lighting is warm and natural, from a kitchen window. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the comforting portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread or focaccia.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of light, dry white wine or sparkling water.
Often served as part of a larger family meal, alongside other antipasti or lighter dishes.
instructions: Rinse rice. Combine rice with 400ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, until water is absorbed. Remove from heat, keep covered 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Spread rice on a baking sheet to cool completely.

Dice chicken breast into 1.5 cm cubes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil. Cook chicken cubes 5-7 minutes, until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside to cool.
Dice red and yellow bell peppers into 1 cm pieces. Halve cherry tomatoes. Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, cooled chicken, diced bell peppers, halved cherry tomatoes, and diced red onion.
Add chopped fresh basil and fresh oregano to the salad.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Refrigerate salad 30 minutes for flavors to meld. Serve chilled.
notes: For best flavor, use fresh herbs.
Adjust dressing to your preference.
Salad can be prepared a few hours in advance.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: Golden pan-seared chicken breast, whole or in two thick pieces, positioned on a pristine white round plate. Earthy brown sautéed cremini mushroom slices are artfully scattered around. A rich, glossy Marsala wine sauce, deep amber, pools around the chicken, lightly coating it. Vibrant green fresh chopped Italian parsley garnishes the dish. Presented on a light wooden table with a crisp white linen napkin and silver flatware. A subtle glass of red wine in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights textures: crisp chicken surface, tender mushrooms, smooth shimmering sauce. Balanced composition with negative space, focusing on the refined single serving.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple buttered pasta or creamy polenta.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a dry red wine, such as a Chianti or Merlot.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Dredge chicken breasts lightly in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms to the same skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with Marsala wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Allow chicken to warm through in the sauce.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in cold butter until melted and incorporated (mantecare).
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use a good quality dry Marsala wine for best flavor, not cooking Marsala.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Salami and Smoked Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of baked rigatoni is presented in a deep, classic white porcelain bowl. The top crust is a rich golden-brown from the melted, bubbling smoked mozzarella and grated Parmesan. Below the crust, tender rigatoni tubes are coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce. Interspersed throughout are creamy pockets of white ricotta cheese and small, irregular diced pieces of reddish-pink Italian salami, offering textural contrast. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully scattered on top, providing a fresh aromatic garnish. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The dish is centrally placed on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s hearty appeal and rich colors, with a soft, blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
A glass of robust red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice onion and mince garlic. Dice salami into small cubes. Grate smoked mozzarella and Parmesan.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
Cook rigatoni in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
In a medium bowl, combine ricotta cheese, grated Parmesan, and egg. Mix until well combined. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooked rigatoni, tomato sauce, and diced salami. Toss to coat evenly.
Spoon half of the pasta mixture into a 20 cm x 30 cm baking dish. Dot with spoonfuls of the ricotta mixture. Sprinkle with half of the smoked mozzarella.
Top with the remaining pasta mixture. Dot with remaining ricotta. Sprinkle with remaining smoked mozzarella.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown on top.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef and Pork Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Cooked Beef and Pork Ragu with Pappardelle is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Wide, golden pappardelle noodles are loosely coiled, generously coated in the rich, deep reddish-brown ragu. Visible are large, tender chunks of braised beef and pork, nestled amongst the pasta, showcasing their succulent texture. A generous mound of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese crowns the dish, adding a snowy contrast. A few vibrant green leaves of fresh basil or parsley are placed artfully for a pop of color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white linen napkin, and a silver fork beside the plate, all under soft, natural lighting, creating a warm, inviting, and authentic Italian bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.
Offer with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Pat beef and pork dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown meat on all sides until deeply caramelized. Remove meat and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring often, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, milk, bay leaves, and rosemary sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Return browned meat to the pot. Ensure meat is mostly submerged. Cover and simmer on low heat for 3-4 hours. Meat should be fork-tender. Internal temperature of pork and beef should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove meat from pot. Discard bay leaves and rosemary sprigs. Shred or pull the meat into large tender chunks.
Return shredded meat to the sauce. Simmer uncovered for 20-30 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately with a generous grating of Parmigiano-Reggiano and fresh herbs.
notes: The longer the ragu simmers, the more complex and tender the flavors become.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Caramelized Onion Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Beef and Caramelized Onion Pilaf is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The pilaf forms a soft, organic mound at the center of the plate, with individual grains of basmati rice appearing distinct and fluffy, stained a warm, golden-amber hue from the spices and caramelized onions. Nestled within and resting atop the pilaf are several substantial, irregularly shaped chunks of seared beef, each with a rich, dark brown crust. Scattered over the pilaf and beef are vibrant green flecks of freshly chopped parsley. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. To the left of the plate, a polished metal fork and knife are neatly placed on a folded off-white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and warm colors, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or a simple cucumber and tomato salad.
Traditionally enjoyed with fresh flatbread or lavash.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are deeply caramelized and golden brown, about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add rinsed rice and beef broth. Stir gently to combine.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let pilaf rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Serve hot.
notes: Ensure beef is seared in batches to avoid overcrowding and steaming.
Caramelizing onions properly is key for flavor and color.
Do not stir the rice too much after adding liquid to prevent stickiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Harvest Chicken with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Harvest Chicken is presented on a clean, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, placed on a light bamboo table surface. A mound of earthy brown rice forms the base. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its skin visibly crispy and glistening with a dark, savory glaze, rests beside the rice. Scattered naturally around the plate are thin rounds of reddish-pink fermented radishes and delicate, bright orange julienned fermented carrots, adding vibrant color and texture. The confit garlic cloves are subtly integrated into the glaze, contributing to the rich hue of the chicken. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh green scallions, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is minimalistic and unforced, with ample negative space. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic textures and natural colors of the ingredients. An undyed linen napkin rests subtly to the side, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Radish & Carrot Pickles: Thinly slice radishes into rounds. Julienne carrots into thin strips. Pack vegetables tightly into a clean 1-liter glass jar. Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 liter filtered water to make a 2% brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar tightly. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp jar daily to release pressure. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Garlic Confit: Peel one head of garlic cloves. Place cloves in a small saucepan. Cover completely with 200ml olive oil. Simmer gently over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until garlic is very soft and lightly golden. Do not brown. Strain garlic from oil. Reserve both confit garlic and garlic oil separately.

Cook Brown Rice: Rinse 250g brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 625ml water and 5ml reserved garlic confit oil in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Prepare Chicken Glaze: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, honey (or maple syrup), rice vinegar, and grated fresh ginger. Mash half of the reserved confit garlic cloves and stir into the glaze mixture.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and black pepper. Heat 10ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Continue cooking for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).

Glaze Chicken: Remove chicken from skillet. Pour excess fat from skillet, leaving 1-2 tablespoons. Add the prepared glaze mixture to the skillet. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Return chicken to the skillet, turning to coat evenly with the glaze. Cook for 1-2 minutes until glaze thickens slightly and coats chicken.

Assemble Dish: Divide cooked brown rice among four plates. Place one glazed chicken thigh next to the rice. Arrange a portion of the fermented radish and carrot pickles alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro or scallions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Root Vegetables and Herb-Infused Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of pan-seared chicken, golden-brown and whole, rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. Beside it, a mound of fluffy, white basmati rice, its individual grains visible. A vibrant cluster of fermented root vegetables—diced carrots, parsnip, and celeriac—adds pops of natural color (pale orange, cream, light yellow) and varied textures, arranged organically. A delicate drizzle of bright green herb oil streaks across the plate, providing a subtle color contrast. The composition is minimalist, with ample white space on the plate, highlighting the pure beauty of each ingredient. The plate sits on a light reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin and a simple, natural element like a small stone or a dried seed pod are nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing natural textures.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Root Vegetables: Wash and peel carrots, parsnip, celeriac. Cut into 1cm cubes. Combine 500ml water and 15g sea salt for brine. Pack vegetables into a clean jar. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring full submersion. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy. Refrigerate.

Cook Rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. In a saucepan, combine rice and 500ml vegetable stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Herb Oil: Wash parsley and chives. Roughly chop leaves and stems. In a small blender, combine herbs and 30ml olive oil. Blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear oil, or use unstrained for more texture.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from pan, rest 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a portion of fluffy rice onto the center of each plate. Arrange one seared chicken breast beside the rice. Place a generous spoonful of fermented root vegetables next to the chicken. Drizzle herb oil sparingly around the plate. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Beef with Fermented Broccoli & Olive Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a minimalist, handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A single, thick, succulent chunk of roasted beef, with a rich sear and tender, rosy interior, anchors the composition. Beside it, a vibrant, smooth swirl of bright green pea puree provides striking contrast. Neatly arranged roasted broccoli florets, retaining natural shape and slight char, highlight their texture. A small mound of dark, chunky fermented broccoli and olive relish, showcasing finely diced stem and chopped olives, adds complex, briny notes. Ample negative space emphasizes the pure beauty and natural colors of each ingredient. A few delicate sprigs of fresh dill offer subtle, natural garnish. The setting is clean and uncluttered, with soft, natural lighting and an undyed linen napkin.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Relish (24-48 hours in advance): Separate broccoli florets from stem. Reserve florets. Peel and finely dice the broccoli stem. Mince 1 garlic clove. Roughly chop the pitted olives. In a clean, sterile jar, combine diced broccoli stem, chopped olives, and minced garlic.
Make Relish Brine: In a small saucepan, combine 100 ml filtered water, 50 ml apple cider vinegar, and 5 g sea salt. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Let cool completely to room temperature.

Start Fermentation: Pour the cooled brine over the broccoli stem, olives, and garlic in the jar. Ensure all ingredients are fully submerged. Seal the jar loosely with a lid or use an airlock. Place the jar at room temperature (18-24°C) for 24 to 48 hours. Bubbles indicate fermentation. Taste after 24 hours; it should be tangy and slightly effervescent. Once desired tanginess is achieved, refrigerate to slow fermentation.
Prepare Beef (on cooking day): Pat beef roast dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper on all sides.

Sear Beef: Preheat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef in the hot skillet. Sear on all sides until a deep brown crust forms, about 2-3 minutes per side.

Roast Beef: Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes for medium-rare, or until an internal temperature of 60-65°C is reached. Remove beef from the oven and transfer to a cutting board. Loosely tent with foil and let rest for at least 10 minutes.

Roast Broccoli Florets: While beef rests, toss the reserved broccoli florets with 10 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast in the same oven for 10-15 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Make Pea Puree: Bring a small pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add the frozen green peas and cook for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender. Drain immediately.

Blend Pea Puree: Transfer the cooked peas to a blender. Add the remaining 5 ml olive oil, the juice from 1/2 lemon, and 1 minced garlic clove. Blend until very smooth and creamy. If too thick, add a tablespoon of the pea cooking water. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble & Serve: Slice the rested beef into thick, individual chunks. Spoon a generous dollop of the vibrant pea puree onto each plate. Arrange the roasted broccoli florets neatly beside the puree. Place 1-2 beef chunks on the plate. Spoon a portion of the tangy fermented broccoli and olive relish over or beside the beef. Garnish with a few small sprigs of fresh dill or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Baked Ziti with Beef and Three Cheeses
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of Hearty Baked Ziti rests on a simple, round ceramic plate, just scooped from a well-loved rectangular ceramic baking dish. The dish showcases a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella and Parmesan cheese, with rich red tomato sauce and tender ziti pasta visible underneath. Specks of dried oregano are embedded in the sauce. The ground beef chunks are well-integrated into the pasta and sauce, adding a hearty texture. The pasta is not overly neat; it's a natural, comforting mound with components touching and overlapping. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered casually on top. The plate sits on a worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The background is minimal, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen setting, emphasizing the homely comfort of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish at the table
Offer with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Serve alongside a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook ziti pasta according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add ground beef. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, half of the shredded mozzarella, and half of the grated Parmesan. Mix well.
Add cooked ziti to the meat sauce. Stir to coat evenly.
Spread half of the pasta mixture into a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Spoon dollops of the ricotta mixture over the pasta layer.
Cover with the remaining pasta mixture.
Sprinkle remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Bell Pepper Savory Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous rectangular portion of Sausage and Bell Pepper Savory Bake is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The top crust is golden-brown and slightly crispy, revealing tender, custard-soaked bread cubes beneath. Irregular, browned chunks of savory sausage are interspersed throughout, alongside vibrant, tender-crisp strips of red and yellow bell peppers and softened onion. The dish has a balanced composition, showcasing the rich colors and varied textures. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final touch of freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet inviting restaurant-style visual.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.

Remove sausage from casings. Break into small chunks. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from skillet.
Cut bread into 2.5 cm cubes. Set aside.
Cut bell peppers into thick 2 cm strips. Slice onion thinly. Mince garlic.
Add bell peppers and onion to the same skillet. Cook over medium heat until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, broth, half of the Parmesan cheese, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Add cooked sausage, sautéed bell peppers, onion, and bread cubes to the baking dish. Toss gently to combine.
Pour egg mixture evenly over the sausage and bread mixture. Press down gently to ensure all bread is moistened. Let stand for 15 minutes to allow bread to soak.
Bake for 30 minutes. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese over the top. Continue baking for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and the center is set.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the bake with fresh parsley before serving.
Let the bake rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Chicken Breast with Peas, Carrots, and Gruyere
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared stuffed chicken breast, cut diagonally into two thick, inviting pieces, is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The golden-brown seared exterior of the chicken contrasts with the vibrant, colorful filling visible at the cut edge. Inside, small diced bright orange carrots and plump green peas are nestled amongst melted, creamy Gruyere cheese. The chicken is moist and tender. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered around the base of the chicken for a touch of fresh green. The plate is positioned centrally on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting, allowing the dish to be the sole focus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Prepare chicken: Carefully slice each chicken breast horizontally almost all the way through. Open like a book. Cover with plastic wrap. Pound to an even thickness, about 1 cm.

Prepare vegetables: Dice carrots into small cubes (brunoise). Blanch diced carrots in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Add green peas for the last 30 seconds. Drain vegetables well. Immediately plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again thoroughly.
Make filling: Melt butter in a medium pan over medium heat. Sauté diced shallot until soft, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Combine filling: Remove pan from heat. Add blanched carrots and peas to the pan. Stir in shredded Gruyere cheese, chopped fresh parsley, salt, and black pepper. Mix well to combine.
Stuff chicken: Spoon an equal amount of filling onto one half of each pounded chicken breast. Fold the other half of the chicken breast over the filling. Secure the edges with toothpicks.
Sear chicken: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Carefully place stuffed chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Bake chicken: Transfer the skillet with the chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).

Rest and serve: Remove chicken from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes before slicing. Remove toothpicks. Slice each chicken breast diagonally into two thick pieces. Arrange on individual plates and serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and succulent, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly seared crust. A rich, creamy Dijon sauce, glistening with a pale yellow hue, is elegantly spooned around the base of the chicken, creating a delicate pool. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley provides a vibrant green contrast and a fresh aroma. The dish is garnished simply, allowing the quality of the ingredients to shine. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft, blurred background maintaining focus on the food.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallot. Sauté 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 2-3 minutes. Do not boil vigorously.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat through 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Mushroom Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two pan-seared pork medallions, each about 2.5 cm thick, are centrally placed, slightly overlapping. They exhibit a beautiful golden-brown crust with a hint of pink interior, indicating tender doneness. A luscious, creamy mushroom sauce generously coats the medallions and pools around them. The sauce is a rich, warm beige color, flecked with darker brown mushroom slices and bright green chopped parsley. The mushrooms are tender and slightly caramelized. A few vibrant green parsley sprigs are delicately placed on top for garnish. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting. Moderate negative space surrounds the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted small potatoes or creamy mashed potatoes.
Accompany with blanched green beans or asparagus.
Offer a crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Pat pork medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F).
Remove pork from skillet. Set aside. Keep warm.
Add butter to the same skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Add diced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Pour in chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer.
Cook 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return pork medallions to the skillet. Coat with sauce.
Taste sauce. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Allow pork to rest for a few minutes after cooking for maximum juiciness.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for thicker or adding more stock for thinner.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Mexican Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of One-Pan Mexican Chicken and Rice is presented on a rustic, terracotta-colored ceramic plate, centered on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features tender, browned chicken chunks nestled among fluffy, vibrant orange-red rice, plump black beans, and visible pieces of diced tomato. The rice is infused with chili and garlic. A generous layer of melted, golden-brown shredded cheddar cheese covers the top, with some bubbling edges. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is scattered over the cheese. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their rustic preparation. The plate is adequately filled but not overflowing, leaving some negative space. A small stack of warm corn tortillas rests beside the plate. A simple, unbleached cloth napkin is casually placed near the plate. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Provide a side of salsa or guacamole.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Heat oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Deseed and dice jalapeño.
Add onion, garlic, and jalapeño to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in rice and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and diced tomatoes with their juice. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the skillet. Stir gently.
Cover skillet tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 20 minutes, or until rice is almost tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken should reach 75°C internal temperature.
Rinse and drain black beans. Stir beans into the rice mixture.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top.
Return skillet to the oven. Bake uncovered for 5-10 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Chop fresh cilantro.
Garnish with chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
For best results, use an oven-safe skillet with a tight-fitting lid.
Adjust cayenne pepper to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef with Fermented Potato Purée and Crispy Root Vegetable Skins
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a muted cream tone, set against a light bamboo table surface. A single, substantial chunk of slow-cooked beef, boasting a rich, dark brown exterior from searing and a tender, yielding interior, is placed slightly off-center. Beside it, a generous, free-flowing pool of creamy, pale yellow fermented potato purée spreads naturally across the plate, its smooth texture contrasting with the beef. A light drizzle of glossy, reduced beef braising liquid cascades over the beef and pools around the purée. Scattered artfully atop the purée and beef are golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy root vegetable skins—thin, delicate shards offering a textural counterpoint. A small, vibrant sprig of fresh rosemary or thyme rests gently on the beef, providing a touch of green. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. A simple, undyed linen napkin and perhaps a subtly textured ceramic water glass complete the eco-conscious setting. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the organic textures and earthy colors of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Whey or Brine from a previous ferment (optional for faster ferment)
ingredients.quantity: 50 ml (or 1 tsp salt dissolved in 50ml water for a simple lacto-ferment)

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef.
Add chopped onion, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme to the Dutch oven. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.

Return beef to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 3-4 hours, or until beef is very tender and easily shredded with a fork. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While beef cooks, prepare potato purée. Cut peeled potatoes into large chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 20 minutes. Drain well.

Mash potatoes with butter until smooth. Stir in whey or salt solution. Cover loosely and let sit at room temperature for 12-24 hours for a subtle ferment, or use immediately if preferred (will be less tangy).
Prepare crispy root vegetable skins. Thoroughly wash and pat dry reserved carrot, parsnip, and celery root peels. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread peels in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Once beef is cooked, remove from pot. Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Reduce liquid over high heat until slightly thickened, if desired, for a richer sauce.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of fermented potato purée onto each plate. Place a slow-cooked beef chunk beside it. Drizzle with reduced braising liquid. Top with crispy root vegetable skins.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of creamy chicken and broccoli pasta sits on an everyday ceramic plate. The pasta, likely penne or fettuccine, is coated in a rich, off-white Alfredo sauce. Scattered throughout are tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (about 2 cm cubes) and vibrant green broccoli florets. The components naturally touch and overlap, creating a comforting, unpretentious mound. A light sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a touch of color and freshness on top. A dusting of grated Parmesan cheese is visible. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table. The background is minimally cluttered, showing hints of a relaxed family dining area with warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed beside the plate. Standard, simple metal flatware (fork) is laid beside the dish. The portion is a standard, satisfying home-style serving, not oversized. The scene is homely and inviting, focusing entirely on the comforting appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side salad.
Serve with warm garlic bread.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Reserve 120 ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 6-8 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add broccoli florets to the same pan. If needed, add a splash of water. Cover. Steam until tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes. Remove broccoli. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Once melted, add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Gradually whisk in Parmesan cheese until smooth and melted. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Return cooked chicken and broccoli to the pan with the sauce. Add cooked pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Cheesy Chicken, Potato, and Rice Bake
