Deglaze skillet with chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Reduce stock by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in cold butter, one cube at a time, until sauce is emulsified and glossy.
Stir in fresh lemon juice from one lemon and chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken breasts whole, alongside roasted asparagus. Spoon lemon-herb sauce generously over chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Manicotti Ripieni con Spinaci e Friarielli
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown baked manicotti tubes, generously filled, nestled in a vibrant, rich tomato passata. Each tube is plump, revealing creamy ricotta and vibrant green wilted spinach within. Tender, slightly charred florets of blanched broccoli rabe are arranged alongside, with deep red sun-dried tomato pieces and dark, briny olive slivers peeking through. The top is lightly crusted with melted, bubbly Pecorino Romano cheese. Fresh basil leaves provide bright green contrast. The dish is presented as a single portion on a rustic white ceramic plate, hinting at Italian countryside charm. A simple fork and a folded linen napkin are placed to the side. Natural light highlights the varied textures, from the soft pasta to the tender-crisp broccoli rabe.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread (pane casareccio) for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained and chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli rabe for 2-3 minutes. Drain and immediately transfer to an ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato passata. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, wilt spinach in a separate pan with a splash of water or olive oil. Squeeze out all excess liquid. Chop finely.
In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, chopped spinach, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, chopped olives, and 50 g grated Pecorino Romano. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Cook manicotti tubes in boiling salted water for 5-7 minutes. They should be al dente, not fully cooked. Drain carefully and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of a 23x33 cm (9x13 inch) baking dish.
Carefully stuff each manicotti tube with the ricotta mixture using a spoon or piping bag. Arrange stuffed manicotti in a single layer in the baking dish.
Pour remaining tomato sauce evenly over the manicotti. Arrange chopped broccoli rabe florets around and over the manicotti.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g Pecorino Romano over the top.
Cover baking dish with foil. Bake for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is golden and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil before serving.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality ricotta cheese.
Ensure spinach and broccoli rabe are thoroughly drained to prevent a watery filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Penne alla Vodka with Seared Prawns
recipes.visual_description: Penne pasta, al dente, is generously coated in a vibrant pink-orange vodka sauce. The sauce is creamy and rich, with subtle specks of finely diced tomato and fresh green basil visible throughout. Four large, plump prawns, perfectly seared to a golden-pink hue, are arranged naturally atop the pasta, showcasing their tender texture. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves and a generous dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese add complementary color and texture. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits neatly beside the pasta. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered on a light wooden table. A simple white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware accompany the plate, creating a professional yet approachable setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer additional grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Cook penne pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente according to package directions. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in vodka. Increase heat to medium-high. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes, allowing alcohol to evaporate.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream. Season sauce with salt and black pepper.
In a separate pan, heat remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Add prawns. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Season with salt and pepper.
Add drained penne to the vodka sauce. Add reserved pasta water as needed to reach desired consistency. Toss to coat evenly.
Stir in most of the chopped fresh basil.
Serve pasta immediately onto individual plates. Arrange seared prawns on top of the pasta.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil, grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Mediterranean Chicken Thighs with Herbed Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are artfully arranged, rustic chunks of roasted golden potatoes and vibrant orange butternut squash, each with slightly caramelized edges. Halved roasted cherry tomatoes, bursting with color, and tender, slightly charred red onion wedges are interspersed among the vegetables. A light, savory pan sauce is drizzled sparingly over the chicken and vegetables, catching the light. Fresh sprigs of green rosemary and thyme are thoughtfully placed as a simple, aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, all bathed in natural, even lighting to highlight the dish's textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices
A simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large oven-safe skillet or roasting pan, heat 30ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear for 2 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pan. Add potatoes, butternut squash, red onion, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in an even layer in the pan. Nest the seared chicken thighs among the vegetables, skin-side up.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized. Rotate pan halfway through.
Remove chicken and vegetables to a platter. Cover loosely with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth and white wine (if using) to the pan. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid slightly, about 2-3 minutes, to create a light pan sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning for the sauce.
Serve chicken and vegetables immediately, drizzled with pan sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Umami Beef Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of a Sustainable Umami Beef Bowl is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy beige finish, resting on a light, reclaimed wood table. The base is a mound of fluffy, wholesome brown rice. Scattered over the rice are irregular, savory seared beef chunks, deeply browned and glistening. Adjacent are tender, golden-brown sautéed cremini mushroom slices and vibrant green whole peas, providing contrasting textures and colors. A delicate drizzle of dark, glossy mushroom umami reduction subtly pools around the ingredients. A small, vibrant cluster of pink pickled red onion rings adds a bright pop of color and visual interest to one side. The overall composition is minimalistic and uncrowded, emphasizing natural textures and the pure beauty of each ingredient. A simple undyed linen napkin and a single piece of minimalist cutlery are beside the bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a hint of green foliage from a background plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple, clear vegetable broth to complement the savory notes
Accompany with small portions of seasonal, lightly steamed greens for added freshness
instructions: Prepare pickled red onions: Thinly slice red onion into rings. In a small pot, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over onion slices in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. The longer it sits, the more pickled it becomes.

Cook brown rice: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 400 ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Prepare mushrooms: Separate mushroom caps from stems. Thinly slice mushroom caps. Roughly chop mushroom stems. Mince garlic.

Make mushroom umami reduction: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped mushroom stems and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and fragrant. Add 100 ml water. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Blend the mixture until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed to reach a pourable consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Cook green peas: If using fresh peas, blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. If using frozen peas, boil for 1-2 minutes until heated through. Drain immediately and refresh in cold water to retain bright green color. Set aside.

Cook beef: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add beef chunks. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until deeply browned and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Add Worcestershire sauce during the last minute of cooking, tossing to coat. Remove beef from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
Sauté mushrooms: In the same pan, add sliced mushroom caps. Sauté over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among 4 serving bowls. Arrange beef chunks, sautéed mushrooms, and green peas artfully on top of the rice. Place a generous portion of pickled red onions on the side. Drizzle mushroom umami reduction over the beef and mushrooms. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing mushroom stems for a flavorful umami reduction. Consider composting any vegetable trimmings.
Prioritize locally sourced and seasonal ingredients when possible to enhance sustainability and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Salad with Dill
recipes.visual_description: A classic American Potato Salad is presented in a deep, everyday ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The diced potatoes are coated generously in a creamy, pale yellow mayonnaise-based dressing, showing their soft, cooked texture. Finely chopped celery and thinly sliced red onion pieces are visibly mixed throughout, adding subtle green and purple color notes. The salad is casually mounded, allowing some components to naturally overlap. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped dill is scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and herbaceous aroma. A simple stainless steel serving spoon rests beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, mimicking natural kitchen light, highlighting the comforting, homestyle appeal of the dish. A casually folded cloth napkin and a water glass are subtly visible in the background, completing the unpretentious family meal setting.
instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm dice.
Place diced potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add 5 grams of salt.
Bring water to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium. Simmer until potatoes are tender when pierced with a fork, about 10-15 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly in a colander. Let them cool completely.
While potatoes cool, finely chop celery stalks. Thinly slice the red onion.
Finely chop fresh dill.
In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and apple cider vinegar. Season with 2 grams of black pepper.
Add cooled potatoes, chopped celery, and sliced red onion to the dressing bowl. Gently fold to combine.
Stir in chopped fresh dill.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt or pepper if needed.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. This allows flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Mole Poblano served on a clean white porcelain plate. The centerpiece is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh completely coated in a thick, velvety, dark reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce appears glossy and rich with visible texture from ground seeds and spices. Toasted white sesame seeds are sprinkled evenly over the chicken. Three small sprigs of fresh cilantro and four thin rings of raw red onion provide a vibrant color contrast. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy Mexican red rice is positioned. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small basket of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a colorful woven cloth and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas served in a traditional cloth-lined basket
Mexican red rice (arroz rojo)
Refried beans topped with crumbled queso fresco
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from all dried chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl of hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Toast almonds, 15g of sesame seeds, and the cinnamon stick in a dry pan until golden.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic in a dry pan until blackened in spots.
Drain chilies and place in a blender with toasted nuts, spices, and charred vegetables.
Add 100ml of chicken stock and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil in a large pot. Add the mole paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the remaining chicken stock and chopped dark chocolate. Simmer on low heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear in a separate pan until the skin is golden brown.
Transfer chicken to the mole sauce. Simmer until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Adjust seasoning with salt if necessary.
notes: Do not burn the chilies during toasting or the sauce will become bitter.
The mole sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C at the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Ragout with Raspberry Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty Beef and Mushroom Ragout is presented in an everyday, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The ragout is rich, dark brown, filled with tender, irregularly cut chunks of braised beef and quartered, browned cremini mushrooms. Bright, softened raspberries are visible, adding a subtle crimson hue. The thick sauce coats ingredients generously. A small mound of creamy mashed potatoes is nestled beside the ragout, allowing sauce to pool naturally. A fresh sprig of thyme rests casually on top. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm cubes

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf from the ragout.
Add raspberries to the ragout. Simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes, allowing raspberries to break down and the sauce to thicken slightly. Gently mash some raspberries with a spoon.
If a thicker sauce is desired, mix cornstarch with water to form a slurry. Stir into the ragout. Simmer until thickened.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
notes: Serve hot with mashed potatoes, polenta, or wide pasta like pappardelle.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage and Root Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with an earthy, matte finish. Thinly sliced green and red cabbage form the base, interspersed with vibrant julienned carrots, translucent, thinly sliced beetroot, and crisp, thinly sliced radishes. Cooked chickpeas are scattered throughout, adding a textural contrast. The ingredients are arranged naturally, allowing their individual colors and textures to shine, with ample negative space around the components. A light miso dressing gently coats the vegetables, visible as a subtle sheen. Toasted pumpkin seeds are sprinkled on top, alongside a few fresh dill sprigs for a touch of green. The overall composition is clean and unforced, emphasizing the natural beauty of each ingredient. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is minimalist, with subtle hints of blurred green foliage from a houseplant, maintaining an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light main course or a substantial side dish.
instructions: Thinly slice both green and red cabbage. Place in a large bowl.
Julienne carrots. Thinly slice beetroot. Thinly slice radishes. Add to the cabbage.
Rinse and drain chickpeas. Add to the vegetable mixture.
In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated ginger, and water until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over vegetables and chickpeas. Toss gently to combine.
Sprinkle with pumpkin seeds and chopped fresh dill before serving.
notes: For enhanced sustainability, consider fermenting your own cabbage (sauerkraut) in advance. This recipe uses the concept of 'fermented' by having a dressing with miso, a fermented product.
Utilize vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, beetroot tops) for homemade vegetable stock or compost them to minimize waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuna and Spinach Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy tuna and spinach pasta is casually swirled onto a round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The pasta, likely fusilli or penne, is coated in a light, creamy, almost translucent sauce. Flakes of pale pinkish-grey tuna are visibly distributed throughout the pasta. Vibrant green, roughly chopped spinach leaves are intertwined, adding pops of color. Small, golden-brown diced onion pieces are interspersed, along with flecks of fresh, bright green parsley. The overall appearance is hearty and comforting, with a slightly rustic, homemade feel. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple metal fork rests beside the plate, and a casually crumpled cloth napkin is nearby. The background is minimal, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen setting.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in olive oil, drained

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 120 ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, dice the onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Flake the drained tuna into the pan. Stir gently to combine.
In a small bowl, whisk together Greek yogurt and 60 ml of the reserved pasta water. This creates a smooth sauce.
Add the cooked pasta to the pan with tuna and vegetables. Pour the yogurt sauce over. Toss gently to coat.
If the sauce is too thick, add more reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley and lemon zest.
Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The foundation is a bed of broad, al dente pappardelle ribbons thoroughly coated in a vibrant, chunky tomato sauce. Three large, succulent chunks of seared chicken thigh are nestled atop the pasta, displaying a rich, golden-brown caramelized crust. Visible within the sauce are softened julienned onions and whole, blistered cherry tomatoes. Small flecks of fresh rosemary and cracked black pepper garnish the dish. The plating is clean with moderate negative space around the rim. It sits on a dark wood bistro table with a neutral linen napkin and polished silver fork under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty ciabatta bread to mop up the sauce.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
Provide a small bowl of freshly grated Pecorino Romano for dusting.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, cut into 5cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides.
Remove chicken from the skillet and set aside.
Add remaining olive oil and julienned onion to the same skillet.
Sauté onion 6 minutes until softened and translucent.
Stir in minced garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine and scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Add crushed tomatoes, cherry tomatoes, and chicken stock.
Return chicken to the skillet and submerge in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil pappardelle in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 60ml of cooking water.
Toss pasta with the sauce and reserved water over low heat until glossy.
Serve immediately.
notes: Using San Marzano tomatoes provides the authentic sweetness required for this sauce.
Ensure the pasta is tossed in the sauce for one minute to achieve the perfect mantecatura consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken thigh rests centrally on an off-white ceramic plate. The chicken, golden-brown from searing, is a whole piece, not sliced. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. Sliced cremini mushrooms and small, finely diced onion pieces are clearly visible within the thick, flowing sauce, which pools gently around the chicken. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, with a simple fork and knife placed casually beside it. A folded cloth napkin adds to the relaxed, homely atmosphere. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the food. The background is minimal, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Mashed potatoes
Steamed green beans
Plain rice
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Add diced onion and minced garlic. Cook 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 5 minutes, or until sauce thickens slightly.
Return cooked chicken thighs to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat through 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust sauce thickness by simmering longer for a thicker sauce, or adding a touch more broth for a thinner consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Black Bean Taco Salad
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Mushroom and Black Bean Taco Salad is presented on an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, centered on a well-used wooden dining table. The salad features a generous bed of chopped romaine lettuce, topped with a vibrant mix of ingredients. Sautéed sliced mushrooms, dark black beans, bright red halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion are casually arranged. Shredded yellow cheddar cheese is sprinkled throughout, with golden, crispy tortilla strips placed artfully on top. The colors are natural and inviting. The components are mixed but distinct, showing varied textures. Warm, soft light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene. A simple cloth napkin and a small bottle of hot sauce rest nearby, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges.
Offer a side of your favorite salsa or guacamole.
Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and tender, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool.
While mushrooms cook, preheat oven to 180°C. Spread tortilla strips on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy. Let cool.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, chopped coriander, yogurt/sour cream, garlic powder, and cumin. Season the dressing with salt and pepper.
In a large salad bowl, combine chopped romaine lettuce, rinsed black beans, halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion.
Add the cooled cooked mushrooms and shredded cheddar cheese to the salad bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Divide the salad among four plates. Top each portion with crispy tortilla strips just before serving.
notes: For extra heat, add a pinch of chili powder to the mushroom seasoning.
Adjust dressing consistency by adding a splash of water if too thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Katsu with Japanese Potato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, oblong white porcelain plate. Golden-crisp chicken katsu, cut into thick, diagonal strips, is arranged neatly on one side. The panko breading is visibly crunchy, a deep golden brown. Adjacent to the katsu, a generous scoop of Japanese potato salad rests. It is creamy, with visible chunks of potato, finely diced cucumber, carrot, and onion, showing subtle color variations. A mound of finely shredded green cabbage sits alongside the chicken, providing a fresh, crisp contrast. A dark, glossy drizzle of Tonkatsu sauce is artfully applied over the chicken. The overall palette is warm golden browns, creamy whites, and vibrant greens, with the dark sauce providing depth. Textures are a mix of crunchy, creamy, and crisp. The plate is centered on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a set of traditional Japanese chopsticks are placed to the side. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a clean, inviting restaurant atmosphere. This is a single, refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional Tonkatsu sauce on the side
Accompanied by a small bowl of steamed short-grain rice
Often served with a side of miso soup
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well and mash roughly. Do not over-mash.
Finely dice cucumber, carrot, and onion. For the onion, you may rinse briefly under cold water to reduce pungency, then pat dry.

In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, diced cucumber, carrot, and onion. Add Japanese mayonnaise, rice vinegar, sugar, salt, and black pepper. Mix gently until combined. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Place each chicken thigh between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound with a meat mallet to an even 1.5cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with panko breadcrumbs. Dredge each chicken thigh in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg to coat completely. Press firmly into panko until fully coated.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 170°C. Carefully lower one or two chicken thighs into the hot oil. Fry for 5-7 minutes per side, or until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Remove chicken katsu from oil. Place on a wire rack over paper towels to drain excess oil. Repeat with remaining chicken.
Slice each cooked chicken katsu into thick, diagonal strips, approximately 2-3cm wide. Do not fan out the slices.
Finely shred the green cabbage.

To serve, arrange sliced chicken katsu on one side of each plate. Place a generous scoop of Japanese potato salad next to the katsu. Pile shredded cabbage on the plate. Drizzle Tonkatsu sauce over the chicken katsu.
notes: For best flavor, use authentic Japanese mayonnaise (Kewpie brand).
Ensure oil temperature is consistent for even frying to achieve a crisp crust and cooked interior.
traditional_techniques: Mise en place for efficient preparation

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Cherry Panna Cotta
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant serving of chocolate cherry panna cotta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The panna cotta, unmolded and standing upright, is a smooth, glossy cylinder of deep, rich chocolate brown. Its surface is perfectly unblemished, showcasing a refined texture. Beside it, a vibrant, ruby-red cherry compote is spooned with a natural, flowing arrangement, featuring softened cherry pieces. The contrast between the dark panna cotta and the bright compote is striking. A fresh, bright green mint sprig is delicately placed on the plate, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro setting. Standard silver flatware is placed neatly beside the plate, and a folded cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, casually blurred restaurant-style background, maintaining a professional yet approachable atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, emphasizing the dish as the focal point without overcrowding.
instructions: Soak gelatine sheets in cold water for 5 minutes until softened. Squeeze out excess water.
In a saucepan, combine milk, 70 g sugar, and cocoa powder. Whisk well.
Heat over medium heat, stirring, until sugar dissolves and mixture is hot but not boiling.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla extract and squeezed gelatine until fully dissolved.
Pour mixture into four 150 ml molds or ramekins. Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until set.
For the cherry compote, combine pitted cherries, remaining 30 g sugar, 50 ml water, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes until cherries soften.
In a small bowl, mix cornstarch with 1 tablespoon cold water to create a slurry.
Pour cornstarch slurry into simmering cherries. Stir constantly until compote thickens. Remove from heat and cool.
To serve, briefly dip the bottom of each mold in hot water. Invert panna cotta onto individual clean white porcelain plates.
Spoon cherry compote around the base or artfully over a portion of each panna cotta.
Garnish each plate with a fresh mint sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Ukrainian Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A rustic yet refined Ukrainian Chicken and Vegetable Stew, presented in a deep, matte white ceramic bowl. The stew features tender, 3cm chunks of braised chicken, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, diced tomatoes, and tender onion, all enveloped in a rich, reddish-brown gravy. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped dill and parsley garnishes the top. Alongside the stew, on the same plate, are golden-brown roasted potato wedges, slightly crispy on the exterior and fluffy inside. A small side salad of crisp mixed greens, lightly dressed with a lemon vinaigrette, and adorned with quartered hard-boiled egg, completes the presentation. The dish is set on a simple, light wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece of a casual, authentic Ukrainian meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of smetana (sour cream) on top of the stew.
Accompany with fresh dark rye bread for dipping.
Garnish generously with extra fresh dill and parsley.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken chunks on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Dice onion. Slice bell peppers into thin strips. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Sauté onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add bell pepper strips and minced garlic. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in tomato paste and sweet paprika. Cook for 1 minute.

Return chicken to the pot. Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into wedges. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
Steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes.
Hard-boil the egg. Cool, peel, and quarter.
Prepare lemon vinaigrette: whisk juice of half a lemon with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Toss salad greens with lemon vinaigrette. Arrange on serving plates with quartered egg.
Stir chopped fresh dill and parsley into the stew just before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve the stew in deep bowls. Arrange roasted potato wedges alongside. Serve with the fresh side salad.
notes: This stew often tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz Rojo con Cerdo y Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Arroz Rojo con Cerdo y Pollo is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, cooked to a tender, slightly firm texture, displays a rich reddish-orange hue, forming a cohesive base. Scattered generously over the rice are succulent, browned chunks of pan-seared pork shoulder and thick pieces of seared chicken breast. The meats are tender with a slight char on their edges. Bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro is sprinkled over the entire dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. A single lime wedge rests beside the main mound of food. The dish is centrally placed on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a small, rustic ceramic bowl containing a vibrant salsa roja, suggesting traditional Mexican accompaniments. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing colors and textures, with moderate negative space on the plate and a minimal, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of salsa roja or pico de gallo.
Serve with sliced avocado.
instructions: Rehydrate guajillo chiles in hot water for 20 minutes. Drain, deseed, and blend with a splash of fresh water to form a smooth paste.
Season pork and chicken cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Sear chicken cubes until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature during cooking or later.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried Mexican oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the guajillo chile paste and tomato paste. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the rice to the pot. Stir to coat the rice grains with the chili mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return the seared pork and chicken to the pot, nestling them into the rice.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C internal temperature. If not, continue cooking until safe.
For extra heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a chopped serrano chile to the onion-garlic sauté.
traditional_techniques: Preparing a chile paste from rehydrated dried chiles
Building a sofrito base with onion, garlic, and spices

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Gruyère Stuffing
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is golden-brown with a lightly crisp exterior. It is sliced diagonally in half to reveal the rich, creamy Gruyère and vibrant green spinach stuffing. A glossy, amber-hued pan sauce is spooned elegantly around the chicken. Garnish includes a fresh thyme sprig and a sprinkle of finely chopped parsley. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver flatware, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat a small pan with 5ml olive oil. Sauté diced shallot until translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add wilted, chopped spinach, chopped thyme, and chopped parsley. Cook briefly to combine. Remove from heat.
Transfer spinach mixture to a bowl. Mix with shredded Gruyère cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Using a sharp knife, carefully butterfly each chicken breast, creating a pocket.
Lightly pound chicken breasts to an even thickness if needed.
Divide cheese and spinach mixture evenly. Stuff into each chicken breast pocket. Secure opening with toothpicks if necessary.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 25ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add stuffed chicken breasts to the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, loosely tented with foil.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Remove from heat. Swirl in unsalted butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened.
Remove toothpicks from chicken breasts. Slice each breast diagonally in half.
Serve immediately with pan sauce spooned over.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after cooking helps keep it moist and tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Beef Bulgogi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Beef Bulgogi is artfully arranged on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The thinly sliced beef sirloin, seared to a beautiful caramelized brown with slight charring, forms a central, appealing mound. Each piece retains its delicate shape, glistening with the rich marinade. A generous scattering of vibrant green spring onion slices and toasted white sesame seeds provides a fresh, aromatic contrast. The beef's texture appears tender yet slightly chewy. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table, suggestive of a modern bistro. Beside the dish, a small, clean white rice bowl holds perfectly steamed white rice. Metal chopsticks rest neatly on a simple ceramic chopstick rest. A small side dish of bright red kimchi adds a pop of traditional color. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the focal point within an authentic Korean casual dining context.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer various banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi or pickled radishes.
Provide ssamjang (spicy dipping sauce) and fresh lettuce leaves for wrapping the beef.

ingredients.name: Spring onions, white parts thinly sliced
Spring onions, green parts sliced diagonally (for garnish)

instructions: Place the very thinly sliced beef into a large bowl.

In a separate bowl, combine soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, brown sugar, grated Asian pear, and the thinly sliced white parts of the spring onions. Add black pepper. Mix well to form the marinade.
Pour the marinade over the beef. Toss to coat all beef slices evenly. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours, for optimal flavor.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.

Add the marinated beef to the hot pan in batches. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook each batch for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently, until the beef is browned and cooked through. Remove cooked beef and set aside.
Repeat with remaining beef until all batches are cooked.
Transfer the cooked bulgogi to a serving plate. Garnish generously with the diagonally sliced green parts of spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
traditional_techniques: Marinating for tenderization and flavor infusion

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Forest Mushroom Ragout and Crispy Potato Medallions
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared boneless chicken thigh, golden-brown, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a rich, earthy forest mushroom ragout with thinly sliced mushrooms, diced red bell pepper, and carrots, is neatly spooned. The ragout shows warm brown and vibrant orange hues. Crispy, golden-yellow potato medallions, 5 mm thick, are arranged attractively. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the ragout and part of the chicken. Bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry white wine or still water.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Slice potatoes into 5 mm thick medallions. Rinse and pat dry thoroughly.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add potato medallions in a single layer. Cook 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Season with salt. Remove and set aside.
Dice onion, carrot, and bell pepper into 1 cm cubes. Slice mushrooms thinly. Mince garlic.

In the same skillet, add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside. Keep warm.
Add butter to the skillet. Sauté diced onion, carrot, and bell pepper for 5 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken broth and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10-12 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Remove thyme sprigs.
Season ragout with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Grate Parmesan cheese.

To serve, place a chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amount of mushroom ragout alongside. Arrange crispy potato medallions next to the chicken. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan and chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure potatoes are very dry before cooking for maximum crispiness.
Adjust seasoning of ragout to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown seared pork chop rests prominently on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chop exhibits a beautifully caramelized crust, indicating a perfect sear, and appears juicy. A rich, velvety cream sauce, studded with tender, earthy brown mushroom slices and flecks of fresh parsley, is elegantly spooned over and around the pork. Beside the chop, a neat bundle of vibrant green, tender-crisp roasted asparagus spears adds a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro setting. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting presentation. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and professional single serving.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer chops to a plate. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add finely diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Return pork chops to skillet with sauce. Spoon sauce over chops. Cook 2-3 minutes or until heated through.
Meanwhile, toss asparagus with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a preheated 200°C oven for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Garnish sauce with fresh chopped parsley. Serve pork chops immediately with mushroom cream sauce and roasted asparagus.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl. A mound of vibrant red-orange pasta, coated in a rich tomato sauce, forms the base. Two to three thick, golden-brown medallions of pan-seared chicken, displaying a slight char, are nestled on top. Chicken is not fanned. Bright green fresh parsley or basil flecks are scattered over, providing a pop of color. Finely grated pale yellow Parmesan and golden toasted breadcrumbs add texture. Thin lemon zest strands enhance aroma. Chicken is sliced into 1.5 cm thick medallions; onion is finely diced, garlic minced. The bowl rests on a light wooden table, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served as a 'primo' (first course) in a larger Italian meal, but often enjoyed as a main course.
Accompanied by crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 10ml olive oil in a medium pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken breast. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest 5 minutes. Slice chicken into 1.5 cm thick medallions.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 50ml pasta water.
In the same pan used for chicken, add 5ml olive oil and butter over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add reserved pasta water. Toss to combine.
Stir in half of the grated cheese and half of the chopped fresh herbs. Squeeze in 10ml lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small dry pan, toast breadcrumbs over medium heat until golden brown and crisp.
Transfer pasta to a shallow bowl. Arrange sliced chicken medallions on top. Garnish with remaining grated cheese, remaining fresh herbs, lemon zest, and toasted breadcrumbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Brown Rice is presented in a shallow, rustic white ceramic bowl with a wide rim, reflecting a modern bistro aesthetic. A golden-brown, crisply seared chicken thigh is positioned as the centerpiece, nestled into a vibrant bed of deeply colored brown rice. The rice, cooked to a tender, slightly firm texture, is infused with the rich hues of diced red and green bell peppers and sweet tomatoes, showing a mosaic of reds, greens, and golden brown. Minced garlic and onion are visible throughout the rice. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, providing a fresh contrast. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space around the rim. The bowl rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface, beside a folded white cotton napkin and a fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a softly blurred restaurant-style background maintaining focus on the food. The chicken is presented as a whole, succulent piece, not sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan if serving family-style.
Accompany with crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or paella pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deeply golden and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. If using, add saffron threads. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking down tomatoes with a spoon.
Add brown rice to the pan. Stir well to coat rice with the vegetable mixture. Toast for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken adds more flavor and keeps the chicken moist.
Adjust broth quantity if using a different type of rice, as cooking times and liquid absorption may vary.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Penne
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, single portion of Chicken Cacciatore is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic pasta bowl. One large, tender chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening with rich tomato sauce, rests prominently atop a generous bed of al dente penne pasta. The vibrant red sauce, infused with diced onions and substantial pieces of red and green bell peppers, coats the pasta and chicken. The sauce has a natural, slightly chunky texture. Fresh, roughly torn green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is natural and comforting, with components touching and overlapping in a homely, inviting manner. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a hearty, satisfying portion. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, with a simple cloth napkin casually placed beside the bowl and a traditional fork resting nearby, reflecting a relaxed, family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette makes a fresh accompaniment.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Montepulciano.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: small bunch, roughly torn, for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy. This takes about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper pieces to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through.
While chicken simmers, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve chicken cacciatore directly over the cooked pasta. Garnish each portion with fresh torn basil.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce benefits from a longer, slower simmer, allowing flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Beer-Braised Chicken with Cilantro Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chipotle Beer-Braised Chicken is plated on a round white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of fluffy white cilantro rice, bright with green flecks, cradles a whole, tender, rich brown chicken thigh. The chicken is generously coated in a deep reddish-brown chipotle-beer braising sauce, which pools invitingly around its base. A fresh lime wedge and a sprinkle of vibrant green cilantro leaves complete the dish. The presentation is professional yet approachable, with ample negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures. The entire plate is visible, presenting a balanced and appealing composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh salsa
Sliced avocado

ingredients.name: Chicken broth
ingredients.quantity: 1 litre (500 ml for braising, 500 ml for rice)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook chicken to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, minced chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer and hot sauce. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add 500 ml chicken broth. Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender.
While chicken braises, prepare cilantro rice. Rinse long-grain white rice until water runs clear.
Combine rinsed rice and 500 ml chicken broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover saucepan tightly. Simmer 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Stir chopped cilantro and fresh lime juice into the cooked rice.
Remove chicken from braising liquid. Shred chicken with two forks or keep whole. Skim excess fat from sauce if desired. Reduce sauce over high heat if too thin.
Serve braised chicken over a bed of cilantro rice. Spoon rich chipotle-beer sauce generously over chicken and rice.
Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge.
notes: This dish benefits from being made a day ahead, allowing flavors to deepen.
Adjust chipotle and hot sauce quantities to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Spanish Chicken and Rice with Potatoes is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, resting on a rustic wooden table. Golden-brown seared chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are placed atop a bed of saffron-infused short-grain rice. The rice is studded with diced ripe red tomatoes, small diced white potatoes, and bright green peas, creating a mosaic of colors and textures. Minced garlic and finely diced onions are subtly integrated into the rice. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, adding a pop of verdant green. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the rich colors and inviting textures. A simple white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, with a small, culturally authentic Spanish ceramic olive dish nearby, adding to the bistro-style setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan in the center of the table.
Offer with crusty bread to soak up the juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of dry Spanish red wine or sangria.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: a pinch (approx. 0.1g), steeped in 60ml warm water

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Red Bliss)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide, shallow pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking them down with a spoon.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to coat rice grains with the mixture.
Pour in warm chicken broth and saffron liquid. Stir well. Add diced potatoes.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid. Stir in frozen green peas. If rice is too dry, add a little more broth.
Cook uncovered for another 5 minutes, allowing any excess liquid to evaporate and peas to warm through.
Remove from heat. Let the dish rest, covered, for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Using a short-grain rice like Bomba rice will yield the best texture for absorbing flavors.
Adjust chili (bell pepper) for heat preference; a pinch of red pepper flakes can be added for more spice.
Ensure the pan is wide enough for the rice to cook evenly in a thin layer.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle Beer Braised Chicken with Cilantro Lime Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. At the center, a generous portion of fluffy, bright white cilantro lime rice forms a bed. Nestled atop the rice are two whole, deeply browned, fork-tender braised chicken thighs. The chicken glistens with a rich, dark mahogany sauce, showcasing its slow-cooked texture. Small flecks of minced chipotle and herbs are visible in the sauce. A vibrant lime wedge is placed beside the chicken, offering a pop of bright green and yellow. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro garnishes the chicken and rice, adding freshness and color contrast. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin, and a stack of warm corn tortillas in a traditional basket. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping up chicken and sauce.
Offer a side of fresh pico de gallo or a simple avocado salsa.
Serve with a Mexican lager or horchata.

ingredients.name: Chipotle chiles in adobo sauce, minced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in minced chipotle chiles and adobo sauce. Cook 30 seconds.
Pour in Mexican lager and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 45-60 minutes. Chicken should be fork-tender and reach 75°C internal temperature.
While chicken braises, prepare cilantro lime rice. Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear.
Combine rinsed rice with 500ml water and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed.
Remove rice from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Stir in chopped cilantro and juice of one lime.
Remove braised chicken from sauce. Shred chicken if desired, or leave whole.
Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, about 5-10 minutes.
Serve braised chicken over cilantro lime rice. Spoon rich sauce over chicken. Garnish with fresh lime wedges and extra cilantro. Offer hot sauce on the side.
notes: For best flavor, braise chicken a day ahead and reheat. Flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust chipotle quantity to preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Penne with Creamy Mushroom and Fontina Béchamel
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of baked penne pasta is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, showcasing a golden-brown, bubbly gratin top. The rich, creamy interior reveals tender, earthy sliced cremini mushrooms intertwined with al dente penne pasta, all coated in a luxurious, melted Fontina béchamel sauce. Scattered golden-brown bits of caramelized cheese add texture and color. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped Italian parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The dish sits on a simple, rustic light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver European flatware and a folded off-white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting warmth and inviting textures, with a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background suggesting a casual bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the creamy sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Cook penne pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 8-10 minutes. Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 20g butter to the same skillet. Add chopped shallot and minced garlic. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in fresh thyme. Remove from heat.
To make the béchamel, melt remaining 60g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in all-purpose flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm whole milk, a little at a time, until smooth. Continue whisking constantly until sauce thickens and comes to a gentle boil, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove béchamel from heat. Stir in grated nutmeg, salt, and black pepper to taste. Stir in Fontina cheese and half of the Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Add sautéed mushrooms and shallot-garlic mixture to the béchamel sauce. Stir to combine. Add cooked penne pasta to the sauce. Gently toss until all pasta is coated.
Transfer the pasta mixture to the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the top is golden brown. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a richer flavor, use a mix of wild mushrooms like shiitake or oyster alongside cremini.
Any short, tubular pasta like rigatoni or cavatappi can be substituted for penne.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Beef Short Ribs (Galbi Jim)
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Korean Braised Beef Short Ribs, known as Galbi Jim, presented in a traditional dark stoneware dolsot or a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. The beef short ribs are substantial, fork-tender chunks, coated in a glossy, dark mahogany braising liquid. Large 3 cm diced daikon and carrots, whole shiitake mushrooms, chestnuts, and dried jujubes are nestled among the beef, showing their distinct shapes and colors. The rich, thick sauce pools slightly at the bottom, reflecting light. The dish is generously garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds for contrast. The setting is a modern bistro table with a simple wooden surface. A small white porcelain rice bowl and a small ceramic dish of bright red kimchi sit beside the main bowl. Metal chopsticks rest neatly beside the dolsot. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, authentic Korean dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Accompany with various banchan (side dishes) like kimchi and pickled radishes.
Eat with metal chopsticks and a spoon.
instructions: Rinse beef short ribs under cold water. Soak ribs in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain water. Repeat soaking and draining two more times to remove excess blood.
Place soaked ribs in a large pot. Cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil over high heat. Boil for 10 minutes. Skim off any foam. Drain ribs and rinse thoroughly under cold water.
Cut daikon radish and carrots into large 3 cm chunks. Remove stems from shiitake mushrooms. Leave small mushrooms whole, halve larger ones.
In a large bowl, combine soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, minced garlic, minced ginger, and black pepper. Whisk until sugar dissolves.
Add blanched beef ribs to a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. Add prepared daikon, carrots, shiitake mushrooms, chestnuts, and jujubes.
Pour the prepared sauce over the ribs and vegetables. Add 750 ml of water to the pot. Liquid should almost cover ingredients.
Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove lid for the last 15-20 minutes of cooking. Increase heat slightly to reduce sauce to a desired thickness. Sauce should be glossy and coat the ribs.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Slice green onions thinly for garnish.
Serve hot in individual bowls, garnished with green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Soaking and blanching the short ribs are crucial steps for a clean, flavorful broth and tender meat.
The sweetness can be adjusted to preference; add more or less brown sugar.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Creamy Dijon Sauce, Roasted Potatoes, and Herb Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut, pan-seared beef medallion, displaying a deep golden-brown crust and a tender interior, is the centerpiece on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Beside it rests a neat mound of fluffy herb rice, speckled with vibrant green parsley and chives. Golden-brown roasted potato wedges, with slightly crispy exteriors, are artfully arranged alongside the beef. A rich, creamy Dijon sauce is generously draped over the beef, pooling elegantly on the plate. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The colors are natural and appealing: the deep browns of the beef and potatoes, the creamy beige of the sauce, and the subtle green accents from the herbs. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into 2cm wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and tender, flipping halfway.

Rinse basmati rice under cold water until water runs clear. Combine rice with 400ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat, keep covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped parsley and chives.

Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add beef medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Transfer beef to a plate, tent with foil, and let rest.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Add minced shallot and cook for 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.

Gradually whisk in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining fresh parsley and chives.
