Finely chopped vibrant green chives are meticulously sprinkled over the crab, adding a final touch of fresh color. The composition is organic and flowing, each element positioned with purpose. The plate rests on a cool, grey-veined Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated simplicity and premium quality.

ingredients.name: King Crab legs or premium lump crab meat

instructions: Combine sugar and 2 tablespoons water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium until sugar caramelizes to a deep amber. Do not stir.
Carefully add red wine and red wine vinegar. Bring to a simmer.
Add 25 ml vodka. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until liquid is syrupy and reduced by half.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Set gastrique aside.
In a separate small saucepan, combine minced shallots, minced garlic, and 25 ml vodka.
Add rum and chicken or fish stock. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce liquid until almost evaporated.
Lower heat to very low. Gradually whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time. Whisk continuously until butter is fully incorporated and sauce is emulsified and creamy.
Stir in heavy cream and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Keep warm over very low heat or in a warm water bath. Do not boil.
If using King Crab legs, carefully crack and remove crab meat in large, intact pieces.
Pat crab meat very dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Carefully place crab meat in the hot pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and heated through. Avoid overcrowding the pan.
Season lightly with sea salt and black pepper.
Ladle a small pool of Red Wine-Vodka Gastrique onto one side of each plate.
Place a portion of seared crab meat next to the gastrique.
Spoon Rum Beurre Blanc around the crab.
Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: The Red Wine-Vodka Gastrique can be made a day in advance and gently reheated.
Ensure butter for beurre blanc is very cold for proper emulsification.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Cucumber Dill Salad
recipes.visual_description: Diced ripe red tomatoes, crisp green cucumbers, and thinly sliced red onion are casually tossed in a large, simple white ceramic serving bowl, showcasing their vibrant natural colors and varied textures. Fresh green dill sprigs are generously sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of verdant color and aromatic freshness. The vegetables are uniformly diced into small cubes, ensuring a balanced bite. A light, glistening vinaigrette coats each piece, reflecting the warm, cozy kitchen light. The bowl is centrally placed on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its rich grain. A casually placed, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone, and a set of basic, everyday stainless steel flatware, complete the homely setting. The overall presentation is unpretentious and inviting, perfect for a relaxed family meal, with all components clearly visible and appetizingly arranged.
instructions: Wash tomatoes and cucumbers. Dice tomatoes into 2 cm cubes. Dice cucumbers into 2 cm cubes.
Peel red onion. Thinly slice red onion into half-moons.
In a large serving bowl, combine diced tomatoes, diced cucumbers, and sliced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Pour dressing over the vegetables. Add chopped fresh dill.
Gently toss all ingredients until well combined and coated with dressing. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fricassée de Poulet aux Champignons
recipes.visual_description: A classic French Fricassée de Poulet aux Champignons is presented centrally on a round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing its rich, creamy texture. Large, irregular chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are nestled amongst quartered, earthy sautéed mushrooms. A velvety, pale ivory sauce, infused with herbs, generously coats the ingredients. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the dish. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and comforting appeal, with a soft-focus bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with crusty baguette slices for dipping.
A simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette makes a perfect accompaniment.
Steamed rice or boiled potatoes are also traditional sides.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Cut into 4 cm irregular chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if needed. Do not overcrowd.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 40g butter to the pan. Add quartered mushrooms. Sauté until golden and softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add diced shallots and minced garlic to the pan. Cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and shallots. Stir well to coat. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook until slightly reduced.
Gradually whisk in hot chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sauce thickens.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Add thyme sprigs. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes; do not boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley just before serving.
notes: This classic French dish is comforting and elegant. Ensure chicken is cooked through for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Cucumber Garden Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh salad presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The salad features generous portions of bright red diced tomatoes and crisp green diced cucumbers, interspersed with thinly sliced white and purple red onion rings and small emerald green diced bell pepper pieces. Freshly chopped parsley flecks the surface, adding bursts of darker green. The ingredients are casually tossed, allowing them to overlap naturally, coated lightly with a simple vinaigrette that glistens on the vegetable surfaces. The colors are natural and inviting, showcasing the freshness of the produce. A plain, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim is ready next to the bowl. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with warm, soft lighting from above, and a simple cloth napkin casually placed beside the bowl. A crusty slice of bread might be visible nearby, suggesting a complete, unpretentious meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Dice tomatoes and cucumbers into 1.5 cm cubes.
Thinly slice the red onion.
Dice the green bell pepper into 1.5 cm cubes.
Chop fresh parsley.
In a large bowl, combine diced tomatoes, cucumbers, sliced red onion, diced bell pepper, and chopped parsley.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients and coat with dressing.
Serve immediately or chill briefly.

recipes.recipe_name: Argentine Beef & Apple Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the hearty Argentine Beef & Apple Stew is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, inviting colors and textures. Chunks of dark, slow-braised beef are nestled among tender, golden-brown potato chunks and softened, slightly translucent apple pieces. The stew's thick, reddish-brown broth, infused with tomato and spices, coats the ingredients generously. The beef appears incredibly tender, almost falling apart. The potatoes hold their shape but show a soft interior. The apple pieces are soft but still distinct. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley contrasts beautifully with the stew's deep tones, adding a fresh visual pop. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl. A set of standard, polished silver flatware rests on the napkin. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and depth without harsh shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (e.g., pan francés) for dipping.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 600 g, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Apple
ingredients.quantity: 1 large, peeled, cored, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with red wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours.
Add potato chunks to the pot. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30 minutes.
Add apple chunks. Cook for 15-20 minutes more, or until beef and potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle hot stew into serving bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This stew deepens in flavor overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Giant Pasta Shells with Savory Beef and Rice Stuffing
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Giant Pasta Shells with Savory Beef and Rice Stuffing is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four generously stuffed conchiglioni shells, glistening with a rich, bubbling tomato-beef sauce, are nestled neatly but organically on the plate. The golden-brown melted mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese forms a bubbly crust over the top, with some of the savory beef and rice stuffing peeking out from the shell openings. The deep red sauce contrasts beautifully with the off-white rice and dark brown beef. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The textures are inviting: tender pasta, soft rice, and gooey cheese. The plate is set on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting appeal, maintaining a casual yet refined restaurant aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside to cool.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the pot. Brown beef, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains. Drain any excess fat.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Add beef broth if a thinner sauce is desired.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta shells in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
In a mixing bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, 50g of grated Parmesan cheese, and 100g of shredded mozzarella cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir approximately 200g of the prepared beef sauce into the rice and cheese stuffing mixture. Mix well to combine.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Spread a thin layer of the remaining beef sauce in the bottom of a 23x33cm baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the beef and rice mixture. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer in the prepared baking dish.
Pour the remaining beef sauce evenly over the stuffed shells.
Sprinkle the remaining 50g of grated Parmesan cheese and 100g of shredded mozzarella cheese over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the sauce is heated through.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Sugo and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp crust, is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole, plump piece, not sliced. Beneath and around the chicken, a rich, vibrant red tomato sugo is generously pooled, showing its slightly chunky texture from the crushed tomatoes. Scattered over and around the chicken are irregular, golden-hued shards of crispy parmesan, adding height and a delicate crunch. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully placed on the chicken and sugo, providing a pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, all under natural, even lighting that highlights the food's textures and colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Canned San Marzano whole peeled tomatoes

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Grate 50g of parmesan cheese. Spread grated parmesan into four thin circles on the parchment paper. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Let cool completely on the sheet. They will crisp as they cool. Break into shards.
For the sugo, heat 30ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in canned tomatoes, crushing them with your hands or a spoon. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in half of the fresh basil, roughly torn.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge chicken lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven.
Bake chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Spoon a generous pool of tomato sugo onto each plate. Place a whole pan-seared chicken breast on top of the sugo. Garnish with parmesan crisps/shards and fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Pearl Onions and Thyme Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly golden-brown braised chicken thigh rests prominently on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, with its skin lightly crisped, is nestled beside a generous, free-form mound of fluffy, white long-grain rice pilaf. The rich, light golden-brown braising sauce, studded with tender, creamy pearl onions and earthy quartered cremini mushrooms, pools elegantly around the chicken and slightly under the rice. The chicken shows its tender, moist texture beneath the seared skin. The rice is distinct, not clumpy, with subtle flecks of finely diced yellow onion and green thyme leaves. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a white cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the inviting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing complements the richness of the dish.
Pair with a glass of the dry white wine used in the braise.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside. Pour off excess fat, leaving about 15ml in the pot.
Add pearl onions and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Sauté over medium heat until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.

Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir for 1 minute. Pour in white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Add chicken broth, 4 thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure liquid mostly covers chicken.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F). Braise for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.

While chicken braises, melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced yellow onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast lightly.

Pour in 500ml water. Add remaining 2 thyme sprigs and season with salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Once chicken is cooked, remove chicken, pearl onions, and mushrooms from the braising liquid. Discard bay leaf and thyme sprigs. If sauce is too thin, simmer over medium-high heat on stovetop until slightly reduced and thickened. Adjust seasoning.

Place a portion of rice pilaf on each plate. Arrange one braised chicken thigh next to the rice. Spoon pearl onions, mushrooms, and braising sauce generously over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs for maximum flavor and moisture.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallion, Red Wine-Chocolate Jus, Apple Confit, Crab Mousse, Mustard Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef medallion, golden-brown with a pink center, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, a rich, glossy pool of dark red wine-chocolate jus glistens, reflecting light. Adjacent to the beef, a small, artfully arranged mound of translucent, diced spiced apple confit offers subtle contrast. A delicate, pearly-white quenelle of steamed crab mousse rests elegantly nearby, its smooth surface hinting at a creamy interior. A crisp, golden mustard seed tuile, irregularly shaped, leans gracefully against the beef, adding an architectural element. Abundant negative space emphasizes the dish's minimalist elegance. The composition rests on a superpremium marble surface, with a crisp, precisely folded white linen napkin and minimalist, modern flatware. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture, creating an ultra-sophisticated, clean aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Red Wine-Chocolate Jus:
Sauté minced shallot in a small saucepan with a knob of butter until translucent.
Deglaze with red wine. Reduce by half.
Add beef stock and thyme sprig. Simmer gently until reduced to a syrupy consistency (approx. 150 ml).
Remove thyme. Stir in chopped dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare Spiced Apple Confit:
Peel, core, and dice apples into 1 cm cubes.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar, water, cinnamon stick, and star anise. Bring to a simmer.
Add diced apples. Cook gently until tender but still holding shape, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove apples with a slotted spoon. Reduce the syrup slightly if needed.
Stir in rum. Set aside.
Prepare Crab Mousse:
Place picked crab meat, double cream, egg white, lemon juice, salt, and white pepper into a food processor.
Pulse until just combined and a coarse mousse forms. Do not overmix.
Fold in chopped chives.
Form small quenelles using two spoons, or pipe small mounds onto a parchment-lined tray.
Gently steam the quenelles for 3-5 minutes until just set. Keep warm.
Prepare Mustard Seed Tuiles:
In a small bowl, whisk together mustard powder, water, flour, olive oil, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour small spoonfuls of batter onto the hot pan, spreading thinly.
Cook until crisp and golden, about 1-2 minutes per side.
Carefully remove and cool on a wire rack. Break into desired shapes.
Cook Beef Tenderloin:
Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat with a touch of high-smoke point oil.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches desired doneness (e.g., 55-60°C for medium-rare to medium).
Add 15g butter and a sprig of thyme to the pan during the last minute. Baste beef.
Remove beef from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.
Plating (for 4 servings):
Spoon a generous pool of red wine-chocolate jus onto one side of each plate.
Place a seared beef medallion next to the jus.
Artistically arrange a small mound of spiced apple confit beside the beef.
Carefully place a steamed crab mousse quenelle on the plate.
Lean a mustard seed tuile against the beef or apple.
Garnish with a few microgreens.
notes: Beef doneness can be adjusted to preference; for a more well-done steak, cook to 70°C internal temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Broccoli & Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, skin golden and crisp, rests centrally on a cream-colored ceramic plate. Alongside, tender roasted potato wedges and substantial chunks of roasted red bell pepper display their earthy tones and slight caramelization. Bright green, roasted broccoli florets provide a vibrant contrast. A generous heap of vivid, reddish-orange fermented broccoli stems, thinly sliced, adds a dynamic texture and tangy counterpoint. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with ample negative space around the components. The plate sits on a light reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin and a simple, subtle plant element complete the clean, minimalist, and eco-conscious presentation, all bathed in soft natural lighting.
instructions: Separate broccoli florets from stems. Trim tough outer layer from stems. Thinly slice stems into rounds or julienne. Blanch florets in boiling salted water for 2 minutes; immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well.

In a bowl, combine sliced broccoli stems with gochugaru, minced garlic, grated ginger, fish sauce (or soy sauce), sugar, and salt. Mix thoroughly. Pack tightly into a clean jar, pressing down to remove air bubbles. Seal jar. Let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Halve or quarter small potatoes. Cut bell pepper into large chunks.

Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss potatoes, bell pepper, and blanched broccoli florets with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Add rosemary/thyme sprigs if using. Spread vegetables on a large baking sheet.

Place seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up on the same baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and skin is golden and crispy. Vegetables should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Arrange roasted chicken, potatoes, and bell pepper on individual plates. Spoon a generous portion of fermented broccoli stems alongside.
notes: Save chicken bones and vegetable trimmings (e.g., bell pepper cores, broccoli leaves) for making flavorful stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Gochujang Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Spicy Korean Gochujang Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Substantial 2.5 cm chicken chunks, seared to a dark golden-brown with visible charred edges, are coated in a glossy, rich reddish-orange gochujang sauce. They are mixed with bright orange julienned carrots and crisp-tender pieces of green and white napa cabbage. Vivid green 5cm spring onion pieces are scattered throughout. The stir-fry is arranged artfully next to a neat mound of fluffy white Basmati rice. A sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds garnishes the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks resting beside the plate, and a small, simple white rice bowl nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a blurred, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain rice (bap).
Traditionally accompanied by various banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi or pickled radish.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm chunks.
In a large bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, honey, and rice vinegar. Whisk well to create the marinade.
Add chicken chunks to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken to the hot wok in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add julienned carrots and chopped napa cabbage to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add spring onions. Toss everything together for 1 minute to combine and heat through.
Serve immediately with a side of steamed Basmati rice. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Potato and Bell Pepper Relish
recipes.visual_description: Pan-seared chicken breast, cut into two substantial pieces, sits slightly off-center on a matte, cream-colored ceramic plate. The chicken boasts a deep golden-brown sear, highlighting its natural contours. Alongside, a mound of lacto-fermented potato slices, their creamy texture and subtle sheen contrasting with the chicken. Scattered around are vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, retaining their natural form and slight char. A small, artful dollop of bright red and yellow bell pepper and broccoli stem relish provides a pop of color and texture. The composition is clean and airy, with ample white space, emphasizing the pure beauty of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a folded undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the organic textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with filtered water or kombucha to complement the clean flavors.
Offer a side of simple, undressed leafy greens.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Potatoes: Wash and thinly slice potatoes (approx. 3mm thick). Dissolve 15g sea salt in 500ml non-chlorinated water to make a 3% brine. Place potato slices in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over potatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged (use a fermentation weight if available). Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Bell Pepper & Broccoli Stem Relish: Separate broccoli florets from stems. Dice bell peppers and broccoli stems into small 5mm cubes (utilizing bell pepper cores and broccoli stems for zero-waste). In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, sugar, mustard seeds, and black peppercorns. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Add diced bell peppers and broccoli stems. Simmer for 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat. Transfer to a clean jar. Allow to cool. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
Roast Broccoli Florets: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 12-15 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly charred.

Pan-Sear Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden-brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Slice each breast into two substantial, thick chunks.

Assemble Dish: Drain fermented potato slices. Arrange a portion of fermented potatoes on each plate. Place two chicken chunks alongside the potatoes. Scatter roasted broccoli florets around. Spoon a dollop of bell pepper and broccoli stem relish over the chicken or alongside. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermentation of potatoes requires several days. Plan this step in advance.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing broccoli stems and bell pepper cores/scraps for the relish.
Fermentation enhances nutrient availability and adds complex flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Potato, and Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of baked pasta, golden-brown and bubbling, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The top crust is a rich blend of melted mozzarella and crispy panko breadcrumbs, creating a textural contrast. Below the surface, layers of tender penne pasta, thinly sliced roasted potatoes, and succulent diced chicken are bound by a creamy, savory cheese sauce. The internal colors are a warm beige and off-white from the sauce and pasta, with hints of golden potato edges and white chicken pieces. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of green. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and inviting warmth.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.
Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until lightly browned and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Thinly slice potatoes into 3 mm rounds. No need to peel.
Melt butter in the same pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sauce thickens. Remove from heat.
Stir 150 g mozzarella and all Parmesan into the sauce until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cooked pasta, cooked chicken, and sauce in a large bowl. Mix well.
Spread half of the pasta mixture evenly in the prepared baking dish.
Arrange half of the potato slices over the pasta mixture.
Add the remaining pasta mixture. Top with remaining potato slices.
Sprinkle remaining 50 g mozzarella and panko breadcrumbs over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown and bubbly. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Roasted Broccoli and Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: The Orecchiette with Roasted Broccoli and Cherry Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, refined single portion of pasta forms a gentle, organic mound in the center of the plate. The orecchiette, with its characteristic ear-like shape, is evenly coated in a light, glossy olive oil and garlic sauce. Interspersed throughout the pasta are vibrant, slightly charred broccoli florets and burst, juicy cherry tomato halves. The broccoli florets are tender-crisp with bright green hues and subtle roasted edges. The cherry tomatoes exhibit a deep red color, some slightly shriveled from roasting, adding a sweet and tangy element. A scattering of fresh, bright green oregano leaves provides a fragrant garnish and a pop of color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate white contrast and umami. The arrangement is natural and flowing, avoiding rigid patterns, with moderate negative space around the dish's perimeter. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the dish as the main subject. The setting is a modern bistro style, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients. Traditional silver flatware is placed alongside the plate, completing the authentic Italian dining experience.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut broccoli into small florets. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Toss broccoli florets and halved cherry tomatoes with 40 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add orecchiette pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, mince garlic. Roughly chop fresh oregano leaves.
In a small pan, heat remaining 40 ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Stir in chopped fresh oregano. Remove from heat.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 60 ml of pasta water.
Combine drained pasta, roasted broccoli and cherry tomatoes, and garlic-oregano oil in a large bowl.
Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to create a light sauce.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately, topped with grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Garlic Herb Chicken with Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, embodying a refined Italian rustic aesthetic. A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, cooked to a deep caramel hue, sits prominently at the center. It is generously draped with a rich, creamy sun-dried tomato sauce, flecked with vibrant green wilted spinach and crimson tomato pieces. The sauce has a glossy sheen, clinging to the chicken. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of roasted rosemary potatoes displays their crispy, golden exterior and fluffy interior, with small pieces of fresh rosemary clinging to them. The plate maintains moderate negative space, allowing the colors of the chicken, red sauce, and golden potatoes to stand out. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a fork and knife, creating an inviting, casual dining scene with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or small new potatoes)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato chunks with remaining 15 ml olive oil, rosemary sprigs, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden.
Reduce skillet heat to medium. Add minced garlic to skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced sun-dried tomatoes, chopped fresh rosemary, and chopped fresh thyme to skillet. Sauté 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce liquid by half, about 5 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in fresh spinach until wilted, about 1-2 minutes. Remove skillet from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Serve immediately with roasted rosemary potatoes.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken Japchae
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Cheesy Chicken Japchae is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with a subtle glaze. Translucent, springy bean thread noodles form the base, interwoven with tender, golden-brown chicken chunks. Vibrant strips of sautéed red and yellow bell peppers are interspersed throughout, maintaining a slight crispness. A generous layer of melted, gooey mozzarella cheese cascades over the top, creating inviting streaks of white and light gold. The dish is garnished simply with bright green slivers of fresh green onion and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. The overall composition is natural and abundant. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. A pair of metal chopsticks rests beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small side dishes (banchan) like kimchi or pickled radish.
Eat with chopsticks.
Best enjoyed family-style, with everyone sharing from a large central dish or individual portions served from it.
instructions: Soak bean thread noodles in warm water for 30 minutes. Drain. Cut into shorter strands if desired.
Cut chicken thighs into 1.5 cm strips. In a bowl, combine chicken strips, 30 ml soy sauce, 15 ml sesame oil, 5 g sugar, and black pepper. Mix well. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Mince garlic. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add marinated chicken to the pan. Cook until chicken is browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Slice bell peppers into thin strips. Add sliced bell peppers to the same pan. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add drained noodles to the pan with bell peppers. Add remaining 30 ml soy sauce, 10 g sugar, and 15 ml sesame oil. Toss well to combine and coat noodles.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Mix everything together.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese over the top of the mixture in the pan. Cover the pan with a lid for 2-3 minutes, or until mozzarella is melted and gooey.
Transfer to serving bowls. Thinly slice green onions. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust sweetness and saltiness to taste.
For a spicier version, add a teaspoon of gochujang with the soy sauce.
traditional_techniques: Seasoning with soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of roasted chicken thigh rests on a well-used wooden dining table. The chicken, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is placed alongside a generous portion of roasted potato chunks. The potatoes are fork-tender with slightly browned, crisp edges. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs, along with roasted lemon slices, are scattered naturally around the chicken and potatoes. The dish is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a rustic rim, showing natural imperfections. Warm, soft light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The overall scene is homely and inviting, focusing on comforting textures and natural colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large roasting pan, toss potato chunks with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up over and among the potatoes.
Tuck lemon slices, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs around chicken and potatoes.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be golden and crispy.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish before serving.
notes: This dish is a complete meal. Adjust roasting time for larger chicken pieces.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Lemon Chicken Soup (Avgolemono)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Avgolemono soup is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The soup displays a creamy, pale yellow hue, indicative of its rich egg and lemon base. Shredded chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm in length, are visible throughout the broth, alongside plump grains of Arborio rice. A generous sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green oregano leaves garnishes the surface, providing a vibrant color contrast. The soup's texture appears smooth and slightly thickened, with a gentle sheen. A silver soup spoon rests on the side of the bowl. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
A light sprinkle of black pepper or a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil can be added before serving.
instructions: Place chicken breast in a large pot. Cover with 1.5 L chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cook chicken gently for 20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from stock. Set aside to cool slightly.
Add remaining 500 ml stock to the pot. Bring stock to a boil. Add rice. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer rice for 15 minutes, or until tender.
Shred cooled chicken breast into bite-sized pieces. Alternatively, dice into 1 cm cubes.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs until frothy. Gradually whisk in fresh lemon juice from both lemons.
Slowly ladle 2-3 scoops of hot broth from the pot into the egg-lemon mixture while continuously whisking. This is tempering the eggs.
Pour the tempered egg-lemon mixture back into the pot with the rice and remaining broth. Stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until soup thickens slightly. Do not boil after adding egg mixture.
Stir in shredded chicken. Season soup with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in chopped fresh oregano.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The key to Avgolemono is tempering the eggs slowly to prevent scrambling. Do not boil the soup once the egg mixture is added.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Rosemary Potatoes and Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef with Rosemary Potatoes and Roasted Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Three substantial chunks of dark, rich braised beef, each with a tender, slightly crusted exterior, are centrally placed. Beside the beef are golden-brown roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly crisp, seasoned with flecks of dark green rosemary. Scattered around are vibrant, burst-skinned roasted cherry tomatoes, their deep red contrasting with the potatoes and beef. A light drizzle of the reduced, glossy braising jus surrounds the beef. A small sprig of fresh rosemary and a few thyme leaves are placed artfully for garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping in the flavorful braising jus.
instructions: Pat beef chuck dry. Cut into 4-5 large chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Stir in beef stock, 2 rosemary sprigs, and 4 thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Cover tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, preheat oven to 200°C. Cut potatoes into wedges. Toss with 1 rosemary sprig, 1 thyme sprig, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender.
Toss cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add to the baking sheet with potatoes for the last 15 minutes of roasting, or roast separately.
Remove braised beef from the oven. Carefully remove beef chunks from the pot. Discard bay leaf and herb stems.
Return pot with braising liquid to stovetop. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce liquid until slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Spoon braised beef and a generous amount of sauce onto plates. Serve with roasted potato wedges and roasted cherry tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken & Scallops with Umami Mushroom-Spinach Ragout
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-crisp skin, rests prominently on a clean white round plate. Beside it, three perfectly seared, plump sea scallops display a beautiful caramelized crust. A rich, earthy mushroom and spinach ragout, studded with finely minced chicken liver and subtle flakes of smoked trout, is artfully spooned next to the proteins. A vibrant pile of crisp-tender whole green beans adds a fresh green contrast. A delicate drizzle of pale green avocado-lime emulsion weaves across the plate, enhancing the colors. The dish is garnished with finely snipped fresh chives, adding a final touch of color and freshness. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with thoughtful spacing. Served on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Fresh chives or dill, for garnish

instructions: Trim green beans. Slice mushrooms. Mince shallots and garlic.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season all sides with salt and pepper.
Pat scallops dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced shallots. Cook 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Add minced chicken liver to the pan. Cook 3-4 minutes until browned. Break up any clumps.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Increase heat to medium-high. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.

Stir in spinach. Cook until wilted. Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until liquid slightly reduces. Stir in flaked smoked trout. Season ragout with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans. Blanch 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain immediately. Toss with a small knob of butter or drizzle of olive oil.
For the avocado-lime emulsion: Combine avocado flesh, lime juice, egg white, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of pepper in a blender. Blend until very smooth and emulsified. Adjust seasoning as needed.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate large pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Continue cooking 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest 5 minutes.

While chicken rests, add remaining 15g butter to the hot pan. Increase heat to high. Add scallops in a single layer. Sear 1.5-2 minutes per side until golden brown and caramelized. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Slice each chicken breast into two thick pieces, or serve whole if preferred. Place one chicken piece on each plate. Arrange three seared scallops beside the chicken.
Spoon a generous portion of the mushroom-spinach ragout next to the proteins. Arrange a pile of blanched green beans on the plate.
Drizzle the avocado-lime emulsion artfully over the dish. Garnish with fresh chives or dill.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing chicken or scallops to ensure a good sear.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Pavo
recipes.visual_description: A central mound of vibrant, golden-orange saffron rice is neatly plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Generous chunks of seared chicken and turkey are nestled throughout and atop the rice, showcasing their golden-brown crusts. The chicken and turkey are cut into 3-4 cm irregular chunks. Bright green peas are scattered across the dish, along with flecks of finely diced red bell pepper and onion from the rich sofrito base. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a verdant contrast, and a fresh lime wedge rests beside the rice. The dish exhibits a rich golden-orange hue from the saffron, deep browns from the seared meats, and vibrant greens and reds from the vegetables. The rice is moist and tender, with individual grains distinct yet integrated. The meats are succulent and fully cooked. The plate is placed on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene from the side, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere. A small, rustic ceramic bowl with extra lime wedges is subtly visible in the background. The presentation is professional, balanced, and uncluttered, showcasing a single individual portion.
instructions: Cut chicken and turkey into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove from skillet.
Add turkey chunks to skillet. Sear until browned. Remove from skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30 ml olive oil, diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and bay leaf. Simmer for 5 minutes, breaking up tomatoes. This is your sofrito.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir well to coat rice with sofrito and toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken and turkey chunks to the skillet, nestling them into the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not stir excessively.
Stir in frozen green peas. Cover and let stand off heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Sautéed Garlic Mushrooms and Crispy Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Sautéed Garlic Mushrooms and Crispy Smashed Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A large, whole pan-seared chicken thigh, with perfectly golden-brown and crispy skin, sits prominently on the plate. Beside the chicken are several golden-brown, crispy smashed potatoes, their irregular edges showcasing their rustic texture. A rich, earthy brown pile of sautéed garlic mushrooms is spooned generously over and around the chicken, with some spilling onto the plate. The entire dish is lightly garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, adding a touch of freshness and color contrast. The colors are natural and appealing: deep golden-browns from the chicken and potatoes, rich browns from the mushrooms, and bright green from the parsley. The plating is organized but not overly rigid, allowing for natural flow. The dish is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard metal flatware placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space surrounding the components.

ingredients.name: Small waxy potatoes (e.g., baby potatoes, Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Place in large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Let cool slightly.

Arrange cooked potatoes on a large baking sheet. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Gently smash each potato with a fork or potato masher until flattened but still intact. Season generously with salt, pepper, thyme, and rosemary.
Roast smashed potatoes in preheated oven for 25-35 minutes, or until deeply golden and crispy.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot skillet.
Sear chicken for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Do not move chicken during searing. Flip chicken.

Transfer skillet to the preheated oven with the potatoes. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Return skillet to medium heat (drain excess chicken fat if desired). Add butter to the skillet. Add quartered mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until liquid slightly reduces. Season mushroom mixture with salt and pepper to taste.

To plate, arrange crispy smashed potatoes on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Place one seared chicken thigh next to the potatoes. Spoon generous amounts of garlic mushrooms over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Potato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone, providing a clean, natural canvas. At the center, two substantial, roasted chicken thigh chunks, their skin deeply golden and crisp, rest naturally without being fanned. Beside the chicken, a generous, organic mound of pale, diced fermented potato salad offers a subtle tang, its texture slightly softened but retaining structure. Sautéed mixed mushroom caps, varying in earthy brown hues, are artfully scattered around the chicken and potatoes, showcasing their natural forms. A glossy, dark amber mushroom stem reduction is drizzled sparingly over the chicken and around the plate, creating subtle pools of rich color. A few crisp, golden-brown potato skins stand upright, adding textural contrast and a zero-waste element. The entire composition is accented by a sparse scattering of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh parsley or chives, providing a delicate pop of color. The plating emphasizes natural shapes, ample white space, and a refined, unfussy presentation. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery, creating an eco-conscious and serene dining experience.

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake), caps sliced, stems reserved
Small waxy potatoes, scrubbed clean, skins reserved
Olive oil
ingredients.quantity: 30ml, plus extra for roasting and dressing

ingredients.name: Dry white wine (optional, for mushroom reduction)
Apple cider vinegar (for potato fermentation brine)
Fresh parsley or chives, roughly chopped (for garnish)

instructions: Step 1: Prepare Fermented Potatoes & Garlic.
Peel potatoes. Reserve skins. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
In a clean jar, combine 120ml apple cider vinegar, 240ml filtered water, 2-3 peeled garlic cloves, 1 bay leaf, 5g mustard seeds, and 5g salt. Stir until salt dissolves.
Add diced potatoes to the jar. Ensure potatoes are fully submerged.
Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly tangy. Taste daily. Refrigerate once desired tang is reached.
Step 2: Make Mushroom Stem Reduction.
Chop reserved mushroom stems finely.
Heat 5ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped stems. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Deglaze with 60ml white wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add 200ml vegetable broth. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until liquid reduces to a thick, flavorful sauce. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Keep reduction warm.
Step 3: Crisp Potato Skins.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss reserved potato skins with 5ml olive oil, pinch of salt and pepper.
Spread skins in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Set aside.
Step 4: Roast Chicken & Sauté Mushrooms.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add sliced garlic and mushroom caps to the skillet around the chicken. Sauté mushrooms for 3-5 minutes until softened.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice chicken into 2-3 large chunks per thigh.
Step 5: Prepare Fermented Potato Salad.
Drain fermented potatoes. Reserve a tablespoon of the brine.
In a bowl, combine drained potatoes with a drizzle of olive oil and reserved brine. Gently toss.
Step 6: Assemble Dish.
On each plate, arrange a portion of fermented potato salad.
Place roasted chicken chunks alongside.
Spoon sautéed mushrooms around the chicken and potatoes.
Drizzle generously with the warm mushroom stem reduction.
Garnish with crispy potato skins and fresh parsley or chives. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe champions sustainable cooking by utilizing mushroom stems for a rich reduction and potato skins for a crispy garnish, minimizing food waste.
Fermenting the potatoes adds a unique tangy depth of flavor and extends their shelf life naturally.
Source local, seasonal ingredients when possible to further enhance the dish's eco-conscious profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Pickled Root Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Apple and Pickled Root Vegetable Salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, set against a light, reclaimed wood surface. Thinly sliced apple wedges are artfully interspersed among tender green lentils, vibrant grated carrots, delicate julienned parsnips, and finely shredded green cabbage. Bright pink pickled red onion slices provide a striking color contrast and textural pop. The ingredients are tossed with a light, glistening dressing, highlighting their natural colors and varied textures. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a final touch of green. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing ample negative space to emphasize the freshness and organic beauty of each ingredient. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, enhancing its earthy, wholesome appeal. An undyed linen napkin rests subtly beside the plate, reinforcing the sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare pickled red onions: Thinly slice the red onion. In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and pickling salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot liquid over sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Cook lentils: Rinse green lentils. Place lentils in a pot with 500 ml water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Drain excess water. Set aside to cool.
Prepare vegetables: Grate carrots. Julienne parsnips. Finely shred green cabbage. Slice apples into thin wedges or small cubes. Coarsely chop fresh parsley.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together extra virgin olive oil, Dijon mustard, maple syrup, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
Assemble salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled lentils, grated carrots, julienned parsnips, shredded cabbage, and sliced apples.
Drain pickled red onions, reserving a small amount of liquid if desired. Add pickled onions to the salad mixture.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Add chopped parsley. Toss again. Serve immediately.
notes: To enhance sustainability, save apple cores and peels to make homemade apple cider vinegar for future use.
Feel free to use other seasonal root vegetables like beetroot (roasted) or daikon radish (julienned).

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Gratin with Gruyère
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Gratin served in a clean white porcelain bowl. The base features thinly sliced 3mm potato rounds, layered and baked in a creamy, nutmeg-infused sauce. The surface has a bubbly, golden-brown crust of melted Gruyère cheese with caramelized edges. Two whole, pan-seared chicken thighs with crispy, deep-brown skin sit centrally atop the gratin. Fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the dish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a white linen napkin, and a silver fork. Natural lighting highlights the contrast between the creamy sauce and the roasted chicken skin. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty French baguette to soak up the cream sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed in a sharp dijon vinaigrette
Pair with a glass of chilled Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir
instructions: Peel and slice potatoes into 3mm rounds.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and cook for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Whisk heavy cream, chicken stock, garlic, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Arrange half the potato slices in a greased ceramic baking dish.
Sprinkle 75g of Gruyère over the potatoes.
Layer the remaining potatoes on top.
Pour the cream mixture evenly over the potatoes.
Place the whole chicken thighs on top of the potato layers.
Bake at 190°C for 45 minutes.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle remaining cheese over the dish.
Broil for 3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
Let the dish rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Using a mandoline ensures even potato slices for consistent cooking.
Dry the chicken skin thoroughly before searing to ensure maximum crispiness.
Check the thickest part of the chicken thigh to confirm it reaches 75°C.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Quick-Fermented Broccoli and Bell Pepper
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken with quick-fermented vegetables presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a muted cream tone. Three to four golden-brown, irregularly shaped roasted chicken chunks are positioned naturally on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant mix of quick-fermented broccoli florets and bell pepper strips, along with small blanched broccoli stem cubes, are loosely arranged, showcasing their bright green and red hues. The broccoli florets retain their distinct shapes, and bell pepper strips are visibly crisp. The overall plating is clean and minimalist, with ample white space on the plate. The table surface is light, textured reclaimed wood, with an undyed linen napkin in beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating subtle shadows. The background is clean and slightly out of focus, with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Wash broccoli and bell peppers. Separate broccoli florets from stems.
Cut broccoli florets into bite-sized pieces. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm strips.
Slice 2 garlic cloves thinly.
Combine 150 ml apple cider vinegar, 150 ml water, 10g salt, and 5g sugar in a clean glass jar. Stir to dissolve.
Add broccoli florets, bell pepper strips, and sliced garlic to the jar. Ensure vegetables are submerged.
Seal jar. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Pat 4 chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks.
Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves.
Toss chicken chunks with 15 ml olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Spread chicken chunks in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast 20-25 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Peel tough outer layer of broccoli stems. Dice stems into 1 cm cubes.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Blanch diced stems for 2 minutes. Drain.
Drain quick-fermented vegetables.
Combine roasted chicken, drained quick-fermented vegetables, and blanched broccoli stem cubes in a large bowl.
Drizzle with remaining 15 ml olive oil. Toss gently. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Saffron Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, seared golden-brown chicken thigh, cooked whole, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. Beside it, a generous mound of fluffy, saffron-infused basmati rice exhibits a soft, pale yellow hue. The rice is adorned with a vibrant scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley, glistening toasted slivered almonds, and a sprinkle of deep red barberries, offering textural contrast and bursts of color. The chicken's surface shows a delicate sear, while the rice grains are distinct and tender. A bright lemon wedge is positioned near the chicken, ready for squeezing. The entire plate is centered on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic flatware, bathed in natural, even light, creating an inviting, refined casual dining presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or a simple cucumber and tomato salad.
instructions: Steep saffron threads in 30ml hot water for 10 minutes. Set aside.
Rinse basmati rice under cold running water until water runs clear. Drain well.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, turmeric, cumin, and coriander.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken, set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute more.
Stir in rinsed rice. Pour in chicken broth and bloomed saffron. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly.
Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Plate chicken and rice. Garnish with fresh chopped herbs, toasted slivered almonds, and barberries or pomegranate seeds. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Rinsing rice thoroughly prevents stickiness and promotes fluffy grains.
Allowing the dish to rest off the heat helps the rice absorb remaining moisture and ensures even cooking.
traditional_techniques: Layering of rice for even cooking and distinct texture

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Chicken & Crispy Potato Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Japanese Chicken and Crispy Potato Rice Bowl is presented in a clean, white ceramic donburi bowl, centered on a light wooden table. The base is fluffy, perfectly cooked white short-grain rice. Succulent pan-seared chicken thigh chunks, cooked to a golden-brown, are artfully arranged on one side. Alongside them, golden-crisp potato batons, fried to perfection, add a delightful textural contrast. Bright red cherry tomato halves, lightly seared, are scattered across the top, providing pops of color and juicy freshness. A delicate zigzag drizzle of creamy Japanese mayonnaise adds richness. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a white cotton napkin. The background is a soft-focus, modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks.
Offer a small side dish of pickled ginger (gari) or quick daikon pickle.
instructions: Cook short-grain rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, grated garlic, and grated ginger. Set aside.
Peel potatoes and cut into 1 cm x 5 cm batons.
Boil potato batons in a pot of salted water for 5 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add potato batons. Fry until golden-brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Remove and season with salt. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the same skillet. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden-brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Pour the reserved sauce mixture over the chicken. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly and coats the chicken. Remove from heat.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Quickly sear in the same skillet for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened.
To assemble: Divide cooked rice among 4 donburi bowls. Arrange chicken chunks, crispy potato batons, and seared cherry tomatoes on top of the rice.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise and a dash of soy sauce. Drizzle this mixture over each assembled bowl.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use Japanese mayonnaise (like Kewpie) for its richer, tangier flavor. Regular mayonnaise can be used as a substitute.

recipes.recipe_name: Truffled Chicken Roulade, Hijiki Emulsion, Kimchi Purée
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut, golden-brown chicken roulade medallion, revealing a vibrant green spinach filling, anchors the center of a pristine white, modern designer plate. The chicken boasts a perfectly seared, slightly torched crisp skin. Alongside the chicken, an artful, organic sweep of dark, glossy hijiki emulsion provides a rich, contrasting texture. A small, precise dollop of bright red-orange kimchi purée adds a pop of color and a bold flavor accent. Nestled delicately nearby are one or two translucent, glistening soy sauce spheres, ready to burst with umami. A vibrant green basil oil is subtly drizzled or painted onto the plate, adding freshness and visual flow. Abundant fresh white truffle shavings delicately crown the chicken, their ethereal presence hinting at luxury. The entire composition is meticulously placed, leaving significant negative space on the plate, emphasizing minimalist elegance. The dish rests on a premium grey veined marble surface, flanked by a precisely folded white linen napkin and a single modern, elegant fork. Dramatic, directional lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the textures and refined presentation.
instructions: Rehydrate hijiki seaweed in 100ml water for 15 minutes. Drain well.
Prepare alginate bath: In a tall container, whisk sodium alginate into 500ml distilled water. Blend until smooth. Let rest for at least 2 hours to remove air bubbles.

Prepare basil oil: Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze dry. Blend basil with 100ml grapeseed oil and a pinch of salt until smooth. Pass through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth. Set aside.
Prepare kimchi purée: Combine kimchi, 50ml stock, sesame oil, and sugar in a small saucepan. Simmer for 10 minutes. Blend until smooth. Pass through a fine mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Prepare hijiki emulsion: Sauté rehydrated hijiki in a small pan for 2 minutes. Add 5ml soy sauce and 5ml rice vinegar. Simmer until liquid evaporates. Transfer to a blender. Slowly emulsify with 100ml neutral oil until smooth. Set aside.

Prepare soy sauce spheres: Dissolve calcium lactate gluconate in 100ml soy sauce. Fill a syringe or dropper with the soy-calcium mixture. Slowly drop individual drops into the sodium alginate bath from a height of 5-10cm. Let spheres set for 2-3 minutes. Carefully remove spheres with a slotted spoon. Rinse gently in clean water. Store in a small amount of soy sauce or oil until serving.

Prepare chicken roulades: Pound each chicken breast evenly to 1.5cm thickness. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Sauté minced garlic in 15g butter until fragrant. Add spinach and cook until wilted. Season. Divide spinach mixture among chicken breasts. Roll each breast tightly into a roulade. Secure with kitchen twine.

Cook chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades on all sides until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest for 5 minutes. Remove twine. Use a kitchen torch to crisp the chicken skin lightly on all sides for texture.

Plate the dish: Slice each chicken roulade diagonally into 2 thick medallions. Place one or two medallions artfully on each plate. Create a sweeping line or organic dollop of hijiki emulsion beside the chicken. Add a small, precise dollop of kimchi purée. Carefully place 1-2 soy sauce spheres near the chicken. Drizzle basil oil around the plate. Finely shave fresh white truffle over the chicken and around the plate. Garnish with a few microgreens if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Chicken Teriyaki
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Chicken Teriyaki is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick medallions of pan-seared chicken thigh, boasting a rich, glossy dark brown teriyaki glaze, are arranged centrally. The chicken skin exhibits a crispy, caramelized texture. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy white short-grain rice provides a contrasting color and texture. A vibrant cluster of steamed green broccoli florets is placed opposite the rice, adding a fresh, verdant accent. The dish is garnished with a scattering of toasted white sesame seeds and delicate thin slices of bright green spring onion over the chicken. The composition is balanced and appealing, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, with traditional chopsticks resting beside a small, round rice bowl, and a small ceramic dish containing pickled ginger, enhancing the authentic Japanese bistro aesthetic. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Trim excess fat.
Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic in a small saucepan. Whisk well.
Bring sauce mixture to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown.
Flip chicken thighs. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook for another 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Meanwhile, cook rice according to package instructions.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Once chicken is cooked, pour the prepared teriyaki sauce over the chicken in the skillet. Simmer for 1-2 minutes, coating chicken evenly with the glaze.
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes. Cut each thigh into thick medallions or serve whole.
Serve chicken immediately with steamed rice and blanched broccoli. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Clásico
recipes.visual_description: The Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous single portion. Golden-orange, moist medium-grain rice forms the base, studded with vibrant, uniformly diced red and yellow bell peppers, bright orange diced carrots, and soft, creamy diced butternut squash. Large, succulent chunks of seared chicken are nestled throughout the rice, displaying a rich, caramelized exterior. A scattering of bright green peas adds pops of color. The dish is garnished with freshly chopped green cilantro, providing a contrasting verdant hue. The composition is organic and flowing, not overly structured, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin, and a traditional, simple fork and spoon.
