Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh citrus squeeze.
Traditionally accompanied by warm, crusty bread.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion, red and yellow bell peppers, carrot, and butternut squash to the pan. Sauté 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, and bay leaf. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes to coat rice in aromatics.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking, if using.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Discard bay leaf.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
For best results, use a heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven to prevent sticking.
Avoid over-stirring the rice to prevent it from becoming gummy.
traditional_techniques: Sofrito preparation for the aromatic base

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Potato Noodle Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Cheesy Chicken and Potato Noodle Bake is scooped onto a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The top layer features golden-brown, bubbly melted American cheese draped over thinly sliced (3mm thick) Russet potatoes, some edges slightly crisped from baking. Beneath, creamy white sauce coats tender 2 cm diced chicken cubes and soft, off-white egg noodles. A light, functional sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adds a touch of green. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, everyday silver fork is placed casually to the right. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family meal. A casually folded beige cloth napkin lies nearby. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere, ensuring the focus remains on the hearty comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with a simple green salad or steamed vegetables.

ingredients.name: Russet potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 400g, peeled and thinly sliced (approx. 3 mm thick)

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sauce thickens.
Season sauce with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Stir in cooked noodles. Mix well.
Pour the chicken and noodle mixture into a 20x30 cm baking dish. Spread evenly.
Arrange thinly sliced potatoes over the noodle mixture, slightly overlapping.
Lay American cheese slices over the potatoes, covering the top completely.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: White Truffle Chicken Ballotine with Basil-Hijiki Emulsion and Soy Spheres
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of White Truffle Chicken Ballotine is presented on an elegant, pristine white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight the dish. Two thick medallion slices of golden-crusted, tender chicken ballotine, revealing a subtle, textured kimchi-truffle filling, are artfully arranged in a slightly overlapping, natural composition. A flowing, organic smear of light beige hijiki emulsion provides a creamy base. A vibrant, deep green basil oil is delicately drizzled around the chicken and emulsion, adding visual contrast and freshness. Two or three dark, glistening soy spheres, perfectly formed, are strategically placed to offer a burst of umami. The entire dish is generously adorned with delicate, translucent shavings of fresh white truffle. The setting is a luxurious, polished white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, professional lighting that creates soft shadows and emphasizes texture. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate, completing the sophisticated, minimalist presentation.

ingredients.name: White truffle
ingredients.quantity: 10g, finely minced for filling, plus 10g fresh for shaving

instructions: Prepare Chicken Ballotine: Pound chicken breasts to 1 cm thickness. Season lightly with salt and pepper. In a bowl, combine minced kimchi, minced white truffle, panko breadcrumbs, and egg yolk. Mix well. Divide filling evenly among chicken breasts. Roll each breast tightly into a cylinder. Tie securely with kitchen twine.

Sear and Roast Chicken: Preheat oven to 180°C. Heat 30ml grapeseed oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken ballotines until golden brown on all sides. Transfer skillet to oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 10 minutes. Remove twine. Slice each ballotine into 2 cm thick medallions.

Make Basil Oil: Blanch basil leaves in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well and squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 150ml grapeseed oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for clear oil. Season with salt.

Prepare Hijiki Emulsion: Rehydrate hijiki seaweed in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain well. In a small saucepan, combine rehydrated hijiki and dashi broth. Simmer for 5 minutes. Blend the hijiki mixture with 50ml grapeseed oil until completely smooth and emulsified. Season with a pinch of salt.

Create Soy Spheres: Dissolve 2g sodium alginate in 50ml soy sauce. Blend well until no lumps remain. Let sit for 30 minutes to remove air bubbles. In a separate bowl, dissolve 5g calcium chloride in 500ml distilled water to create the calcium bath. Using a syringe or dropper, carefully drop the soy-alginate mixture into the calcium bath. Allow spheres to form for 1-2 minutes. Gently remove spheres with a slotted spoon. Rinse briefly in clean water. Set aside.

Plate the Dish: Spoon a flowing, organic smear of hijiki emulsion onto one side of each plate. Arrange two chicken ballotine medallions on top of the emulsion. Drizzle basil oil artistically around the chicken and emulsion. Carefully place 2-3 soy spheres near the chicken. Shave fresh white truffle generously over the chicken. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Root Vegetables and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of braised chicken thigh, golden-brown and glistening, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. It is surrounded by tender root vegetable chunks, including 2 cm carrot chunks and halved or quartered potatoes, alongside quartered cremini mushrooms. All ingredients are coated in a rich, savory, slightly thickened sauce. A scattering of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh basil leaves adds a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add roughly chopped onion, 2 cm chunks of carrots, and halved or quartered potatoes to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Pour in white wine and deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them among the vegetables. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables are tender.
Remove lid. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes to slightly reduce sauce, if desired.
Stir in roughly chopped fresh basil just before serving. Adjust seasoning as needed.
notes: This dish is even better the next day as flavors deepen.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown roasted chicken and potatoes rests on a rustic ceramic plate. Two crispy-skinned chicken thighs are positioned naturally. Thick-cut potato wedges, roasted to a deep golden hue with soft interiors, are scattered around the chicken. Bright red, blistered cherry tomato halves and softened, light brown roasted garlic cloves are interspersed among the potatoes, adding pops of color and texture. Fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves cling to the roasted ingredients. The arrangement is casual, as if scooped directly from a family pan, filling the plate without overcrowding. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Simple, everyday flatware and a casually folded cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place chicken thighs, potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic cloves in a large roasting pan.
Add rosemary sprigs and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients together to coat evenly.
Arrange in a single layer in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca
recipes.visual_description: The Chicken Saltimbocca is plated as a single, refined portion on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown chicken cutlets, each topped with crisped prosciutto and vibrant green sage leaves, are arranged slightly overlapping in the center. The chicken is pounded thin into irregular medallions. A glistening, pale golden pan sauce pools elegantly around the chicken. Textures are varied: the tender, moist chicken contrasts with the slightly crispy prosciutto and soft sage. A small sprig of fresh sage garnishes the dish. The overall presentation is balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors and textures of the components. The plate rests on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside it, under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple pasta (e.g., linguine, tagliatelle) tossed with butter and Parmesan.
Accompany with roasted new potatoes or steamed green beans.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound thin to 0.5 cm thickness.
Season both sides of pounded chicken lightly with salt and pepper.
Lay two slices of prosciutto on top of each chicken cutlet. Place four sage leaves on top of the prosciutto.
Secure prosciutto and sage to chicken using toothpicks or small skewers if desired.
Dredge each chicken cutlet lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the butter.
Add chicken cutlets to skillet, sage-side down first. Cook for 3-4 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until cooked through and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
Deglaze skillet with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken broth to skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in remaining butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened.
Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Pour sauce over chicken cutlets before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is pounded to an even thickness for uniform cooking.
Do not overcrowd the pan when cooking chicken; cook in batches if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Medallion with Lobster & Scallop
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a luxurious, minimalist dish presented on an exquisite, large bone china plate with abundant negative space. A perfectly seared, thick beef tenderloin medallion, cooked to a tender medium-rare, occupies a central position. Beside it, a glistening poached lobster tail half, its vibrant red shell contrasting with its pristine white flesh, is artfully arranged. Two beautifully seared sea scallops, displaying a rich golden-brown crust and a translucent interior, are nestled nearby. A delicate, creamy swirl of rich brown forest mushroom emulsion provides a refined base, while precise dots or a thin, elegant line of deep reddish-brown chipotle-honey gastrique adds a sophisticated pop of color and flavor. A small, glistening quenelle of black caviar delicately rests atop one scallop, signifying luxury. A few vibrant green microgreens are meticulously placed for a final touch of freshness and color. The plating is organic and flowing, avoiding rigid geometric shapes. The setting features a pristine white Carrara marble surface, an expensive bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern, and a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish as the main subject against an ultra-minimalist background, emphasizing the extreme restraint and sophisticated simplicity of this Michelin-starred presentation.
instructions: Prepare Beef Tenderloin: Cut tenderloin into 10 equal medallions (approx. 200g each). Season with salt and pepper. Sear medallions in hot olive oil for 2-3 minutes per side until deeply golden. Transfer to a baking tray. Finish in a preheated oven at 180°C for 5-7 minutes for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches 57°C. Rest beef for 5 minutes.

Prepare Lobster Tails: Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Add lobster tails. Poach for 4-5 minutes until shells turn bright red and flesh is opaque. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Remove lobster meat from shells. Slice each tail in half lengthwise. Lightly brush with melted butter and a squeeze of lemon juice.

Prepare Seared Scallops: Pat scallops completely dry. Season with salt. Heat olive oil in a pan over high heat until shimmering. Add scallops in a single layer. Sear for 2 minutes per side until a deep golden crust forms. Do not overcrowd the pan. Finish with a small knob of butter and a squeeze of lemon juice.

Make Forest Mushroom Emulsion: Finely dice shallots and 2 garlic cloves. Sauté in 20g butter until translucent. Add cleaned and roughly chopped mushrooms. Cook until softened and liquid evaporates. Add chicken stock and reduce by half. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 5 minutes. Blend mixture until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-smooth emulsion. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Make Chipotle-Honey Gastrique: Finely mince chipotle chiles. In a small saucepan, combine honey, red wine vinegar, and minced chipotle. Bring to a simmer. Reduce until syrupy, about 5-7 minutes. Strain if desired for a smoother consistency. Season to taste.

Assembly: On each plate, create a delicate, organic swirl of mushroom emulsion. Place one seared beef medallion centrally. Arrange one lobster tail half and two seared scallops beside the beef. Drizzle a few precise dots or a thin line of chipotle-honey gastrique around the plate. Top one scallop with a small quenelle of caviar. Garnish with a few delicate microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef and Beer with Herbed Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous mound of fluffy brown rice forms a base. Substantial chunks of deeply braised beef, rich and dark brown, are arranged beside the rice. The beef glistens with a thick, glossy, reduced beer and beef stock sauce that pools invitingly. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered over the beef and sauce for color and freshness. A light dusting of red cayenne pepper adds a subtle visual warmth. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table. Standard silver flatware is placed on a folded neutral-colored cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background, suggesting a modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 4-5 cm chunks
Dark beer (e.g., stout or dark ale)

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef chunks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Dredge beef chunks lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef stock and cayenne pepper. Stir to combine. Liquid should mostly cover the beef.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot with a lid.
Transfer pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

While beef braises, cook brown rice. Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 750 ml water and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Once beef is tender, remove pot from oven. Skim any excess fat from the surface of the sauce.
Stir in fresh basil just before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

To serve, place a mound of brown rice on each plate. Spoon generous portions of braised beef and sauce alongside or slightly over the rice. Garnish with additional fresh basil and a light sprinkle of cayenne if desired.
notes: For a thicker sauce, remove beef after braising, reduce sauce on stovetop over medium-high heat until desired consistency.
Quality of beer impacts flavor. Choose a beer you enjoy drinking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Tenderloin with Savory Apple-Oat Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of pan-seared pork tenderloin with savory apple-oat risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto forms a creamy, free-flowing base, showcasing visible small diced apple cubes and specks of thyme. Resting beside the risotto are several thick-cut, golden-brown pork medallions, perfectly seared with a tender interior. A generous sprinkle of roughly chopped, toasted walnuts adds texture and a deeper brown hue across the dish. A few fresh thyme sprigs are placed artfully for a touch of green. The colors are natural and inviting: creamy beige risotto, golden-brown pork, and the earthy tones of walnuts and apples, accented by vibrant green thyme. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard polished silverware, and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, all bathed in natural, even lighting characteristic of a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Dice onion into small cubes. Mince garlic. Dice apples into small cubes. Roughly chop walnuts.
Toast walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes, until fragrant. Set aside.
Season pork tenderloins generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork until golden brown on all sides, about 2-3 minutes per side.

Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast pork for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 70°C (158°F). Pork will reach 75°C (167°F) while resting. Remove from oven, tent with foil, and rest for 10 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.

While pork rests, start the risotto. In the same pan (or a clean pot), melt 20g butter with a splash of olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rolled oats to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. If using, deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook until wine is almost evaporated.

Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 15-20 minutes, until oats are creamy but still have a slight bite.
In a separate small pan, melt 15g butter over medium heat. Add diced apples and sauté for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Stir in apple cider vinegar. Season lightly with salt.

Stir cooked apples, grated Parmesan, remaining 15g butter, and two-thirds of the toasted walnuts into the oat risotto. Season with salt and pepper to taste. The risotto should be creamy and free-flowing.

Ladle a generous portion of the savory apple-oat risotto onto each plate. Arrange several thick pork medallions neatly beside or partially on top of the risotto. Garnish with remaining toasted walnuts and fresh thyme sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken is elegantly presented on a round, matte white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, pan-seared and roasted boneless chicken thighs, each tender and glistening, are positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant, roasted vegetables: several bright red, plump cherry tomatoes, thick-cut planks of tender-crisp zucchini with slight char marks, and soft, caramelized red onion wedges. A light, savory pan sauce, infused with lemon and herbs, is artfully drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. Fresh sprigs of green oregano and thyme, along with a bright yellow lemon wedge, are placed strategically as a garnish, adding color and freshness. The arrangement is organic and balanced, allowing for moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a clean, modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the pan juices.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness.
Roasted potatoes or couscous can be served on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large oven-safe skillet, heat 30 ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down (if skin-on) or presentation-side down for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Flip and sear for another 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add minced garlic, cherry tomatoes, zucchini planks, and red onion wedges. Season with salt and pepper.
Sauté vegetables for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Return chicken to the skillet, nesting it among the vegetables.
In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, chopped oregano, chopped thyme, and chicken broth.
Pour mixture over chicken and vegetables in the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the skillet for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly cooked to 75°C (167°F) for safety.
Do not overcrowd the skillet during searing to ensure proper browning.
Adjust herbs based on personal preference; fresh is highly recommended for flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Tomato and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly braised bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is golden-brown from initial searing, contrasting with the tender meat beneath. It is nestled in a rich, rustic pool of vibrant red tomato sauce, which has visible softened chunks of diced yellow onion and translucent slices of garlic. Halved, bright red cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout the sauce, adding pops of fresh color and texture. A light scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley leaves provides a final aromatic and visual flourish over the chicken and sauce. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside it. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, leaving moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread to sop up the sauce
Served alongside simple rice or roasted potatoes
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add sliced garlic and dried oregano. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Orange-Hibiscus Steamed Cake
recipes.visual_description: A thick, rectangular slice of Orange-Hibiscus Steamed Cake rests centrally on a simple, round ceramic plate with a subtle off-white glaze. The cake displays a soft, light orange hue, with visible, fine crumb structure and tiny dark specks from the hibiscus or orange zest. A thin, glossy, translucent rum-orange glaze coats the top, slightly dripping down the sides. The cake's surface is smooth and slightly domed. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. A small, unglazed clay teacup, partially filled with amber tea, is casually placed beside the plate. A folded, patterned batik cloth napkin is tucked under the teacup. Warm, soft light illuminates the scene from above, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served warm or at room temperature.
Often accompanied by a cup of hot black tea or kopi tubruk (Indonesian coffee).
instructions: Prepare a steamer. Line a 20x20 cm square baking pan or individual ramekins with parchment paper. Lightly grease.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, 100 grams granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites until foamy. Gradually add remaining 20 grams granulated sugar. Whisk until soft peaks form.
In a third bowl, combine cooled hibiscus tea, orange juice, orange zest, vegetable oil, and 15 ml rum.
Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the egg white mixture, alternating with the wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared pan or ramekins.

Steam for 25-30 minutes for a square cake, or 15-20 minutes for individual cakes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. Ensure the steamer lid is wrapped in a cloth to prevent water dripping.
While cake steams, prepare the glaze. In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar with remaining 15 ml rum and 1-2 teaspoons of orange juice until smooth. Adjust consistency with more juice if needed.
Remove cake from steamer. Let cool slightly in the pan.
Drizzle the warm glaze over the top of the cake. Slice and serve.
notes: Ensure the steamer lid is wrapped with a cloth to prevent condensation from dripping onto the cake, which can make it soggy.
Do not overmix the batter; gentle folding ensures a light and fluffy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced. Alongside, vibrant roasted bell pepper strips in red, yellow, and orange are artfully arranged, interspersed with tender red onion wedges and burst cherry tomatoes. Dark, pitted Kalamata olives and creamy white feta crumbles are scattered throughout the vegetables, adding contrasting colors and textures. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley brightens the top. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a light cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or crusty artisanal bread.
Offer a side of tzatziki or hummus.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 2cm strips. Slice red onion into thin wedges.
On a baking sheet, combine bell peppers, red onion, and cherry tomatoes. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, and oregano. Toss to coat.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
To the roasted vegetables, add pitted Kalamata olives and crumbled feta cheese. Toss gently.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the chicken and vegetables.
Plate one chicken breast. Arrange roasted vegetables alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust roasting time for vegetables based on desired tenderness.
Ensure chicken is fully cooked for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Roasted Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, with its crispy skin, is surrounded by a rich, rustic sauce of burst red cherry tomatoes and dark, glossy Kalamata olives. Scattered throughout the vibrant sauce are flecks of fresh green parsley, contrasting beautifully with the deep red and black hues. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its tender texture. The dish has a natural, organic flow, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a fork and knife, all under soft, even natural light, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere with a Mediterranean touch.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, cherry tomatoes, thyme, and rosemary to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.
Cover the pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30 minutes.
Uncover the pan. Continue braising for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and tomatoes have burst.
Remove from oven. Stir in pitted Kalamata olives.
Let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best results, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs for maximum flavor and moisture.
Adjust seasoning to taste after braising.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Spicy Pineapple Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared pork loin medallions is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork, cooked to a tender pink interior with a golden-brown crust, is cut into thick 2 cm rounds and neatly arranged. Alongside the pork, a vibrant, mounded scoop of spicy pineapple salsa provides a burst of color and freshness. The salsa features small, uniformly diced cubes of bright yellow pineapple, deep red onion, and green jalapeño, all flecked with fresh green cilantro. A few fresh cilantro sprigs garnish the salsa. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting, keeping the focus entirely on the inviting main course.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat pork loin dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork loin 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown crust forms.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
While pork roasts, prepare salsa. Peel and core pineapple. Dice pineapple, red onion, and jalapeño into small, uniform cubes.
Chop fresh cilantro. Combine diced pineapple, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro, and lime juice in a medium bowl. Season salsa with salt to taste.
Remove pork from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest 10 minutes.
Slice pork loin into 2 cm thick medallions.
Serve pork medallions with a generous portion of spicy pineapple salsa.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni al Pomodoro Fresco e Burrata
recipes.visual_description: Rigatoni pasta is centrally piled on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta is coated in a vibrant red sauce made from blistered cherry tomatoes, with some tomatoes visibly burst and others still intact. Thinly sliced garlic cloves are interspersed throughout the sauce. A creamy half-ball of burrata is gently placed atop the pasta, its soft interior beginning to meld into the warm sauce. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered generously over the dish, providing a verdant contrast. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The plate is moderately spaced. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate on a simple wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and textures. This is a single, inviting portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately.
Offer extra Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes burst and soften. Gently crush some tomatoes with a spoon to release juices.
Drain pasta, reserving 120ml of pasta water. Add drained pasta to the skillet with the tomato sauce. Add half of the torn basil.

Pour in 60ml of reserved pasta water. Stir well to combine, allowing sauce to coat the pasta. Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly (mantecare).
Remove from heat. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Divide pasta among four plates. Place half a burrata ball on top of each serving. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of fresh olive oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Use high-quality fresh ingredients for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Style Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spanish Style Chicken and Rice is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are nestled amongst the vibrant, reddish-orange rice. The rice is moist, studded with visible diced red bell pepper, white onion, and small chunks of tomato. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish exudes warmth and comfort. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the bowl. The setting is a cozy family kitchen, bathed in warm, natural light, reflecting a homely, lived-in atmosphere. The overall presentation is unpretentious and inviting, typical of a comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to combine.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat the rice grains with the vegetable and tomato mixture.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring gently.
Nestle the seared chicken pieces back into the pan, skin-side up, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked through and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove pan from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are vibrant halved cherry tomatoes, deep purple red onion wedges, and shiny black Kalamata olives, all glistening with savory pan juices. The roasted vegetables are tender with slightly caramelized edges. Fresh green sprigs of oregano and thyme are artfully placed on top of the chicken and among the vegetables, adding a pop of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests beside the chicken, ready for squeezing. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver fork and knife beside the plate. The background features a softly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a relaxed yet refined dining atmosphere, illuminated by natural, even lighting. The composition is balanced, showcasing the natural textures and rich colors of the Mediterranean ingredients with appropriate negative space, emphasizing the rustic elegance of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.
Serve with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with 3g salt and 1g black pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil, red onion wedges, smashed garlic, halved cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives to the pan. Sauté 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in 2g salt and 1g black pepper. Add chicken broth and fresh oregano and thyme sprigs.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them among the vegetables.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 20-25 minutes, until internal chicken temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove pan from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and vegetables with pan juices. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to taste.
Chicken breasts can be substituted; adjust cooking time as needed to prevent drying.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork Pasta with Fermented Corn and Celery Leaf Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of slow-cooked pork pasta is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The dish features tender, pulled pork chunks, naturally integrated with al dente rigatoni pasta. Bright, golden fermented corn kernels are scattered throughout, providing pops of color and texture. A vibrant green celery leaf pesto is artfully drizzled over the top, creating organic lines. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. The pork is presented in natural, untrimmed chunks, showcasing its rustic texture. The overall color palette is earthy and natural, highlighting the ingredients' inherent beauty. The plate rests on a light-colored, reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in beige is folded neatly beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is simple, with a subtle hint of green foliage from a houseplant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Corn: Combine corn kernels, 500ml water, and 15g sea salt in a clean jar. Seal. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tanginess is reached.
Prepare Pork: Pat pork shoulder dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a Dutch oven. Sear pork on all sides until browned. Remove pork.
Dice onion and celery stalks. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to Dutch oven. Sauté diced onion, celery, and minced garlic until softened, about 8 minutes.
Return pork to Dutch oven. Add vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cover. Cook in oven at 150°C for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender.

Remove pork from Dutch oven. Shred or cut pork into large chunks. Skim fat from braising liquid. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened. Return pork to reduced liquid. Keep warm.

Prepare Celery Leaf Pesto: Combine celery leaves, walnuts, 1 clove garlic, lemon juice, 60ml olive oil, and a pinch of salt in a food processor. Blend until smooth. Add more olive oil if needed for desired consistency.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 60ml pasta water.
Combine cooked pasta with shredded pork and reduced braising liquid. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen.
Stir in a few spoonfuls of fermented corn into the pasta mixture.
Plate pasta and pork mixture. Top with more fermented corn and a drizzle of celery leaf pesto.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Roasted Chicken Thighs with Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a rustic, comforting single portion on an off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and slightly blistered, sits prominently. Beside it, generous roasted potato chunks, irregularly cut, show caramelized edges and fluffy interiors. Vibrant orange carrot rounds and tender, slightly charred red onion wedges are interspersed. Vegetables are olive oil-sheened, flecked with dark green rosemary. A few whole rosemary leaves garnish naturally. Colors are warm, earthy: deep browns, rich oranges, purplish-red. The natural, unforced arrangement appears scooped from the pan. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple linen napkin is casually placed. Warm, inviting light suggests a cozy kitchen. Standard fork and knife are beside the plate. Minimal background hints at a lived-in kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the sheet pan for a family-style meal.
Serve with a simple green salad on the side.
Offer a crusty bread for soaking up pan juices.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled, cut into 2 cm thick rounds

ingredients.name: Fresh Rosemary
ingredients.quantity: 2 sprigs, leaves stripped and roughly chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, carrot rounds, and red onion wedges.
Add olive oil, chopped rosemary, minced garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper to vegetables. Toss until evenly coated.
Spread seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up among vegetables on the baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin is not covered.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip vegetables and gently stir them. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
If desired, briefly broil for 2-3 minutes for extra crispy chicken skin. Watch carefully.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure baking sheet is large enough to spread ingredients in a single layer for even roasting. Crowding will steam instead of roast.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.
Check chicken temperature with a meat thermometer in the thickest part, avoiding the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Mushroom Sauce and Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of pan-seared beef medallions is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, seared beef medallions, exhibiting a rich golden-brown crust and a tender, rosy interior, are centrally placed. A generous, glossy garlic mushroom sauce, rich with earthy brown mushrooms and subtle green thyme specks, is spooned over the beef, pooling slightly around it. Crispy roasted potato wedges, golden-brown with a fluffy interior, are artfully arranged alongside the beef. Chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant green garnish, contrasting with the warm tones of the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional bistro-style presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes until golden and tender, flipping halfway.
While potatoes roast, pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Remove beef from skillet and set aside on a plate. Tent with foil.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add minced shallot and minced garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.

Pour in beef broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium. Stir in heavy cream and thyme sprigs. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Return beef medallions to the skillet, spooning sauce over them. Heat gently for 1 minute.
Divide roasted potatoes and beef medallions among four plates. Spoon generous amount of garlic mushroom sauce over beef. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Mediterranean Chicken with Cherry Tomatoes and Feta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, its skin crisped from baking. It rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate, surrounded by a vibrant medley of bursting, roasted cherry tomatoes, tender diced red onion, and glossy whole pitted Kalamata olives. A generous scattering of crumbled white feta cheese melts slightly over the warm ingredients, adding creamy texture and bright contrast. Freshly chopped green parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge provide a final pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin beside the plate, under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Dice red onion. Mince garlic cloves. Chop fresh oregano and parsley.
In a large baking dish, combine whole cherry tomatoes, diced red onion, minced garlic, and whole pitted Kalamata olives.
Drizzle vegetable mixture with 30ml olive oil. Add chopped fresh oregano. Stir to combine.
Nestle seasoned chicken thighs among the vegetables in the baking dish. Drizzle chicken with remaining 30ml olive oil.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature. It should reach 75°C (167°F).
Crumble feta cheese over the chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven for 5-10 minutes, until feta is slightly softened and chicken is fully cooked.
Squeeze half a lemon over the dish. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs add more flavor and crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Chicken and Shrimp Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Cajun Chicken and Shrimp Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The fettuccine is neatly coiled, coated in a rich, creamy orange-red sauce. Seared golden-brown chicken chunks and plump, pink shrimp are arranged atop the pasta. Vibrant diced red, green, and yellow bell peppers are interspersed throughout, adding color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley and grated Parmesan cheese provides a fresh garnish. The dish exhibits balanced composition with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the appealing textures and colors. A cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate, creating a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread or cornbread to sop up the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Toss with 100g Cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper.

Heat 75 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 75 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onions and bell peppers. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, minced jalapeno, and dried chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream, remaining 50g Cajun seasoning, and hot sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Add shrimp to the simmering sauce. Cook for 3-5 minutes until shrimp are pink and opaque. Do not overcook.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Stir in 150g grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Cook fettuccine according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Add drained pasta directly to the sauce. Toss to combine thoroughly. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and remaining grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust spice level to personal preference by modifying hot sauce and jalapeno quantities.
For best results, use freshly grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Mustard Beef Medallions with Cheesy Potato Roesti and Brown Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Mustard Beef Medallions on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. Two to three pan-seared, medium-rare beef medallions, featuring a golden-brown mustard crust, are arranged slightly overlapping. Next to the beef, a single golden-crisp, round potato roesti cake is positioned. A neat scoop of fluffy, slightly cheesy brown rice pilaf is placed opposite the beef and roesti. Fresh chopped parsley is sprinkled over the beef and rice, adding a pop of green. A light drizzle of rich pan jus glistens around the beef. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich browns, creamy whites, and earthy tones, with a subtle, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 400 ml beef broth and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

While rice cooks, peel and grate potatoes using a coarse grater. Squeeze out excess moisture from grated potatoes using a clean kitchen towel. In a bowl, combine grated potatoes with 50 g grated Gruyere, salt, and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Form potato mixture into four round or square roesti cakes. Place cakes in skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Set aside and keep warm.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Spread Dijon mustard evenly over all sides of each beef medallion.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add beef medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness. Remove beef from skillet and let rest on a cutting board.

In the same skillet, add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Deglaze with remaining 100 ml beef broth, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes to reduce slightly. This is your pan jus.
Stir remaining 50 g grated Gruyere into the cooked brown rice. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley.

To plate, place a scoop of cheesy brown rice pilaf on one side of each white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange two to three mustard-crusted beef medallions next to the rice. Place one crispy potato roesti cake on the plate. Drizzle pan jus over the beef. Garnish with remaining fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato-Mustard Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared golden-brown chicken breast is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy tomato-mustard sauce, flecked with tender diced onions and bright red tomato pieces, is generously spooned over and around the chicken. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh garnish. The dish presents a warm, inviting palette of golden-brown, reddish-orange, and lively green. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its beautifully seared crust. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting textures and colors within a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted small potatoes or rice pilaf to soak up the delicious sauce.
Accompany with steamed green beans or asparagus for a balanced meal.
Offer crusty baguette slices on the side.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and a crust forms. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Transfer seared chicken to a plate. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Add canned diced tomatoes (with their juice). Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the sauce to slightly reduce and thicken.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Return the seared chicken breasts to the pan. Spoon sauce over the chicken. Cook for an additional 3-5 minutes, ensuring chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through but remains juicy. Do not overcook.
This sauce is also excellent with pan-seared pork tenderloin medallions.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Chicken Breast with Mushroom, Cheddar, and Mustard Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown stuffed chicken breast is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, seared to a crisp exterior, is sliced into thick, substantial medallions, revealing a rich, creamy filling of earthy sautéed mushrooms and sweet caramelized onions melded with melted sharp cheddar cheese. A vibrant mound of bright green, tender-crisp steamed broccoli florets sits neatly beside the chicken. A glossy, amber-hued mustard-Worcestershire glaze is artfully drizzled over the chicken, adding a lustrous sheen. The dish is garnished with finely chopped fresh parsley, providing a pop of contrasting green. The arrangement is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. It rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin, bathed in natural, even lighting, conveying a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice mushrooms and onion finely.
Heat 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook until mushrooms release liquid and brown, about 8-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Stir in grated cheddar cheese into the mushroom mixture.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly to about 1 cm thickness.
Divide mushroom-cheddar mixture among chicken breasts. Place filling on one end. Roll tightly. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Season outside of stuffed chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

While chicken bakes, prepare the glaze. In a small saucepan, combine Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until sauce slightly thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Cut broccoli into florets. Steam or roast until tender-crisp.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Remove toothpicks.
Slice chicken into thick medallions. Arrange on plates with broccoli. Drizzle with mustard glaze. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chorizo and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Spicy Chorizo and Mushroom Pasta is presented in a classic white porcelain pasta bowl. Al dente rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, savory tomato-cream sauce, showcasing vibrant colors. Scattered throughout are thick, rustic chunks of seared chorizo, golden-brown and slightly crisp. Tender slices of earthy cremini mushrooms and vibrant red bell pepper strips are interspersed. A light sprinkling of finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley adds a bright green contrast. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese rests atop the pasta. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a standard fork are placed beside it. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting appeal in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
instructions: Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml of pasta water.

Remove casing from chorizo. Cut chorizo into thick, rustic chunks. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chorizo chunks. Sear until golden-brown and slightly crisp. Remove chorizo from pan; set aside. Leave rendered fat in pan.
Dice onion. Thinly slice bell peppers into strips. Slice mushrooms. Add onion, bell peppers, and mushrooms to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. This is your soffritto base.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream. Return chorizo chunks to the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Add cooked rigatoni to the sauce. Toss well to coat all pasta. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve hot, garnished with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust the amount of chorizo for desired spice level.
For a milder flavor, use a sweet Italian sausage instead of chorizo.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs are nestled amidst a rustic stew of vibrant red and yellow bell pepper chunks, diced tomatoes, and translucent onion pieces. The seared chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender meat. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to ingredients. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is organic, with moderate negative space. Chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. The plate rests on a light wooden table, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and silver flatware. A rustic ceramic bowl of crusty bread and a simple green salad are nearby, completing the casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Simple green salad

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks
Yellow bell pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper chunks. Cook for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken stock, oregano, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 30-40 minutes. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mascarpone Rice Pudding with Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy mascarpone rice pudding is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The pudding, cooked to a velvety, fluid consistency, has a soft, off-white hue. A vibrant, glossy mixed berry compote, gently simmered to release its natural sweetness, is elegantly dolloped atop the pudding, showcasing rich red and purple tones. Scattered lightly over the compote are golden, toasted slivered almonds, providing a delicate crunch. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the dish. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its smooth texture and contrasting colors, set against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Drain well.
Combine milk, heavy cream, sugar, vanilla bean, vanilla seeds, and salt in a heavy-bottomed saucepan.
Bring mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Add rinsed rice to the simmering liquid. Reduce heat to low.
Cook, stirring frequently, for 25-30 minutes. Rice should be tender and liquid absorbed, creating a creamy pudding.
Remove saucepan from heat. Stir in mascarpone cheese until fully incorporated and smooth.
Remove vanilla bean pod. Let pudding cool slightly.
For the berry compote, combine mixed berries and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes. Berries should soften and release juices, creating a light sauce.
Portion warm or chilled rice pudding into individual serving bowls.
Top each portion with a spoonful of berry compote.
Garnish with toasted slivered almonds before serving.
notes: The primary ingredients provided for the task were largely savory. As the dish type specified was 'dessert' with a 'sweet flavor profile', this recipe uses 'rice' and 'cheese' (mascarpone) from the provided list, supplemented with standard dessert ingredients to create a balanced sweet dish suitable for a restaurant setting.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Spicy Chicken with Peanuts and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sichuan Spicy Chicken with Peanuts and Rice is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, typical of a modern Chinese bistro. Steamed jasmine rice forms a pristine white base, gently mounded. The vibrant stir-fried chicken mixture is piled generously atop the rice. The chicken, cut into 2.5 cm cubes, is visibly tender with a glossy, dark brown sauce coating. Scattered among the chicken are bright red, slightly crinkled dried chili segments and whole, roasted unsalted peanuts, adding contrasting textures and colors. A light drizzle of the savory sauce slightly pools at the base of the chicken, hinting at the rich flavor. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of finely chopped green spring onion tops, providing a fresh, verdant contrast. The overall presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, showcasing the rich colors and textures of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a pair of dark chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with plain steamed rice
Chopsticks

ingredients.name: Dried red chilies (Sichuan Tianying or similar)
ingredients.quantity: 20-30 pieces, cut into 1.5 cm segments (remove some seeds for less heat)

ingredients.name: Spring onions
ingredients.quantity: 3 stalks, white and green parts separated, white parts thinly sliced, green parts chopped for garnish

instructions: Combine chicken cubes with marinade ingredients (Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, cornstarch, sesame oil). Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Whisk together all sauce ingredients (light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, Shaoxing wine, sugar, cornstarch, chicken stock or water) in a small bowl. Set aside.
Rinse jasmine rice. Cook according to package directions using a rice cooker or stovetop method. Keep warm.
Heat 60ml vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken to hot oil. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until chicken is browned and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add dried chili segments and Sichuan peppercorns (if using) to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant and chilies darken slightly. Do not burn.
Add minced garlic, minced ginger, and sliced white parts of spring onions. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked chicken to the wok.
Stir the prepared sauce again. Pour sauce into the wok. Stir quickly to coat chicken. Sauce will thicken rapidly.
Add roasted peanuts. Stir to combine.
Divide cooked jasmine rice among 4 bowls. Spoon Sichuan spicy chicken mixture over rice.
Garnish each serving with chopped green parts of spring onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust dried chili quantity to personal heat preference.
For more authentic 'mala' flavor, increase Sichuan peppercorns.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Aji de Gallina
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Peruvian Aji de Gallina is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, creamy mound of vibrant yellow Aji de Gallina, with visibly shredded chicken, occupies the center. Surrounding its base are neatly arranged, overlapping 1 cm thick rounds of boiled white potato. A scoop of fluffy white rice sits adjacent. The chicken is garnished with halved black olives scattered across its surface and two quartered hard-boiled eggs carefully placed on top. A small sprig of fresh cilantro adds green. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, a light grey cotton napkin, natural, even lighting, and a traditional Peruvian serving spoon beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with white rice and boiled potatoes as traditional accompaniments.
A simple side salad of lettuce and tomato often accompanies this dish.
Traditionally eaten with a fork and knife, sometimes with a spoon for the sauce.
instructions: Cook chicken breast in simmering water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Shred into fine pieces. Reserve 100 ml cooking liquid.
Soak bread slices in milk. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Aji Amarillo paste. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Transfer sautéed onion, garlic, and Aji Amarillo mixture to a blender. Add soaked bread and milk. Blend until smooth. Add reserved chicken liquid if too thick.
Return blended sauce to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in shredded chicken, ground pecans, and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Keep warm.
Meanwhile, boil potatoes until tender. Peel and slice into 1 cm thick rounds.
Cook white rice according to package instructions.

To serve, place a mound of Aji de Gallina in the center of each plate. Arrange sliced potatoes around the chicken. Place a scoop of white rice beside the chicken. Garnish with halved black olives, quartered hard-boiled eggs, and a sprig of fresh parsley or cilantro.
