notes: Aji Amarillo paste is a key ingredient; it provides the signature flavor and color. It can be found in Latin American markets.
For a richer sauce, use chicken broth instead of water to cook the chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cucumber & Peach Pasta Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Fermented Cucumber & Peach Pasta Cake rests slightly off-center on a smooth, light beige handcrafted ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals a tender, moist crumb with subtle flecks of pale green from the finely diced fermented cucumber and soft orange from the diced peaches. A delicate, almost unnoticeable texture from the finely chopped pasta is integrated into the crumb. On top of the slice, or artfully beside it, are a few very thin, curled strips of fresh cucumber peel, emphasizing zero-waste. The plate is on a light, natural-textured surface, possibly bamboo or reclaimed wood. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, natural lighting. In the blurred background, the remaining whole cake sits on a simple wooden board, showcasing its full form.

ingredients.name: Fine pasta (e.g., vermicelli), cooked al dente and finely chopped

instructions: Ferment Cucumbers: Combine water and 15g salt in a clean jar. Stir to dissolve. Add cucumber slices. Ensure cucumbers are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Check for desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Prepare Pasta: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain. Cool. Finely chop.
Prepare Peaches & Fermented Cucumber: Peel and dice peaches. Finely dice fermented cucumber.
Mix Dry Ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and 2g salt.
Mix Wet Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk together maple syrup, plant-based milk, oil, and vanilla extract.
Combine Batter: Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold In: Gently fold in chopped pasta, diced peaches, and diced fermented cucumber.
Bake: Pour batter into a greased and floured 20 cm round cake tin. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 30-35 minutes. Or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool: Let cake cool in tin for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack. Cool completely.
Serve: Slice. Garnish with fresh cucumber peels or thin cucumber slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Eggplant
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin crisped to a deep golden-brown, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are substantial chunks of roasted eggplant, sweet red bell pepper, and halved cherry tomatoes, each vegetable exhibiting a tender, slightly caramelized exterior. The eggplant pieces are soft and slightly browned, while the bell pepper and tomatoes are vibrant in color. A light, glistening pan sauce, infused with herbs, pools subtly around the base of the chicken and vegetables. The dish is finished with a scattering of crumbled white feta cheese, adding bright contrast, and fresh green oregano leaves. A lemon wedge sits beside the chicken. The overall presentation is balanced, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve with a simple green salad
Serve with a side of couscous or rice
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut eggplant into 3 cm chunks. Cut red bell pepper into 3 cm pieces. Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut red onion into wedges.
Toss eggplant, bell pepper, tomatoes, and onion with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a large baking sheet. Spread in a single layer.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes. Stir halfway. Vegetables should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Add minced garlic, half the fresh oregano, and half the fresh thyme to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes.
Stir remaining fresh oregano and thyme into the pan sauce. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon.
Plate roasted vegetables. Place one chicken thigh on top of or beside vegetables.
Spoon pan sauce over chicken and vegetables.
Crumble feta cheese over the dish. Garnish with a lemon wedge.
notes: Adjust seasoning to taste throughout cooking.
For crispier chicken skin, ensure chicken is very dry before searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Sour Cream Panna Cotta with Strawberry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy white sour cream panna cotta is elegantly unmolded onto a round, clean white porcelain dessert plate. Its smooth, jiggly texture is visible. Adjacent to the panna cotta, a vibrant red strawberry compote is generously spooned, showcasing small, soft strawberry pieces. The compote's natural juices create a glossy sheen. A single, fresh green mint sprig is delicately placed on the compote, adding a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space on the plate, highlighting the dessert. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and natural, even lighting from above, creating a clean, inviting restaurant-style ambiance.
instructions: Sprinkle gelatin powder over cold water in a small bowl. Let bloom for 5 minutes.
Combine heavy cream and 60 g sugar in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat until sugar dissolves and cream is hot but not boiling.
Remove from heat. Add bloomed gelatin to the hot cream mixture. Stir until fully dissolved.
Stir in vanilla extract. Let mixture cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Whisk sour cream into the cream mixture until smooth and fully incorporated.
Pour the panna cotta mixture evenly into four 150 ml ramekins or molds.
Cover each ramekin with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or until set.
For the strawberry compote: Wash and hull strawberries. Cut strawberries into small cubes.
Combine cubed strawberries, 30 g sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until strawberries soften and release their juices. Mash lightly with a fork for desired consistency. Cool compote completely.
To serve: Dip the bottom of each ramekin briefly in warm water. Invert panna cotta onto a clean white porcelain dessert plate.
Spoon a generous portion of cooled strawberry compote alongside the panna cotta.
Garnish each plate with a fresh mint sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cucumber & Semolina Delight
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of the Fermented Cucumber & Semolina Delight is plated on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, placed on a light reclaimed wood surface. The cake slice, with its golden-brown crust and subtly textured crumb, reveals tiny specks of pale green fermented cucumber within. A thin, translucent glaze, hinting at the cucumber's tang, coats the top. A few small, translucent slices of fermented Japanese cucumber are artfully arranged on the plate beside the cake, emphasizing the hero ingredient. The entire 20 cm round cake, with its rustic, wholesome appearance, sits on a simple wooden cake stand in the background, out of focus. The setting features a natural beige undyed linen napkin, a minimal background with soft, natural light, and a hint of green foliage from a potted plant. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing the natural beauty of the ingredients and the cake's texture to be the focal point, with ample white space around the dish, highlighting its sustainable approach.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled with a cup of unsweetened herbal tea.
Offer small individual portions as a light, refreshing dessert.
instructions: Prepare fermented cucumbers: Wash cucumbers. Slice into 5 mm thick rounds. Place in a clean jar.
Make brine: Dissolve 10 g sea salt in 500 ml filtered water. Pour over cucumbers. Ensure cucumbers are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Ferment cucumbers: Seal jar. Keep at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Check for small bubbles. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.
Preheat oven: Set oven to 180°C (fan assisted 160°C). Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake tin.
Combine wet ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together plant-based milk, oil, 150 g granulated sugar, and lemon zest.
Combine dry ingredients: In a separate bowl, mix semolina, baking powder, and 1 g salt.
Combine wet and dry: Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Whisk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in cucumbers: Gently fold in 100 g of finely diced fermented cucumber into the batter.
Bake cake: Pour batter into prepared cake tin. Bake for 30-35 minutes. Or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake: Remove cake from oven. Let cool in tin for 10 minutes. Then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare glaze: In a small saucepan, combine 50 ml of fermented cucumber brine with 30 ml lemon juice. Add 50 g granulated sugar. Heat gently until sugar dissolves.
Glaze cake: Once cake is cool, pour glaze evenly over the top. Garnish with remaining fermented cucumber slices or small pieces.
notes: Adjust sugar in glaze based on desired sweetness and tanginess of fermented cucumbers.
For zero-waste, any remaining cucumber brine can be used in salad dressings or marinades.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roast Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Garlic Herb Roast Chicken and Potatoes rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with subtle imperfections. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh is placed prominently, accompanied by several thick, rustic chunks of roasted potatoes. The potatoes display golden, slightly crisp exteriors and tender, fluffy interiors. Softened, caramelized garlic cloves and wedges of roasted onion are scattered naturally among the main components. Natural pan drippings lightly coat the ingredients, providing a rich sheen. A few small sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme are casually placed on top. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural light from a nearby kitchen window. A simple, casually folded cloth napkin and standard metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Serve with crusty bread for soaking up pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, onion wedges, smashed garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme leaves, and olive oil. Toss well to coat. Season with salt and black pepper.
Arrange chicken and potato mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 40-50 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden brown.
Serve immediately.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade, Kimchi Reduction, Basil Oil, Soy Spheres
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick, perfectly seared chicken roulade medallion rests centrally on a large, pristine white bone china plate. Its golden-brown crust contrasts with the subtle texture of the plate. A vibrant green basil oil is artfully streaked across one side of the chicken. Adjacent, a small, deep red pool of glistening kimchi reduction provides a contrasting color accent. Three translucent, dark soy sauce spheres are precisely placed beside the reduction, ready to burst with umami. A delicate, dark, lacy hijiki crisp stands upright, leaning against the chicken, adding a subtle textural and visual element. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist composition. The plate sits on a polished dark wood surface, subtly reflecting light. A single, elegant pair of dark lacquered chopsticks rests beside the plate. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision.
instructions: Soy Sauce Spheres: Dissolve 5g calcium chloride in 500ml distilled water. Set aside. Blend 100ml soy sauce with 5g sodium alginate until smooth. Let mixture rest 30 minutes to degas. Using a syringe or dropper, carefully drop soy mixture into calcium bath. Allow spheres to form for 2 minutes. Gently remove spheres with a slotted spoon. Rinse thoroughly in fresh water. Store in a small amount of fresh water.

Basil Oil: Bring small pot of water to boil. Blanch 50g basil leaves for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze excess water from basil. Blend blanched basil with 150ml neutral oil and pinch of salt until smooth. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth.

Kimchi Reduction: Finely chop 200g drained kimchi. Sauté in a small pot for 2 minutes. Add 100ml clear chicken stock, 15ml rice vinegar, and 5g sugar. Simmer 10 minutes. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Return liquid to pot. Reduce by half. Mix 5g cornstarch with 15ml cold water to form a slurry. Whisk slurry into simmering kimchi liquid. Cook until thickened to a light glaze consistency.

Hijiki Crisps: Rehydrate 10g dried hijiki seaweed in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain very well. Pat dry with paper towels. Spread hijiki in a very thin layer on a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 100°C for 45-60 minutes, or until completely crisp and brittle. Cool.

Chicken Roulade: Pound four 200g chicken breasts to 1cm thickness. Finely mince 100g shiitake mushrooms, 50g spring onions, and 1 garlic clove. Grate 5g ginger. Sauté minced shiitake, spring onion, garlic, and ginger in a pan for 5 minutes. Add 15ml soy sauce. Cook until liquid evaporates. Cool filling completely. Spread cooled filling evenly over each pounded chicken breast. Roll each breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks. Vacuum seal each roulade. Cook sous-vide at 70°C for 1.5 hours. Immediately transfer to ice bath to chill. Remove twine/toothpicks. Pat dry. Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades 3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Rest roulades for 5 minutes. Slice each roulade into three thick medallions.
notes: This recipe utilizes advanced culinary techniques such as sous-vide cooking for precise temperature control, reverse spherification for molecular gastronomy elements, and careful reduction for intense flavor concentration. Precision and timing are key for optimal results and presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Stroganoff
recipes.visual_description: A generous, home-style single portion of Beef and Mushroom Stroganoff rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. Tender, browned beef chunks, cut into 2-3 cm pieces, are nestled within a creamy, light brown sauce. Sliced cremini mushrooms, sautéed to a rich golden hue, are interspersed throughout. The sauce has a smooth, inviting texture. Adjacent to the stroganoff, a neat mound of golden egg noodles provides a comforting contrast. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a touch of freshness. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a plain fork placed beside it. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene. The overall presentation is hearty and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve traditionally with egg noodles or rice.

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin or chuck, cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Cut beef into 2-3 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd pan. Remove beef from pan.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter to the pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms from pan.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over the onion mixture. Stir for 1 minute to cook the flour.
Gradually whisk in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Return seared beef and sautéed mushrooms to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until beef is tender.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in sour cream. Do not boil after adding sour cream. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Meanwhile, cook egg noodles or rice according to package directions.
Serve hot stroganoff over cooked noodles or rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Ballotine with Basil Emulsion, Hijiki Crème, and Soy Spheres

selected_ingredients.name: chicken
selected_ingredients.comment: removed vein, prepared filled, and rolled

recipes.visual_description: A thick medallion of golden-seared chicken ballotine, cut from a perfectly cooked roll, anchors the pristine white bone china plate. It rests slightly off-center. Adjacent to it, a sweeping, organic smear of deep charcoal-grey hijiki crème provides an earthy foundation. Three precisely placed dots of vibrant emerald-green basil oil punctuate the negative space, reflecting light. One or two translucent amber soy sauce spheres, resembling precious pearls, are delicately placed near the chicken. A minuscule, perfectly cut cube of vibrant red kimchi adds a sharp, contrasting accent. Abundant white space surrounds the composition. The plate is set on a premium grey-veined Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, focused overhead lighting creating soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, and minimalist silver flatware complete the sophisticated, uncluttered scene.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Ballotine: Butterfly each chicken breast. Pound gently to even thickness (approx. 1 cm). Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Make Chicken Mousse: Blend chicken thigh meat, egg white, and 50g minced kimchi in a food processor until smooth. Slowly add chilled heavy cream until a smooth mousse forms. Season with salt.
Fill and Roll Ballotine: Spread an even layer of chicken mousse onto each flattened chicken breast. Roll tightly into a cylinder. Tie securely with kitchen twine at 2 cm intervals.
Sous Vide Chicken: Vacuum-seal each ballotine. Cook in a sous vide bath at 63°C for 1 hour 30 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Ice Bath Chicken: Transfer cooked ballotines immediately to an ice bath for 15 minutes. This stops cooking and sets the shape.

Make Basil Oil: Blanch basil leaves in boiling salted water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend basil with grapeseed oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth. Season with salt. Set aside.

Make Hijiki Crème: Rehydrate dried hijiki seaweed in warm water for 15 minutes. Drain thoroughly. Sauté hijiki in a small pot with butter for 2 minutes. Add dashi stock. Simmer until liquid is reduced by half. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Stir in a tablespoon of cream. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Soy Spheres: Dissolve sodium alginate in 50ml distilled water using an immersion blender. Let stand for 1 hour to remove air bubbles. Mix soy sauce with a pinch of xanthan gum (optional, for stability). Using a syringe or squeeze bottle, carefully drop soy sauce into the calcium chloride solution. Let spheres set for 2 minutes. Rinse gently in plain water. Store in a small amount of soy sauce.
Prepare Kimchi Garnish: Finely dice the remaining 20g aged kimchi into 2mm cubes.
Sear Chicken: Remove ballotines from bags. Pat dry thoroughly. Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear ballotines until golden brown and crisp on all sides. Rest for 5 minutes.

Slice and Plate: Remove twine from ballotines. Slice each ballotine into two thick medallions. Arrange one medallion slightly off-center on each plate. Create a sweeping smear of hijiki crème. Dot basil oil around the plate. Place two soy spheres near the chicken. Add a tiny, precise cube of kimchi as a garnish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents seared boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into generous 5cm chunks, coated in a rich, creamy sauce. The golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled amongst vibrant green wilted spinach and ruby-red sun-dried tomato halves. The sauce, a harmonious blend of cream and Parmesan, gently clings to all components, showcasing a velvety texture. Garnished with fresh chopped Italian parsley, the dish offers a delightful contrast of colors and textures. It is served in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting, rustic elegance. A single portion is thoughtfully arranged with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve alongside a simple green salad.
Serve over pasta, such as tagliatelle or penne.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut each thigh into 2-3 large chunks (approx. 5cm pieces). Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in heavy cream and dried oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked chicken pieces to the pan. Toss to coat them in the creamy sauce. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Pork & Corn Pasta with Fermented Celery Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Pork & Corn Pasta is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a wide, shallow rim, resting on a light, reclaimed wood table. The pasta, such as fusilli, is tossed with golden-brown smoked pork chunks, bright yellow corn kernels, and translucent diced onion and celery. The dish has an inviting, rustic yet refined appearance. Nestled among the pasta are small, pale green pieces of fermented celery relish, adding a fresh, tangy contrast. A few vibrant green fresh celery inner leaves are scattered over the top as a natural garnish. The overall color palette is warm and earthy, with pops of yellow and green. Textures are varied: al dente pasta, tender pork, slightly crisp corn, and the delicate crunch of the relish. The composition is organic and unforced, with ample white space around the food. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting its natural textures. A simple, natural wood fork rests beside the bowl on a subtly textured undyed linen napkin.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Celery Relish: Wash and thinly slice 2 celery stalks. Combine water and non-iodized salt to make brine. Submerge sliced celery in brine in a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly tangy. Refrigerate.
Cut smoked pork belly into 1.5 cm chunks. Dice onion and remaining celery stalks into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic. Reserve celery inner leaves for garnish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add smoked pork chunks. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove pork with a slotted spoon. Set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pan.
Add diced onion and celery to the pan with rendered fat. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add corn kernels to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender. Deglaze with white wine. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer gently while pasta cooks.
Cook pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Add cooked pasta, reserved smoked pork, and 60 ml of pasta cooking water to the vegetable and corn mixture in the pan. Toss to combine. If too dry, add more pasta water.
Stir in 2-3 tablespoons of the prepared Fermented Celery Relish. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with reserved fresh celery inner leaves and additional fermented celery relish as desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes rests on an everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken drumsticks, with crispy, crackled skin, are positioned naturally beside a generous pile of thick-cut, golden-brown roasted potato wedges. The potatoes show a slightly crispy exterior and tender interior, some edges lightly charred. Scattered among the potatoes and chicken are a few wilted rosemary and thyme sprigs and roasted garlic cloves. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple cloth napkin and standard flatware nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken pieces. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges, about 2-3 cm thick.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, olive oil, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken pieces and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip potatoes once during cooking.
Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Pork & Corn Pasta with Fermented Celery Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Pork & Corn Pasta is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a wide, shallow rim, resting on a light, reclaimed wood table. The pasta, such as fusilli, is tossed with golden-brown smoked pork chunks, bright yellow corn kernels, and translucent diced onion and celery. The dish has an inviting, rustic yet refined appearance. Nestled among the pasta are small, pale green pieces of fermented celery relish, adding a fresh, tangy contrast. recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Steaks with Garlic Herb Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef steak is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The steak, a thick, rich brown cut, retains its robust shape, showcasing a perfectly seared crust and succulent interior. Adjacent to the steak are vibrant green asparagus spears, roasted to a tender-crisp texture. A generous dollop of creamy, pale yellow garlic herb butter, flecked with dark green rosemary and thyme, melts gently atop the warm beef, creating small rivulets of glistening richness. The plate features thoughtful negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare beef: Pat steaks dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.
Roast asparagus: Toss asparagus with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Make garlic herb butter: In a small bowl, combine softened butter, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme leaves. Mix well.
Sear beef: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add steaks. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness.
Finish steaks: Remove steaks from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Serve: Top each steak with a generous dollop of garlic herb butter. Serve immediately with roasted asparagus.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Braised Chicken with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single portion of rustic braised chicken on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A single, whole braised chicken thigh, rich golden-brown from searing and deeply tender, rests prominently on a bed of fluffy, earthy brown rice. The chicken is generously coated with a rich, reddish-orange tomato sauce, studded with visible diced carrots and onions, showcasing a hearty texture. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A simple set of traditional flatware and a folded cotton napkin are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting textures against a softly blurred, casual restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to soak up the flavorful sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a refreshing accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through.

While chicken braises, cook brown rice according to package instructions. Typically, combine 250g brown rice with 500ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from heat. Stir in the chopped fresh basil.
Serve braised chicken pieces hot over a bed of brown rice, spooning generous amounts of the rustic tomato sauce over the chicken and rice. Garnish with additional fresh basil leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Chicken and Vegetable Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The stew is thick, filling the bowl, showcasing large, irregular chunks of seared chicken. Tender diced potatoes, vibrant orange carrot slices, bright green broccoli florets, and earthy brown mushroom slices are visibly suspended in the rich, opaque cream sauce. The chicken pieces are golden-brown, contrasting with the paler sauce. Vegetables retain their distinct shapes and natural colors. Fresh, chopped green parsley is sprinkled on top. The bowl sits on a well-used, light brown wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. Warm, inviting lighting suggests a cozy kitchen. A standard metal spoon rests beside the bowl. The background is softly blurred, indicating a lived-in family kitchen.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks (3cm). Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Stir until smooth and thickened.
Add diced potatoes (2cm cubes), sliced carrots (1.5cm slices), dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until potatoes and carrots are tender.
Add broccoli florets and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in heavy cream. Heat through, do not boil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Discard bay leaf. Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Jalfrezi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Jalfrezi served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features large, moist 3cm chunks of seared chicken coated in a thick, vibrant red-orange tomato gravy. Interspersed with the meat are 2cm squares of softened yellow onion and bright red tomato wedges that maintain their structure. Long, slender green chili halves provide a vertical element. The sauce has a glossy, rich texture. A generous garnish of freshly chopped green cilantro is scattered over the top. The plate is set on a light wood bistro table. A small side bowl of fluffy white basmati rice and a piece of charred naan bread are placed naturally beside the plate. Even, natural light highlights the textures of the sauce and the sear on the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with steamed long-grain basmati rice
Provide a side of cooling cucumber raita
Include a fresh lime wedge and sliced red onion salad

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, cut into 3cm chunks
Yellow onions (1 finely diced, 1 cut into 2cm squares)

instructions: Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add cumin seeds and fry until they sizzle.
Add diced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in garlic and ginger paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Stir in turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Pour in tomato puree. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add onion squares, tomato wedges, and slit green chilies.
Stir-fry for 3 minutes until vegetables soften but retain shape.
Sprinkle with garam masala and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the diced onions are well-browned for a deep base flavor.
Do not overcook the onion squares and tomato wedges at the end; they should remain distinct.
Use Kashmiri chili powder for vibrant color without excessive heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade with Kimchi Purée and Soy Glaze

selected_ingredients.name: chicken
selected_ingredients.comment: removed vein, prepared filled, and rolled

recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a wide-rimmed, pristine white bone china plate, artfully utilizing abundant negative space. Three thick-cut chicken roulade medallions, showcasing the vibrant green basil and dark hijiki filling, are arranged in a natural, slightly overlapping curve. Each medallion boasts a golden-brown, seared exterior. Beside the chicken, a precise quenelle of smooth, fiery red kimchi purée adds a striking color contrast and creamy texture. A lustrous, dark soy glaze is artfully drizzled across the plate, connecting the elements with a rich sheen. Bright emerald green basil oil is delicately dotted around the composition, offering aromatic freshness and visual pop. The presentation is minimalist, emphasizing the quality of ingredients and precision of execution. A folded white linen napkin and subtle, high-quality flatware complement the elegant setting.
instructions: Rehydrate hijiki: Place dried hijiki in warm water for 15 minutes. Drain thoroughly. Squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop.
Prepare chicken: Butterfly each chicken breast. Place between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly to 0.5 cm thickness. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Prepare basil filling: Finely chop 30g of fresh basil leaves. In a small bowl, combine chopped basil and chopped hijiki.
Fill and roll chicken: Place a portion of basil-hijiki mixture on one end of each pounded chicken breast. Roll tightly into a cylinder. Secure with butcher's twine.

Sear chicken: Preheat oven to 180°C. Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to oven. Roast 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes before slicing.

Prepare kimchi purée: Sauté minced shallot and garlic in 15ml olive oil until fragrant. Add kimchi. Cook 5 minutes. Add 50ml chicken stock. Simmer 10 minutes. Transfer to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-smooth consistency. Season with salt.

Prepare soy glaze: In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, mirin, remaining 100ml chicken stock, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until mixture thickens to a syrupy consistency, about 10-15 minutes. Stir in butter until melted and glossy.

Prepare basil oil: Blanch remaining 20g basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 15ml olive oil until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for clear oil.

Plate the dish: Slice each chicken roulade into three thick medallions. Arrange three medallions on each plate. Place a quenelle of kimchi purée beside the chicken. Drizzle soy glaze artfully around and over the chicken. Dot basil oil around the plate. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Thit Kho Mang (Braised Pork Belly with Bamboo Shoots)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thit Kho Mang is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Generous chunks of braised pork belly, approximately 3-4 cm cubes, are nestled among thick, tender slices of bamboo shoot, about 1 cm thick. The pork belly boasts a rich, glossy dark brown hue from the caramelized sugar and braising liquid. The bamboo shoots are a lighter, muted beige, absorbing the savory sauce. A thick, dark, glossy sauce coats all elements. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of freshly ground black pepper, a few thin, bright green slices of fresh bird's eye chili, and a small sprig of fresh cilantro leaves. The bowl is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A small, pristine white rice bowl with fluffy steamed jasmine rice and dark wooden chopsticks are arranged beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed jasmine rice
Often accompanied by a side of pickled vegetables (dưa giá)
instructions: Cut pork belly into 3-4 cm cubes.
Boil pork belly in water for 5 minutes. Drain. Rinse pork under cold water.
Heat 30g sugar in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Cook until sugar melts and turns deep amber caramel. Do not burn.
Add pork belly to caramel. Stir to coat.
Add minced shallots and garlic. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add 80ml fish sauce, 15g sugar, and 5g black pepper. Stir well.
Pour in 500ml coconut water. Bring to a boil.
Add bamboo shoots. Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until pork is very tender and sauce thickens. Stir occasionally.
Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced chilies and cilantro if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Almond Date Greek Yogurt Parfait
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented in a clear, elegant dessert glass, revealing distinct layers. Thick, creamy white Greek yogurt forms the base, contrasting with finely diced, dark brown Medjool dates. Above, golden-roasted slivered almonds, lightly glazed with honey, add a textural crunch. The parfait is topped with a final layer of yogurt, artfully drizzled with amber honey, allowing some to cascade. A few whole honey-roasted almonds and small date pieces garnish the top. The glass sits on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, with moderate negative space. A slender, polished metal spoon rests beside it. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dessert's refined textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side of traditional shortbread biscuits
Garnish with a fresh mint sprig for color and aroma
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Spread slivered almonds on a baking tray.
Drizzle 20 ml of honey over almonds. Add a pinch of salt. Toss to coat.
Roast almonds for 8-10 minutes. Stir halfway. Almonds should be golden and fragrant. Cool completely.
Finely dice pitted Medjool dates.
In a bowl, combine Greek yogurt with vanilla extract. Mix until smooth.
Divide Greek yogurt mixture into four clear dessert glasses.
Layer diced dates over yogurt in each glass.
Layer roasted almonds over dates.
Repeat layers: yogurt, dates, almonds.
Drizzle remaining honey over the top of each parfait.
Serve immediately or chill until ready to serve.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Eggplant Tagine
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl, reminiscent of a tagine base. Generous chunks of deeply browned chicken are nestled among soft, tender eggplant wedges. A rich, thick, reddish-brown sauce coats all components, glistening under natural light. Specks of vibrant green chopped cilantro and parsley are scattered over the top, providing fresh contrast. Thin slices of bright yellow preserved lemon rind peek through, adding a pop of color. The composition is organic and abundant, showcasing the stew-like nature of the dish. Each chicken piece retains its full shape. The eggplant pieces are visibly soft but hold their wedge form. The scene includes a simple wooden table, a white porcelain dinner plate, and a cotton napkin beside the bowl, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy couscous
Serve with crusty Moroccan bread for dipping
Offer harissa on the side for those who prefer more heat
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or tagine base over medium-high heat.
Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear chicken in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, ginger, and cinnamon stick. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add eggplant cut into 3-4 cm wedges, crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, preserved lemon slices (pulp removed, rind thinly sliced), and pitted green olives. Stir well.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and eggplant is soft. Stir occasionally.
Remove cinnamon stick. Stir in chopped fresh cilantro and parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
The preserved lemon adds unique tang and saltiness; adjust salt in the recipe accordingly.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper, Onion, and Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. Roasted bell pepper chunks (red, yellow, orange), red onion wedges, and halved Roma tomatoes are loosely piled in the center. The vegetables show tender, slightly charred edges and retain their vibrant, natural colors. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered over the top, interspersed with bright green chopped fresh parsley or basil leaves. A light sheen of vinaigrette coats the vegetables. The presentation is natural and unpretentious, as if served directly from a family kitchen. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A casually folded plain cloth napkin and simple, everyday fork are placed beside the plate. The scene is lit with warm, inviting light, suggesting a cozy home environment. Portions are generous, filling the plate without overcrowding.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the flavorful dressing.
Pair with a glass of simple table wine or water.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place bell pepper chunks, onion wedges, and tomato halves/quarters on a large baking tray.
Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Sprinkle with 5 ml dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Toss to coat vegetables evenly.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Vegetables should be tender and slightly charred at the edges.
Remove from oven. Let vegetables cool slightly on the tray.
While vegetables cool, prepare dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml extra virgin olive oil, 30 ml red wine vinegar, 5 ml Dijon mustard (if using), 2 ml dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
Transfer roasted vegetables to a large serving bowl.
Add crumbled feta cheese and chopped fresh parsley or basil.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: This salad can be served warm, at room temperature, or chilled.
Adjust the amount of dressing to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. Two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs, left whole, are nestled within a rich, rustic tomato and olive sauce. The sauce, a vibrant deep red, showcases visible diced onion and halved dark Kalamata olives, creating a satisfyingly chunky texture. Bright green, fresh torn basil leaves are scattered generously over the chicken and sauce, providing a fresh, aromatic contrast. The dish is naturally arranged, allowing the sauce to pool around the succulent chicken. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to dip in the sauce.
Serve alongside polenta or pasta.
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden. Remove chicken from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, olives, and chopped oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Cover and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Uncover. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes to slightly thicken sauce, if desired.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh torn basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Mushroom Rice Pot
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of the Hearty Chicken and Mushroom Rice Pot is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, comforting appeal. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its skin slightly crispy, rests prominently on a bed of savory, reddish-brown rice. The rice is studded with tender, earthy quartered cremini mushrooms, softened diced yellow onions, and bright red minced chili. The texture is moist and cohesive. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast to the deep, warm tones. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, beside a cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the steam. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant setting.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.quantity: a small bunch, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in quartered mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown.
Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir for 1 minute to coat rice grains.
Pour in hot beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Carefully return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Cover the skillet tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A modest, homely portion of penne pasta is casually piled in a rustic, round, off-white ceramic bowl, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange sauce, with visible pieces of finely diced onion, minced garlic, and thin slices of dark red sun-dried tomatoes interspersed throughout. A light dusting of grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the top. The sauce has a comforting, slightly glossy texture, clinging well to the penne. The overall presentation is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a simple, comforting home-cooked meal. A plain metal fork is placed beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen setting.
instructions: Cook penne pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Before draining, reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, prepare the sauce. Drain sun-dried tomatoes and slice them thinly. Mince garlic. Finely dice the onion.
Heat butter and olive oil in a large deep pan or skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown the garlic.
Stir in sliced sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Pour in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Add grated Parmigiano Reggiano to the sauce. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Add the drained pasta to the sauce. Toss well to coat all pasta evenly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Continue tossing for 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh torn basil leaves and an extra sprinkle of grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Garlic Chicken with Mushroom Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige tone, placed on a light bamboo table surface. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene. A single serving occupies the center, leaving ample white space. The mushroom-rice pilaf forms a natural mound, its grains distinct and earthy brown, flecked with sautéed mushrooms and finely diced onion. Beside the pilaf, two thick, golden-brown chicken chunks are arranged, showing a beautiful sear and natural shape; they are not sliced. A vibrant dollop of rustic roasted tomato-bell pepper compote, with visible pieces of softened red bell pepper and tomato, sits adjacent, adding a warm, rich color contrast. The overall composition is clean and unforced, emphasizing the natural textures and colors of each ingredient. A sprig of fresh thyme or a small, vibrant edible flower petal offers a subtle, natural garnish. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural plant greenery. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige and simple, clean flatware complete the eco-conscious table setting.

ingredients.name: Fermented garlic paste
ingredients.quantity: 20g (or 2 minced fresh garlic cloves + 5ml apple cider vinegar)

instructions: Cut chicken into 4 large chunks.
In a bowl, combine chicken chunks with 2 crushed garlic cloves, fermented garlic paste (or alternative), 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve tomatoes, cut bell pepper into large strips, and cut half onion into wedges. Toss with 10ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and herb sprigs on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Transfer roasted tomatoes, bell pepper, and onion wedges to a small saucepan (discard herb sprigs). Mash gently to a rustic consistency. Simmer over low heat for 5-7 minutes. Keep warm.
Finely dice the remaining half onion. Slice mushrooms.
Heat 5ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and sliced mushrooms to the saucepan. Sauté until mushrooms are softened and liquid has evaporated, about 7-10 minutes.

Stir in brown rice. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork. Season with salt and pepper.
While pilaf cooks, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken chunks. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
notes: Source local, seasonal ingredients for best flavor and sustainability.
Utilize chicken bones for homemade stock to minimize waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Italian Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl on a rustic wooden table. Orecchiette pasta shells are tossed with 3cm irregular chunks of seared Italian sausage and vibrant green broccoli rabe florets. Small wedges of red bell pepper and sliced cremini mushrooms provide color contrast. Julienned sun-dried tomatoes add flecks of deep crimson. The sauce is a light, translucent emulsion of olive oil and garlic, coating each ingredient with a gentle sheen. A dusting of coarse, golden-brown toasted breadcrumbs and fresh oregano leaves is concentrated in the center. The arrangement is natural and organic, showing balanced portions with visible negative space around the inner rim of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Primitivo or Negroamaro wine
Provide extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
instructions: Bring 4 liters of heavily salted water to a boil.
Blanch broccoli rabe for 2 minutes until bright green. Remove and shock in ice water. Drain and chop into 5cm pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a pan. Add breadcrumbs and half the oregano. Toast until golden and crisp. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat 20ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Break sausage into 3cm chunks and sear until browned.
Add mushrooms and bell peppers to the skillet. Sauté for 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, and chili flakes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Boil orecchiette in the same water used for broccoli rabe until al dente.
Reserve 150ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.
Add pasta and broccoli rabe to the skillet. Pour in reserved pasta water and remaining olive oil.
Toss vigorously over high heat for 1 minute to emulsify the sauce.
Season with salt and remaining oregano.
Divide into four bowls and top with toasted breadcrumbs.
notes: Do not overcook the broccoli rabe during the blanching stage to maintain its snap
Use high-quality bronze-die pasta for better sauce adhesion

recipes.recipe_name: Scallion Ginger Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of Scallion Ginger Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The chicken, cut into thick, irregular chunks, is coated in a glossy, savory, light brown sauce. Visible within the sauce are small, translucent diced onion pieces, finely minced ginger, and tiny bits of minced garlic. Bright green slices of scallion tops are generously scattered over the chicken, with some white scallion pieces mixed into the dish, providing a fresh contrast. A few thin, diagonal slices of red chili add subtle pops of color. The components are naturally piled in the center of the plate, allowing some of the rich sauce to pool slightly at the base. The overall plating is casual and homely, with components touching and overlapping. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside the main plate, a small, plain white ceramic rice bowl holds a modest mound of fluffy white rice. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests casually on the table next to the rice bowl. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy lighting, mimicking a comfortable family kitchen, with a softly blurred, lived-in background that suggests a relaxed dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice.
Offer a simple clear soup or a side of stir-fried green vegetables.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm thick chunks. In a bowl, combine chicken with 15ml soy sauce, 15ml Shaoxing wine, 15g cornstarch, 5ml sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Mix well. Let marinate for 15 minutes.
Prepare aromatics: Slice scallions into 2 cm pieces, separating white and green parts. Mince ginger finely. Mince garlic. Dice onion. Thinly slice red chili.

Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken chunks. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from the wok and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok if needed. Add diced onion, minced ginger, minced garlic, and sliced chili. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth, 30ml soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar. Bring the sauce to a simmer.

In a small bowl, whisk together 15g cornstarch and 30ml water to create a slurry. Slowly pour the slurry into the simmering sauce, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens to your desired consistency.
Return the cooked chicken chunks to the wok. Add the white parts of the sliced scallions. Toss to coat the chicken evenly with the sauce.
Serve immediately, garnished generously with the green parts of the scallions.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.
Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Roasted Chicken and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Skillet Roasted Chicken and Bell Peppers is centered on a round, rustic ceramic dinner plate with a cream glaze. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, cooked to perfection, is the focal point, its skin lightly crisped. Surrounding the chicken are substantial, irregularly cut chunks of vibrant red, yellow, and orange bell peppers and soft, caramelized onion wedges, showcasing slight browning and tender textures. The arrangement is natural and informal, as if just served from the skillet. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color. The plate rests on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin and basic metal flatware are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Serve with crusty bread for dipping in pan juices
Serve with a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken evenly with salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, and dried oregano.
Cut bell peppers into thick 2.5 cm chunks. Cut onion into thick wedges. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken thighs to the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add bell pepper chunks and onion wedges to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened and lightly browned.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour chicken broth into the skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Arrange them among the vegetables.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove skillet from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve directly from the skillet or plate individual portions.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken with Roasted Eggplant and Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Chicken with Roasted Eggplant and Tomato-Basil Sauce is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown seared chicken thighs are positioned slightly off-center. They rest partially submerged in a rich, vibrant red tomato-basil sauce. Scattered around the chicken and within the sauce are tender, roasted eggplant cubes, their skins a deep purple and interiors soft. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully placed on top of the chicken and sauce. A light dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese adds a delicate finish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a light, natural wooden table surface. A neatly folded cream-colored cotton napkin and a simple silver fork and knife are placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut eggplant into 2.5 cm cubes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread eggplant on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Eggplant should be tender and lightly browned.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes. Cook until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
While chicken cooks, finely dice onion. Mince garlic.
In the same skillet (or a clean pot), add a splash more oil if needed. Sauté diced onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Cook until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes. Sauce should thicken slightly.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the sauce. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Add roasted eggplant to the sauce. Gently stir to combine.
Nestle cooked chicken thighs into the sauce. Simmer briefly for 2-3 minutes to warm through.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Almond Date Yogurt Parfait
recipes.visual_description: A single Honey-Almond Date Yogurt Parfait is presented in a clear glass tumbler on a well-used light wooden kitchen table. The parfait shows distinct, natural layers: thick plain Greek yogurt, finely chopped Medjool dates, and golden-brown toasted slivered almonds. The arrangement is casual, with a final scattering of almonds and a glistening drizzle of amber honey on top. Textures are varied: smooth yogurt, soft chewy dates, crunchy almonds. Colors are natural: creamy white, deep brown, golden-beige. The tumbler sits on a simple, slightly chipped off-white ceramic plate. A loosely folded beige linen napkin rests nearby. Warm, soft kitchen light creates a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Spread slivered almonds on a baking tray.
Toast almonds for 5-7 minutes until golden. Watch closely to prevent burning. Let cool.
Finely chop pitted dates.
In a medium bowl, combine Greek yogurt, 30ml honey, vanilla extract, and salt. Stir well until smooth.
Divide yogurt mixture into four clear glass tumblers or small bowls.
Layer chopped dates over the yogurt in each tumbler.
Sprinkle toasted almonds over the dates.
Repeat layers of yogurt, dates, and almonds if desired, ending with almonds.
Drizzle remaining honey over the top of each parfait just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Pork and Corn Pasta Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A modest, natural portion of Smoked Pork and Corn Pasta Skillet is presented in a shallow, everyday ceramic bowl on a rustic wooden dining table. The pasta, al dente, is coated in a light, creamy sauce. Diced smoked pork pieces, some with browned edges, are visible throughout the dish. Bright yellow corn kernels and tender green celery pieces are generously interspersed, adding color and texture. Small flecks of fresh chopped parsley provide a vibrant green garnish. The colors are natural: creamy white, light yellow, golden brown, and bright green. A casual cloth napkin is placed beside the bowl. Lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. A fork is casually resting on the table next to the bowl. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad and crusty bread.
instructions: Dice smoked pork into 1.5 cm cubes. Dice onion and celery into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced smoked pork. Cook until browned and slightly crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove pork from skillet, leaving rendered fat.
Add diced onion and celery to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in pasta and broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes, or until pasta is al dente, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in corn and heavy cream. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until heated through and sauce thickens slightly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This dish is designed for quick weeknight preparation. Adjust broth amount if pasta absorbs liquid faster.

recipes.recipe_name: Takenoko to Tori no Nimono (Braised Chicken and Bamboo Shoots)
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, homely portion of Takenoko to Tori no Nimono is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The braised chicken chunks, with their rich, caramelized skin, are nestled among the tender, pale yellow bamboo shoot slices, vibrant orange carrot rounds, and dark brown rehydrated shiitake mushroom caps. A glossy, dark amber sauce coats all components, reflecting the warm kitchen light. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with ingredients touching and slightly overlapping, showcasing comforting textures. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Accompanying the dish are a simple white rice bowl, a small bowl of miso soup, and a dish of pickled vegetables. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the main bowl. The lighting is soft and warm, casting gentle shadows that enhance the lived-in, cozy family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Accompany with a side of miso soup.
Offer various Japanese pickles (tsukemono) as a palate cleanser.

ingredients.name: Bamboo shoots (pre-cooked, canned or vacuum-sealed), sliced
Carrots, peeled, cut into 2 cm thick rounds or large chunks
Dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated, stems removed

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm large chunks. Pat dry.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks, skin-side down. Sear until golden brown and crispy, about 4-5 minutes. Flip and sear other sides briefly.
Drain excess fat from the pot.
Add sliced bamboo shoots, carrot chunks, and rehydrated shiitake mushrooms to the pot with the chicken.
Pour in dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover the pot.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and vegetables are tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat slightly. Simmer uncovered for another 5-7 minutes to reduce the sauce slightly, until it lightly coats the ingredients.
Serve hot. Garnish with blanched green beans if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce is meant to be savory and slightly sweet, perfect for pouring over rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Cherry Tomatoes and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef with cherry tomatoes and herbs is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, placed on a simple light wooden table. The beef is cut into thick, irregular chunks, deeply browned and glistening with the rich, reddish-brown sauce. Whole and burst cherry tomatoes are nestled around the beef, adding vibrant pops of red. The sauce is thick and rustic, clinging to the tender beef and tomatoes. A few fresh sprigs of rosemary and thyme are placed artfully on top as a garnish. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. Lighting is natural and even. A simple cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The background features a blurred, casual bistro setting, enhancing the authentic, approachable restaurant feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread like ciabatta or focaccia for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with creamy polenta or roasted potatoes.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm thick chunks. Pat dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, cherry tomatoes, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (320°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove from oven. Discard rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Almond Cake with Date Caramel and Peanut Butter Yogurt Frosting
recipes.visual_description: The Honey-Almond Cake is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. A single, thick square slice of golden-brown cake forms the base, its crumb visible, indicating a moist texture. A rich, glossy pool of amber-brown date caramel is artfully spooned beside and partially over the cake. On top of the cake, a smooth, creamy dollop of light tan peanut butter yogurt frosting provides a soft contrast. Sprinkled generously over the frosting and caramel are toasted slivered almonds, adding a delicate crunch and warm color. A single vibrant green mint sprig is placed on the side of the frosting for a fresh accent. The arrangement is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The background features a simple wooden table surface, with a cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dessert, highlighting its textures and colors.
