ingredients.quantity: 400g, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm thick rounds

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge beef in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove seared beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Add bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours.
Add potato and carrot chunks. Stir well.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is very tender and vegetables are cooked through.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in fresh basil.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot.
notes: This stew can be made ahead and reheats well. The flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale, creamy yellow, flows naturally within the bowl. Diced, golden-seared chicken pieces (2 cm cubes) are visibly integrated, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets and flecks of deep amber caramelized onion. A small, elegant swirl of bright white lemon-herb mayonnaise rests on top, providing a contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan. The setting is a modern bistro, with the bowl placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and a crisp cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pot with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast rice kernels.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan; keep it simmering.
Begin adding hot broth to the rice, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Drain well.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente, stir in cooked chicken and broccoli florets.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and half of the Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until creamy and fluid. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Grate lemon zest. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with half of the chopped parsley and lemon zest. Mix well.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish each serving with a small dollop or swirl of lemon-herb mayonnaise, remaining Parmesan cheese, and a sprinkle of fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Cacio e Pepe
recipes.visual_description: A generous, spiraled mound of golden spaghetti is centrally placed on a round, shallow, white porcelain pasta bowl. The pasta is coated in a glistening, creamy, off-white sauce, appearing rich and smooth. Visible flecks of freshly cracked black pepper adhere to the strands, providing textural contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano rests atop the pasta, with a few larger, coarse grinds of black pepper for enhanced visual texture. The plate has ample negative space, showcasing the dish's simple elegance. The bowl sits on a light-colored wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin lies to the left. Soft, natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the sauce's glossy finish. This is a single, refined restaurant-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately to maintain sauce consistency.
Enjoy as a standalone main course.
Pair with a simple green salad or crusty bread for soaking up residual sauce.
instructions: Bring 3 litres of water to a rolling boil in a large pot. Add 20g sea salt.
Add 360g spaghetti to boiling water. Cook according to package directions until al dente, about 8-10 minutes.
While pasta cooks, finely grate 180g Parmigiano Reggiano.
In a large sauté pan, toast 15g freshly cracked black peppercorns over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Remove half the toasted pepper for garnish.
Before draining, reserve 500ml of starchy pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the sauté pan with toasted pepper.
Add 120ml reserved pasta water to the pan. Add grated cheese gradually, stirring vigorously with tongs.

Continuously stir and toss pasta, adding small splashes of reserved pasta water as needed, until a creamy, emulsified sauce forms. The sauce should coat the pasta without clumping. This process is called "mantecare."
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining toasted pepper.
notes: The key to a successful Cacio e Pepe is the quality of ingredients and the emulsification technique. Use freshly cracked black pepper and high-quality Parmigiano Reggiano.
The starch from the pasta water is essential for creating the creamy sauce.
traditional_techniques: Mantecare (emulsifying pasta with cheese and water)

recipes.recipe_name: Strawberry, Roasted Beetroot, and Walnut Salad
recipes.visual_description: An individual serving of the Strawberry, Roasted Beetroot, and Walnut Salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The composition is minimalistic, featuring a clean arrangement with ample white space. A base of vibrant mixed seasonal greens is gently scattered across the plate. Diced roasted beetroot, in rich purplish-red cubes, is interspersed with thinly sliced bright red strawberries. Toasted walnuts are sprinkled over, providing a textural contrast. A light pinkish-red vinaigrette, made with fermented strawberry liquid, is drizzled artfully over the ingredients, unifying the colors and textures. The overall visual is clean, natural, and unfussy, highlighting the pure beauty of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light bamboo table surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, with a clean, subtle background suggesting natural elements or plants, emphasizing an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: To prepare fermented strawberry liquid: Combine 100g of strawberry scraps (hull, imperfect pieces) with 100ml apple cider vinegar in a clean jar. Seal loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Strain the liquid. Discard solids. This yields approximately 80ml of fermented liquid.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash beetroot thoroughly. Trim ends. Wrap each beetroot in foil. Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until tender when pierced. Let cool. Peel skins. Dice beetroot into 1.5 cm cubes.
Spread walnuts on a baking tray. Toast in the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes until fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool.
Wash fresh strawberries. Hull and slice thinly. Reserve a few whole small strawberries for garnish if desired.
For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the fermented strawberry liquid, 60ml olive oil, 15ml maple syrup, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine mixed seasonal greens, diced beetroot, and sliced fresh strawberries. Add toasted walnuts.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beef & Beer Stew
recipes.visual_description: A rich, dark Belgian Beef & Beer Stew is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, showcasing its hearty, inviting nature. Large, fork-tender beef chunks, deeply browned and glistening from the braising liquid, are nestled among softened, caramelized onion slices and vibrant orange carrot rounds. The stew's thick, dark brown sauce, infused with dark beer and thyme, coats the ingredients beautifully, reflecting the natural light. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a pop of color and freshness against the deep tones of the stew. The presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small pile of golden, crisp frites and a side of traditional crusty bread, emphasizing the authentic Belgian dining experience. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's comforting textures and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crispy frites (fries)
Serve with crusty bread
Serve with mashed potatoes
Pair with a traditional Belgian beer

ingredients.name: Dark beer
ingredients.quantity: 500 ml (e.g., Belgian strong dark ale or stout)

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, cut into 2 cm thick rounds

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil and butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook onions slowly, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized, about 20-25 minutes.
Add minced garlic and carrots. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, Dijon mustard, brown sugar, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) or maintain a very low simmer on the stovetop.
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Roasted Tomato Sauce and Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef is centrally placed on a round, clean white porcelain plate. Two thick-cut beef sirloin medallions, seared to a deep golden-brown crust with a visible rosy medium-rare interior, are nestled beside a generous, soft mound of creamy golden polenta. A rich, glossy roasted tomato sauce, vibrant red in color, is elegantly spooned over the beef and partially onto the polenta, creating an inviting pool. Scattered around are a few halved, slightly blistered roasted cherry tomatoes, adding pops of red. Fresh green thyme leaves are sprinkled over the dish. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Let beef sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Remove beef from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add diced Roma tomatoes, red wine (if using), beef stock, thyme, and rosemary to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens and tomatoes break down. Mash tomatoes with a spoon. Stir in 30g butter. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Remove herb sprigs.

While sauce cooks, prepare polenta. Bring milk and water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in fine polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes until creamy and thick. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan. Season with salt.
Toss cherry tomato halves with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a preheated 200°C oven for 10-15 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

To serve, spoon creamy polenta onto plates. Place seared beef medallions alongside. Spoon roasted tomato sauce over and around the beef. Garnish with roasted cherry tomato halves and fresh thyme leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Relleno de Queso y Chile con Arroz Rojo
recipes.visual_description: A single generously stuffed roasted poblano pepper, its skin slightly charred and tender, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The pepper is split lengthwise, revealing a rich filling of tender shredded chicken and creamy, bubbling Monterey Jack cheese, golden-brown from baking. A vibrant mound of fluffy Mexican red rice, infused with tomato and garlic, forms a base beneath the pepper. A ladle of glossy, reddish-brown roasted tomato-chili sauce partially drapes over the pepper and rice. The dish is garnished with a fresh sprinkle of finely chopped cilantro leaves. A bright green lime wedge is placed beside the pepper. The scene features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a small stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer crema Mexicana or sour cream on the side.
Serve with extra lime wedges for squeezing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Place whole poblano peppers on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, turning occasionally, until skin is blistered and charred. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes. Peel, deseed, and make a slit down one side of each pepper, keeping stems intact. Set aside.

Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Once cool enough to handle, shred or dice chicken into small chunks.

In the same pan, heat 10 ml olive oil. Add half of the diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add shredded chicken, 5 g ancho chili powder, 3 g cumin, 2 g Mexican oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring to combine. Remove from heat. Stir in 100 g shredded cheese.

Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well. Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add remaining diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add rinsed rice. Cook, stirring, for 3-5 minutes until rice is slightly toasted. Stir in remaining diced tomatoes (from the 400g can), 2 g ancho chili powder, 2 g cumin, 1 g Mexican oregano, 700 ml chicken broth, and salt to taste. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid. Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

While peppers bake, blend 200g of the canned diced tomatoes with 50ml chicken broth, a pinch of ancho chili powder, and a small pinch of salt until smooth. Heat gently in a small saucepan until warmed through.

Carefully fill each poblano pepper with the chicken and cheese mixture. Place stuffed peppers in a baking dish. Top with remaining 100 g shredded cheese. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and peppers are heated through.

Serve each stuffed poblano pepper on a bed of Mexican red rice. Drizzle with the warm roasted tomato-chili sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge. Offer crema Mexicana and warm corn tortillas on the side.
notes: Poblano peppers vary in heat; some can be mild, others moderately spicy. Taste a small piece after roasting if you are sensitive to heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Penne with Spicy Tomato, Mushroom, and Three Cheeses
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Penne with Spicy Tomato, Mushroom, and Three Cheeses is presented in a clean, white ceramic pasta bowl, showcasing a rich, bubbling, and golden-brown top crust. The penne pasta is coated in a vibrant red tomato sauce, interspersed with sautéed, earthy brown mushroom slices, and dark, glossy halved black olives. Melted mozzarella and parmesan form a golden-brown, slightly blistered layer on top, with glimpses of creamy white cottage cheese peeking through. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, providing a pop of color and aromatic contrast. The dish is served on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a clean white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, reflecting a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting. The presentation is rustic yet refined, inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a side of crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chili flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Stir in dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir cooked penne into the sauce. Add halved olives and most of the fresh basil. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine cottage cheese with half of the shredded mozzarella and half of the grated parmesan. Season with a pinch of salt.
Spoon half of the pasta mixture into a baking dish.
Dollop half of the cottage cheese mixture evenly over the pasta.
Spoon remaining pasta mixture over the cheese layer.
Top with remaining shredded mozzarella and grated parmesan.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly, and edges are golden.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cheesy Chicken Macaroni Bake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features a creamy, rich blend of elbow macaroni and tender, shredded chicken, coated in a savory, reddish-orange tomato and cheese sauce. Crowning the macaroni is a golden-brown, visibly crispy layer of baked corn tortilla pieces and toasted breadcrumbs, with streaks of melted, bubbly yellow and white cheese. A scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped cilantro garnishes the top, providing a fresh counterpoint to the warm, comforting colors of the bake. The chicken is presented as tender, shredded chunks, not fanned. The plate is set on a light wooden surface, accompanied by a simple white napkin and standard flatware, under soft, natural light, creating an inviting casual dining scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken breasts to the pot. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook chicken 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pot. Shred chicken using two forks. Set aside.
Stir cooked macaroni into the sauce in the pot. Add shredded Cheddar and Mozzarella. Stir until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Fold in shredded chicken. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer macaroni mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe pot.
Cut tortillas into 2 cm strips or tear into pieces. Toss with breadcrumbs and a drizzle of olive oil.
Scatter tortilla-breadcrumb mixture evenly over the macaroni.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Cheddar Frittata with Fresh Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous wedge of golden-brown chicken and cheddar frittata sits on a simple, slightly imperfect cream-colored ceramic plate. The frittata has a firm, set texture with visible chunks of cooked chicken cubes, translucent softened onion pieces, and pockets of melted, slightly browned shredded cheddar cheese. Its edges are lightly crisped. Beside the frittata, a vibrant mound of fresh mixed salad greens is casually arranged, interspersed with halved bright red cherry tomatoes. The salad appears lightly dressed, glistening subtly. The entire plate is visible, occupying the center of the frame. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table. A plain metal fork rests casually to the side of the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment, perhaps with a simple cloth napkin or a spice jar in the distance, but nothing distracting from the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a 24 cm oven-safe non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Dice the brown onion. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
While onion cooks, whisk eggs in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in shredded cheddar cheese, cooked chicken, and sautéed onion.
Pour the egg mixture back into the oven-safe pan. Ensure ingredients are evenly distributed.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the frittata is set and golden brown on top.
While frittata bakes, prepare the salad. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Combine with mixed salad greens in a bowl.
Whisk 15 ml olive oil and white wine vinegar in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Pour dressing over salad and toss gently.
Remove frittata from oven. Let it rest for a few minutes before slicing into 4 wedges.
Serve each frittata wedge immediately with a generous side of fresh tomato and green salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Pasta with Spicy Tomato and Three Cheeses
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of baked pasta is carefully scooped onto a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The penne or ziti pasta is richly coated in a vibrant rustic red tomato sauce, interspersed with dark, thin slices of black olives and flecks of fresh green basil. Melted mozzarella and parmesan cheese create a golden-brown, bubbly crust over the pasta, with some caramelized edges visible. A scattering of fresh chopped basil leaves garnishes the top, adding a bright green accent. The textures are a pleasing contrast of soft pasta, tender sauce, and slightly crisp, bubbly cheese. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, with a white cotton napkin folded beside it. A traditional fork is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's comforting warmth and authentic Italian appeal. The overall presentation is professional and inviting, with ample negative space around the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add 100ml water or broth if sauce is too thick.
Stir in sliced black olives and half of the fresh basil into the sauce.
In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, 100g shredded mozzarella, and half of the grated Parmesan.
Combine cooked pasta with the tomato sauce in the large pot.
Spread half of the pasta mixture into a 20x30cm baking dish.
Dot spoonfuls of the cheese mixture over the pasta layer.
Top with remaining pasta mixture.
Sprinkle remaining 100g shredded mozzarella and remaining Parmesan over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and golden.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.
notes: Adjust chili flakes to your preferred spice level.
For extra richness, add a splash of cream to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Bourguignon with Pommes Purée
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Beef Bourguignon is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Several rich, dark brown beef chunks, approximately 5 cm cubes, are nestled amongst tender, glistening pearl onions and halved button mushrooms. The ingredients are coated in a glossy, deep reddish-brown sauce, thick and rich. Adjacent to the bourguignon is a generous, smooth quenelle of pale yellow pommes purée, showcasing its creamy texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the bourguignon, adding a fresh contrast. The plate rests on a simple, warm-toned wooden table, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The scene is lit with soft, even natural light, highlighting the dish's inviting colors and textures. Classic silver flatware is placed beside the plate, completing the refined yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Pat beef cubes dry. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches until well-caramelized on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced lardons to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove lardons and set aside, leaving fat in the pot.
Add chopped yellow onions and carrots (cut into 2 cm thick rounds) to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Gradually pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return browned beef to the pot.
Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is very tender.
While beef braises, prepare the pearl onions and mushrooms. Melt 30 g butter in a separate pan. Add pearl onions and halved button mushrooms. Sauté until lightly browned and tender. Set aside.
For pommes purée: Peel and cut potatoes into 4 cm chunks. Place in a pot of cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.

Pass hot potatoes through a potato ricer or mash thoroughly. Heat milk and 100 g butter in a small saucepan until butter is melted and milk is warm. Gradually add warm milk and butter mixture to mashed potatoes, stirring until smooth and creamy. Season with salt.
Once beef is tender, remove pot from oven. Stir in sautéed pearl onions and mushrooms. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Ladle generous portions of Beef Bourguignon into shallow bowls. Serve alongside a scoop of creamy pommes purée. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Cabbage & Roasted Root Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and inviting salad presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Shredded, slightly purple fermented red cabbage forms a base, interspersed with warm-toned, diced roasted carrots, beets, and parsnips, showcasing their natural, slightly caramelized textures. A scattering of whole, toasted walnuts adds a rustic, natural crunch. Crispy, small beef pieces are sprinkled sparingly over the vegetables, adding a savory focal point. A creamy, pale yellow advocaat dressing is artfully drizzled over the components, binding them together while leaving negative space on the plate. The arrangement is natural and unforced, highlighting each ingredient's pure beauty. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, and soft, natural lighting that emphasizes the dish's fresh colors. A clean, minimalist background with subtle greenery completes the eco-conscious aesthetic, focusing solely on the sustainable, ingredient-forward presentation.
instructions: Shred red cabbage finely. Place in a bowl. Add 5g salt. Massage cabbage for 5 minutes until it softens and releases liquid. Cover and let ferment at room temperature for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel carrots, beets, and parsnips. Dice all root vegetables into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Dice beef into very small, 0.5 cm pieces. Heat a dry pan over medium-high heat. Add beef. Cook, stirring occasionally, until crispy and browned. Drain excess fat. Set aside.

For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together advocaat, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in remaining 30 ml olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified and smooth.
Drain any excess liquid from the fermented red cabbage. In a large bowl, combine fermented cabbage, roasted root vegetables, and walnuts. Toss gently.
Divide salad among four plates. Sprinkle crispy beef bits over each salad. Drizzle generously with the savory advocaat dressing. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Garlic Bread Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cheesy Chicken and Garlic Bread Pasta Bake rests in a rustic, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden dining table. The dish is a comforting medley of penne pasta, tender chicken cubes, and rich tomato-cream sauce, all bubbling with melted mozzarella. A golden-brown, crispy topping of cheesy garlic breadcrumbs covers the surface, with some crumbs scattered enticingly. The chicken pieces, cut into 2 cm cubes, are visible throughout the pasta, coated in the vibrant red-orange sauce. The texture is invitingly gooey and crunchy. A simple, silver fork is placed beside the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen light, evoking a cozy family meal. A casually folded beige paper towel is visible in the background, adding to the lived-in, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook penne according to package directions until al dente. Drain.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature of chicken must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, and dried basil. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in heavy cream, salt, and pepper. Add cooked pasta and cooked chicken to the sauce. Mix well.
If not using an oven-safe pan, transfer pasta mixture to a 2.5-liter baking dish.
For topping: Process stale bread into coarse crumbs. In a small bowl, combine bread crumbs with melted butter, half of the shredded mozzarella, and grated Parmesan cheese.
Sprinkle the remaining shredded mozzarella over the pasta bake. Then evenly spread the cheesy bread crumb mixture on top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato, Mozzarella and Pasta Salad with Creamy Basil Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, homely individual portion of Tomato, Mozzarella and Pasta Salad is presented in a well-used, rustic ceramic bowl. The small pasta shapes are coated in a creamy, pale green basil dressing, creating a rich texture. Interspersed throughout are vibrant red diced tomatoes, irregular white torn mozzarella pieces, and dark sliced black olives. Finely diced red onion adds a subtle crunch. The salad is casually mounded, showcasing the natural colors and textures. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered generously on top, providing a fresh aroma. The bowl rests on a warm, natural wooden kitchen table. Soft, cozy lighting from overhead fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, lived-in atmosphere. A simple, folded cloth napkin and standard flatware are casually placed nearby, completing the unpretentious, family kitchen table setting.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Tear fresh mozzarella into small pieces or cut into small cubes. Slice pitted black olives.
Finely dice the red onion. Roughly chop half of the fresh basil leaves.
In a blender, combine cottage cheese, olive oil, red wine vinegar, water, chopped basil, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth and creamy. Adjust seasoning to taste.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled pasta, diced tomatoes, mozzarella, sliced olives, and diced red onion.
Pour the creamy basil dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat everything evenly.
Transfer the salad to serving bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped. Serve immediately or chill before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Red Cabbage and Root Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, embodying minimalistic elegance. A vibrant medley of thinly sliced, ruby-red fermented cabbage forms the base, its natural tang visible in its slightly wilted texture. Bright orange julienned carrots and small, deep purple diced raw beets are artfully scattered throughout, adding pops of color and textural contrast. Tender, dark green cooked lentils are interspersed, providing a grounding element. Lightly toasted pumpkin seeds are sprinkled generously, catching the light and offering a delicate crunch. A light, emulsified dressing glistens subtly on the vegetables, binding the composition without pooling. The arrangement is organic and unforced, allowing individual ingredients to shine, with ample negative space around the central mound. Freshly chopped parsley is sprinkled lightly over the top for a final verdant touch. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh, wholesome quality of the ingredients. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing the sustainable and earth-conscious theme.
instructions: Place thinly sliced red cabbage in a large bowl. Add sea salt. Massage cabbage vigorously with hands for 5-7 minutes until it softens and releases liquid.
Let salted cabbage stand for 30 minutes. Gently squeeze out excess liquid. Reserve 15ml of the liquid for the dressing.
While cabbage rests, julienne carrots. Dice peeled beets into small, uniform cubes.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, reserved fermented cabbage brine, and Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine prepared fermented red cabbage, julienned carrots, diced beets, cooked green lentils, and toasted pumpkin seeds.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all components evenly. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Rustic Chicken and Mushroom Stew is presented in a deep, textured ceramic bowl. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks (approximately 3cm) are nestled among thick-sliced brown mushrooms, bright orange 1.5cm diced carrots, and softened white onion pieces. The ingredients are coated in a rich, glossy, light brown cream sauce. A sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast on top. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a hearty, inviting appearance. The bowl rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table. Beside it, a simple ceramic plate holds a modest portion of fluffy white rice. A sturdy silver fork and a plain cloth napkin are casually placed. Warm, soft kitchen lighting enhances the homely atmosphere, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a cozy family kitchen.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dice onion and carrots into 1.5cm pieces. Slice mushrooms thickly.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 minute to cook flour.
Gradually pour in chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Stir well. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Ladle stew into individual bowls. Garnish with chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Brodo di Manzo con Gnocchetti di Semolino
recipes.visual_description: A clear, golden Italian beef broth is presented in a deep white porcelain bowl, portioned for a single serving. Small, irregularly shaped semolina dumplings, light cream in color, float gracefully within the broth, showcasing their tender texture. Shredded pieces of tender, slow-cooked beef, rich brown, are interspersed among the dumplings, adding substance and color. The broth's surface is lightly dotted with tiny droplets of rendered beef fat, catching the light. A vibrant green garnish of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled generously over the soup, providing a fresh aromatic contrast and a pop of color. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a classic silver spoon, creating a clean, inviting bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a 'primo piatto' (first course) in a traditional Italian meal.
Offer with crusty artisanal bread on the side for dipping.
instructions: Prepare beef broth: In a large pot, combine beef marrow bones, beef chuck, coarsely chopped onion, carrot, celery, bay leaf, and black peppercorns. Cover with 4 litres of cold water.
Bring to a boil over high heat. Immediately reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 3-4 hours. Skim any foam from the surface as it appears.
Remove beef chuck and bones from the pot. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard all solids. Shred the cooked beef chuck into small, bite-sized pieces.
Season the strained beef broth with salt to taste. Keep it at a gentle simmer.

Prepare semolina dumplings: In a medium bowl, whisk the egg. Gradually add the fine semolina, grated Parmesan cheese, and a pinch of ground nutmeg and salt. Mix until a firm, pliable dough forms. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more semolina.
Using two teaspoons or your hands, form small, irregular-shaped dumplings (gnocchetti) from the semolina dough. Drop them carefully into the gently simmering beef broth.
Cook the semolina dumplings for 5-7 minutes, or until they float to the surface and are tender when tasted.
Add the shredded beef back into the broth with the cooked dumplings to heat through.
Ladle the hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving generously with fresh chopped flat-leaf parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, vibrant orange-red tomato risotto is presented in a shallow white porcelain pasta bowl. The risotto flows gently, indicating its fluid, 'all'onda' consistency. On top, two or three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are nestled into the rice, showcasing a crisp exterior and tender interior. Bright green chopped basil is mixed throughout the risotto, with fresh whole basil leaves and a light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese garnishing the top. A subtle drizzle of olive oil glistens on the surface. The plate sits on a rustic wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon). The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, emphasizing the dish as the focal point. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp white wine.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 bunch, chopped, plus leaves for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (75°C internal temperature). Remove chicken. Rest.
In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 25g butter. Sauté diced onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast grains.
Pour in white wine (if using). Cook until absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well.
Add one ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. Cook for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan and remaining 25g butter.
Fold in chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick chunks.
Serve risotto immediately. Top with chicken chunks, fresh basil leaves, and extra Parmesan.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (finishing with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Baked Pasta with Three Cheeses
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of spicy baked pasta rests in a deep, round white ceramic baking dish. The top crust is golden-brown and bubbly from melted mozzarella and Parmesan cheese, showing slight charring on raised edges. Visible layers beneath the crust reveal rigatoni pasta tubes coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Creamy white dollops of the baked cottage cheese mixture are interspersed throughout. Dark, glossy black olive rings and vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered across the top, some slightly wilted from the heat. The texture is invitingly gooey and robust. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware. A small, rustic basket holds a few slices of crusty Italian bread. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Accompanied by a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large pot. Add finely diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
While pasta cooks, prepare cheese mixture. In a bowl, combine cottage cheese, 50g grated Parmesan, and one egg. Mix well.
Tear or dice fresh mozzarella into small pieces.
Slice black olives into rings.
Add cooked pasta to the tomato sauce. Stir to coat evenly.
Spread a thin layer of sauce and pasta mixture in a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Dollop half of the cottage cheese mixture over the pasta. Scatter half of the mozzarella and half of the sliced olives.
Add remaining pasta and sauce. Top with remaining cottage cheese mixture, mozzarella, and olives.
Sprinkle remaining Parmesan cheese over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and golden brown on top.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: For best results, use good quality canned tomatoes.
Ensure pasta is truly al dente as it will continue to cook in the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Salmon with Herb Mayonnaise and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly baked salmon fillet rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon is a vibrant pink, topped with a thick, golden-brown crust of herb mayonnaise that is slightly bubbly and charred at the edges. Beneath the crust, rich, deeply caramelized onion slices are visible, adding a warm, amber tone. The salmon's flesh is visibly flaky. A small cluster of fresh green dill sprigs is artfully placed atop the crust, adding a pop of vibrant color and freshness. Beside the salmon, a bright yellow lemon wedge provides a contrasting element. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork and knife placed neatly to the side. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, set against a subtly blurred background consistent with a modern bistro. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the refined yet approachable quality of the dish.
instructions: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-35 minutes until deeply golden brown and very soft. Add granulated sugar during the last 10 minutes. Add minced garlic for the last 5 minutes. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, chopped dill, chopped chives, lemon zest, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Place fillets on the prepared baking sheet.
Divide the caramelized onions evenly among the salmon fillets. Spread them over the top.
Spoon the herb mayonnaise mixture over the onions on each fillet, spreading it to form an even crust.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the salmon reaches 75°C and the mayonnaise crust is golden brown and slightly bubbly.
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over each fillet.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and a sprinkle of fresh herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Gochujang Beef with Sesame Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a single individual portion in a clean, white ceramic bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. Tender, thinly sliced gochujang-glazed beef strips are artfully piled on one side of a bed of fluffy white steamed rice. Beside the beef, vibrant, crisp-tender julienned carrots, sliced shiitake mushrooms, and bright green blanched spinach are arranged. The beef has a rich reddish-brown hue with a slight sheen from the glaze. A sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds and thinly sliced green spring onion rounds garnish the top. Metal chopsticks rest beside the bowl. A small, white ceramic dish containing bright red kimchi is placed as a traditional accompaniment. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the main subject with a minimal, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Offer various banchan (side dishes) like kimchi or pickled radishes.
Eat with chopsticks.

ingredients.name: Spring onions, thinly sliced, for garnish

instructions: Prepare marinade: In a bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, brown sugar, and rice vinegar. Mix well.
Slice beef sirloin into thin strips, approximately 0.5 cm thick. Add beef to marinade. Toss to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat a large wok or frying pan over high heat. Add cooking oil. Add julienned carrots and sliced shiitake mushrooms. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender. Remove from pan.
Quickly blanch spinach in the same pan or a separate pot with a splash of water for 30 seconds. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water.

Reheat wok or frying pan over high heat. Add marinated beef strips in a single layer. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until caramelized and cooked through. Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove from pan and set aside.

Combine cooked beef, stir-fried carrots, mushrooms, and blanched spinach in the wok. Toss gently to warm through. Serve immediately over steamed white rice in individual bowls. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced spring onions.
traditional_techniques: Marinating for tenderization and flavor infusion

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-braised beef ragu is presented on an everyday, off-white ceramic pasta bowl, showcasing its rustic Italian charm. The rich, deep reddish-brown ragu, featuring tender, shredded beef chunks and finely diced carrots and celery, generously coats wide, golden pappardelle noodles. The pasta is naturally intertwined with the sauce, creating a hearty, flowing mound in the center of the bowl. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano adds a creamy white accent and subtle texture. A few small, fresh thyme leaves are casually scattered on top for a touch of green. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Alongside, a simple fork and spoon with classic design are placed on a casually folded beige linen napkin. The background shows a hint of a relaxed family kitchen atmosphere, with warm, cozy lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 4-5 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches if needed. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced carrots and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine is mostly reduced.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender and easily shredded.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef using two forks. Discard herb sprigs and bay leaves.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with a generous amount of beef ragu.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Individual Apple & Banana Meringue Tarts
recipes.visual_description: A single individual apple and banana meringue tart is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The tart, approximately 10 cm in diameter, features a golden-brown, crisp pâte sablée crust. A cloud of lightly toasted, golden-brown meringue, artfully swirled into soft peaks, covers the fruit filling. Its surface shows delicate caramelization, contrasting with its fluffy interior. A vibrant, deep ruby-red cherry coulis is artfully drizzled over and around the tart, creating a visually appealing contrast and gloss. The coulis pools beside the tart, highlighting its rich color. The presentation is clean and elegant, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table, in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is placed beside. Natural, even lighting from the top-left casts soft shadows, and the background is softly blurred.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as an individual dessert at the end of a meal.

ingredients.name: Apples (e.g., Granny Smith or Honeycrisp), peeled, cored, thinly sliced

instructions: Prepare Tart Dough: In a large bowl, combine flour, 30g sugar, and salt. Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add cold milk/water gradually, mixing until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap in cling film, and chill for 30 minutes.

Pre-bake Tart Shells: Preheat oven to 180°C. On a lightly floured surface, roll out dough to 3mm thickness. Cut out four circles to fit individual tart tins (approx. 10-12 cm diameter). Press dough into tins. Prick bases with a fork. Line with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 10-12 minutes, or until edges are lightly golden. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5 minutes until dry. Let cool.

Prepare Apple & Banana Filling: In a pan, melt 10g butter over medium heat. Add sliced apples, 20g sugar, and 5ml vanilla extract. Cook for 5-7 minutes until apples soften slightly. Add sliced bananas and cook for 2 minutes more. Remove from heat.
Assemble Tarts: Divide apple and banana filling evenly among the four pre-baked tart shells.
Prepare Meringue: In a clean, dry bowl, whisk egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 100g caster sugar, a tablespoon at a time, whisking continuously until stiff, glossy peaks form.

Top and Bake Tarts: Spoon or pipe meringue over the fruit filling in each tart, ensuring it covers the fruit completely. Bake in the 180°C oven for 10-15 minutes, or until meringue is golden brown and slightly crisp.

Prepare Cherry Coulis: While tarts bake, combine 150g cherries, 30g sugar, and 15ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cherries break down and sauce thickens slightly. Remove from heat, stir in 2ml vanilla extract. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a smoother coulis, if desired.
Serve: Let tarts cool slightly. Drizzle generously with cherry coulis before serving.
notes: Ensure all equipment for meringue (bowl, whisk) is completely grease-free for best results.
Adjust sweetness of fruit filling based on apple tartness.

recipes.recipe_name: Homely Tuna Mozzarella Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A rectangular ceramic baking dish, possibly well-used, sits on a rustic wooden kitchen table. The dish holds a single, generous portion of golden-brown, bubbly tuna mozzarella pasta bake, scooped onto an everyday ceramic plate. The surface displays melted, slightly browned mozzarella cheese, with creamy, rich pasta peeking through. The pasta, such as penne or fusilli, is coated in a thick, savory white sauce, interspersed with visible flakes of tuna. The color palette is warm, featuring golden-brown cheese, creamy white sauce, and the subtle tan of tuna. A few specks of dried chili flakes are visible on the surface. The background is a blurred, cozy kitchen setting with warm, inviting light. A simple fork and a crumpled cloth napkin are casually placed beside the plate. The overall presentation is unpretentious and hearty, reflecting home-style comfort food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until soft.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Melt butter in the pan with onion and garlic.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sauce thickens.
Season sauce with salt and pepper. Add chili flakes if using.
Stir in drained tuna and cooked pasta into the sauce. Mix well.
Transfer pasta mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella evenly over the top.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Rustic Chicken and Rice Pilaf is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. A whole, crispy-skinned, golden-brown chicken thigh rests slightly off-center on a bed of fluffy, tender long-grain rice. The rice is visibly separated, infused with savory broth, and contains small, softened pieces of caramelized onion and tiny flecks of minced garlic. A casual sprinkling of bright green chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of color over the chicken and rice. The chicken thigh is cooked whole, not sliced or fanned. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Beside the plate, a standard metal fork and knife are casually placed, alongside a simple ceramic water glass. A crumpled, natural linen napkin is loosely arranged nearby. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy, lived-in kitchen with warm, inviting ambient lighting, creating an overall impression of comforting, unpretentious home cooking.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add roughly chopped onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and paprika to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked rice. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until rice is lightly toasted.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add dried thyme.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pan tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5-10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Tuscan Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, rustic red-orange tomato sauce, infused with oregano and garlic. Tender, seared chicken breast, cut into thick chunks, is nestled amidst the pasta and sauce. Diced red bell peppers and onions are visible within the sauce, adding vibrant color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped oregano leaves garnishes the dish, providing a contrasting green. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the top. The overall presentation is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the focal point with a soft, blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce and chicken. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped oregano or basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef Cheek with Fermented Potato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-braised beef cheek rests atop a creamy, slightly off-white mound of fermented potato puree. The beef cheek, deep brown and glistening from the rich braising liquid, showcases its natural, irregular shape. A few delicate, golden-brown crispy potato skin shards are strategically placed, adding vertical interest and texture. Thin, translucent shavings of aged hard cheese are scattered over the beef and puree, providing a subtle contrast. The dish is presented on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, allowing ample negative space around the food. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin is subtly placed nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural elements, ensuring the dish remains the focal point.

ingredients.name: Whey or brine from previous fermentation (for potato starter, optional)

instructions: Prepare fermented potato: Peel 200g of potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Place in a clean jar. Add 1 tablespoon of salt and 2 tablespoons of whey or brine (optional). Cover with filtered water. Seal jar. Leave at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.
Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F).
Season beef cheeks generously with salt and pepper. Sear beef cheeks in a large, oven-safe pot over high heat until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add crushed garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef cheeks to the pot. Pour in beef stock. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring liquid to a simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

Remove beef cheeks from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids. Skim any excess fat from the liquid. Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens slightly to a rich sauce consistency.

Prepare potato puree: Peel remaining 800g potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly. Drain fermented potato cubes. Add to mashed potatoes. Mash again to combine.
Heat butter and milk/cream in a small saucepan. Add to mashed potatoes. Beat until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Prepare crispy potato skins: Reserve peels from the 800g potatoes. Wash and dry thoroughly. Toss with a drizzle of oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until golden and crisp.

To serve: Spoon a generous portion of fermented potato puree onto the center of each plate. Place one braised beef cheek on top of the puree. Drizzle with the reduced braising sauce. Garnish with a few crispy potato skin shards. Shave aged hard cheese thinly over the top.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tatsoi & Egg Savory Tart
recipes.visual_description: A substantial slice of the Fermented Tatsoi & Egg Savory Tart rests on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural beige tone. The tart features a golden-brown, rustic fermented crust. Its creamy, pale yellow egg custard filling is studded with vibrant, roughly chopped blansoi leaves and tender, thinly sliced spring onion. The interior reveals the soft, set texture of the egg and cream cheese. Alongside, a small cluster of thinly sliced, bright pink quick-pickled radishes provides crisp contrast. Fresh tatsoi leaves and finely chopped chives garnish the plate. The setting is a light reclaimed wood table with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting organic textures. A clean, minimalist background hints at green foliage, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced, uncrowded composition.

ingredients.name: spring onions, thinly sliced (white and light green parts)

instructions: Prepare Tart Crust Dough: In a large bowl, combine flour, water, sourdough starter, salt, and olive oil. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover bowl with a damp cloth. Let ferment at room temperature for 4-6 hours, or until doubled. Alternatively, cold ferment in the refrigerator for 12-24 hours.

Prepare Tart Shell: Lightly flour a work surface. Roll out fermented dough into a 30 cm circle. Carefully transfer dough to a 24 cm tart pan with a removable bottom. Press dough into pan, trimming excess. Prick bottom with a fork. Chill for 30 minutes.

Blind Bake Crust: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line tart shell with parchment paper, fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake an additional 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Remove from oven. Reduce oven temperature to 170°C.
Prepare Filling: In a large bowl, whisk eggs, softened cream cheese, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until smooth. Set aside.

Prepare Tatsoi and Spring Onions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch tatsoi leaves for 30 seconds until bright green. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to cool. Drain well and gently squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop. In a small pan, sauté sliced spring onions in a touch of olive oil for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Assemble Tart: Scatter chopped tatsoi and sautéed spring onions evenly over the bottom of the blind-baked tart crust. Pour the egg and cream cheese mixture over the vegetables.
Bake Tart: Carefully transfer tart to the preheated 170°C oven. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the center is just set and lightly golden. A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.

Prepare Quick-Pickled Radishes: While tart bakes, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Add thinly sliced radishes. Let sit for at least 15 minutes to quick pickle.
Serve: Let tart cool for 10-15 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature, accompanied by the quick-pickled radishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single refined portion of Slow-Roasted Chicken with Fermented Tomato-Garlic Pasta is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in a warm cream tone. Rustic chunks of slow-roasted chicken, boasting a golden-brown exterior and tender interior, are nestled among al dente short pasta. The pasta is coated in a vibrant, naturally red fermented tomato sauce, punctuated by soft, golden whole confit garlic cloves and scattered with rough-chopped fresh cherry tomatoes. A scattering of fresh green oregano leaves provides a contrasting pop of color and texture. The plating is minimalistic, allowing natural negative space to highlight each ingredient's organic form and color, avoiding any rigid arrangements. The dish rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, with a subtle, out-of-focus green plant in the background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes for fermenting (e.g., Roma or cherry)

instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Roughly chop 500g ripe tomatoes. Place in a clean jar with 1 teaspoon of sea salt. Cover loosely. Allow to ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate when ready.

Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Place on a baking tray. Slow-roast for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken, then cut into rustic chunks.

Prepare garlic confit: Peel garlic cloves from 1 head. Place in a small saucepan. Cover with 150ml olive oil. Cook over very low heat for 20-30 minutes, until garlic is soft and golden. Do not brown. Strain garlic, reserving oil.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

Prepare sauce: In a large pan, combine fermented tomatoes (and their liquid) with 4-5 confit garlic cloves. Crush gently. Add rough-chopped fresh cherry tomatoes. Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Add 100-150ml reserved pasta water to reach desired consistency.
Combine: Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss well to coat. Add chicken chunks. Gently mix.
Serve: Plate immediately. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves and a drizzle of the reserved garlic confit oil.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing chicken bones for stock (if using bone-in chicken) and using the entire garlic head for confit. The fermented tomatoes extend the life of fresh produce.
The reserved garlic oil can be used for other dishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, rustic bowl of Hearty Chicken Vegetable Soup is presented on a well-used wooden dining table. The ceramic bowl, in a natural, earthy tone, holds a generous single portion. Diced chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm, are visible throughout the rich, golden broth. Bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and creamy white diced potatoes are interspersed, showcasing their distinct textures. The chicken is cooked through, tender, and retains its natural shape. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley sits on top, adding a fresh contrast. The soup fills the bowl appropriately, with some negative space around the rim. The setting includes a simple, slightly worn wooden spoon resting beside the bowl and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, homely atmosphere. The focus remains on the wholesome, unpretentious food.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm diced chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Pour in chicken broth. Add dried thyme and bay leaf.
Bring soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes.
Add diced potatoes. Continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Saffron Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow bomba rice, infused with saffron, is mounded slightly in the center, appearing moist and flavorful, not dry. Scattered throughout the rice are vibrant orange diced carrots and bright green peas. Nestled naturally within and on top of the rice are golden-brown, tender chunks of boneless chicken thigh, showcasing their seared exterior. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green and freshness. A lemon wedge rests on the side of the plate, ready for squeezing. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a soft, casual restaurant-style background that remains unobtrusive.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or shallow pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion and carrots to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced.
Add bomba rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice.
Pour in hot chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan, nestling it into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice has absorbed most of the liquid and is tender. Do not stir frequently.
Stir in frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Garlic Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken drumstick or thigh on an everyday ceramic plate. Beside it, rustic, golden potato wedges and caramelized onion pieces. Smashed garlic cloves are visible. Fresh rosemary sprigs are casually scattered. Components touch and slightly overlap, forming a natural, comforting pile. Colors are warm browns, golden yellows, and green from rosemary; textures are crispy skin and soft interiors. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table with a simple off-white cloth napkin. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting casts soft shadows. The blurred background suggests a lived-in kitchen, perhaps a salt cellar nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served often with a simple green salad or steamed vegetables.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, smashed garlic, rosemary leaves, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Add chicken pieces to the bowl. Toss again to coat chicken with oil and seasonings.
Spread chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden brown.
Flip chicken and potatoes halfway through cooking for even browning.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mexican Chicken & Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Spicy Mexican Chicken & Rice Soup is presented in a clean, round white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The rich, clear red-orange broth is filled with tender 3 cm chicken chunks, soft 2 cm potato dice, distinct grains of white rice, and diced tomatoes. Fresh green cilantro leaves are generously scattered over the surface, with a few thin, bright green serrano chili slices providing a contrasting pop of color and subtle heat. A fresh lime wedge rests on the bowl's rim, ready to be squeezed. Beside the bowl, a small stack of warm corn tortillas, neatly wrapped in a beige cotton napkin, and a rustic ceramic dish holding creamy avocado slices complete the authentic Mexican casual dining experience. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping or making small tacos.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh citrusy finish.
