Serve sliced avocado as a cooling accompaniment.
Provide additional hot sauce on the side for those who prefer more heat.

ingredients.name: Jalapeño or serrano chili, thinly sliced

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add minced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Brown lightly on all sides for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in diced Roma tomatoes, ground cumin, and dried Mexican oregano. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and washed rice to the pot. Stir well.
Continue to simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F), potatoes are tender, and rice is cooked.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls.
Garnish each serving with fresh chopped cilantro, extra chili slices if desired, and a lime wedge.
Serve immediately with warm corn tortillas and sliced avocado on the side.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.
For a richer flavor, brown chicken chunks more deeply before adding liquids.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Roasted Chicken and Root Vegetables is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The plate sits on a rustic, well-used wooden dining table. One golden-brown chicken thigh, roasted to a crispy finish, is centered on the plate. Surrounding the chicken are generous portions of roasted potato chunks, their skins lightly crisped and interiors fluffy, mixed with tender, caramelized onion wedges. Bright green broccoli florets, tender-crisp from roasting, are scattered throughout the dish, adding a pop of color. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, home-style appearance. No decorative garnishes are present, only the seasoned roasted vegetables. A simple white linen napkin is casually placed beside the plate, with a standard fork and knife resting on it. Warm, soft ambient light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting, homely atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, such as Maris Piper or Russet

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into 3cm chunks. Cut onion into thick wedges. Cut broccoli into florets.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, potato chunks, and onion wedges.
Drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with garlic powder, paprika, dried thyme, salt, and pepper.
Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray. Do not overcrowd.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove tray from oven. Add broccoli florets to the tray. Toss gently with the other ingredients.
Return to oven. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken Pasta with Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of baked chicken pasta is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta, specifically penne, is coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, with tender, browned chicken cubes visible throughout. Melted mozzarella cheese forms a bubbly, golden-brown crust over the top, with some cheese strands stretching as if just served. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped rosemary or basil garnishes the dish. The overall arrangement is natural and comforting, with components touching and overlapping. A simple white or cream-colored cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting textures and colors of the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot directly from the baking dish
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Cook until browned on all sides and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add chopped rosemary. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the sauce. Stir well. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook penne pasta in a separate pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add to the chicken and tomato sauce. Stir to combine.
Stir in half of the mozzarella cheese and half of the Parmesan cheese.
Transfer pasta mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe pan. Top with remaining mozzarella and Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and edges are golden brown.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Tortilla
recipes.visual_description: A thick, round Spanish Tortilla, with a rustic golden-brown exterior, is the centerpiece on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. A generous wedge is cut, revealing the soft, moist interior where tender, thinly sliced potatoes and translucent onion pieces are suspended in creamy, bright yellow egg. The potato slices are clearly visible in their natural, irregular shapes. The plate is set on a well-worn, dark wooden dining table, embodying a homely, comfortable kitchen scene. Simple, everyday flatware rests beside the plate. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures. A casually folded linen napkin completes the inviting, unpretentious presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.
Accompany with crusty bread and a simple green salad or olives.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Thinly slice potatoes and onion.
Heat 250ml olive oil in a 24cm non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced potatoes and onion to the pan. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes. Potatoes should be very tender, not browned.
Drain excess olive oil from potatoes and onion using a colander. Reserve oil.
Whisk eggs in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Add drained potatoes and onion to the whisked eggs. Mix gently. Let sit for 5 minutes.
Wipe the pan clean. Add 15ml fresh olive oil. Heat over medium heat.
Pour egg and potato mixture into the hot pan. Spread evenly.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until edges set and bottom is golden.
Place a large plate over the pan. Carefully invert the tortilla onto the plate.
Slide the tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until set.
Slide onto a serving plate. Let rest a few minutes before slicing into thick wedges.
notes: This dish is often served as a main course for breakfast or brunch in Spain, or as a tapa.
The slow cooking of potatoes in olive oil is crucial for the correct texture.
traditional_techniques: Slow frying potatoes in olive oil
The 'flip' technique for cooking both sides

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Parmigiana
recipes.visual_description: A single whole golden-brown pan-fried chicken breast serves as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is topped with a generous layer of rich, vibrant red tomato sauce and a thick medallion of melted, slightly charred fresh mozzarella cheese. The breading on the edges remains visible and crispy. A delicate garnish of whole fresh basil leaves and finely grated parmesan adds contrast. The dish is presented in a modern bistro setting on a dark oak table with a white cotton napkin. To the side, a small nest of herb-tossed spaghetti provides balance. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the melted cheese and the golden crust.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small portion of al dente spaghetti with olive oil
Accompany with a simple arugula salad and balsamic vinaigrette
Provide a side of crusty Italian bread to mop up the tomato sauce
instructions: Flatten chicken breasts to 1.5cm thickness using a meat mallet.
Season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper.
Combine breadcrumbs with 25g of parmesan in a shallow bowl.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry chicken for 4 minutes per side until the coating is golden and crisp.
Combine passata, garlic, and oregano in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes and season to taste.
Place fried chicken breasts into a baking dish.
Spoon tomato sauce over each breast and top with mozzarella slices.
Bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until cheese is melted and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with fresh basil and remaining parmesan before serving.
notes: Always verify the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C.
Use low-moisture fresh mozzarella to prevent the breading from becoming soggy.
Press the breadcrumbs firmly into the chicken to ensure a consistent crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Teriyaki with Roasted Broccoli and Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Chicken Teriyaki is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, irregular chunks of seared, glossy dark brown chicken, coated in a rich teriyaki glaze, are arranged prominently. Alongside, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets, retaining a slight crispness and hints of char, are carefully placed. A neat mound of fluffy white steamed Jasmine rice sits opposite the main components. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds and thinly sliced bright green spring onions. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and traditional Japanese chopsticks resting on a small chopstick rest. A small white rice bowl accompanies the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights colors and textures in a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup.
Offer pickled ginger as an accompaniment.
Serve green tea alongside the meal.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 10 ml vegetable oil. Season lightly with salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.

In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, grated ginger, and minced garlic. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens. Set aside.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 20 ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Add chicken thighs to the hot skillet, skin-side down if skin-on. Sear for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest for 5 minutes.

Pour half of the teriyaki sauce into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken, coating thoroughly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until chicken is well glazed. Remove chicken from skillet.
Cut chicken thighs into thick, irregular chunks. Do not slice thinly or fan out.

To serve, arrange chicken chunks, roasted broccoli, and a mound of steamed rice on each plate. Drizzle remaining teriyaki sauce over chicken. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions.
notes: For extra flavor, marinate chicken in a small amount of teriyaki sauce for 30 minutes before searing.
Adjust sugar in teriyaki sauce to taste, depending on desired sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Quick-Pickled Tomato & Mixed Greens Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, minimalist salad presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. At the center, a bed of crisp, mixed seasonal greens forms the base. Scattered artfully across the greens are ruby-red quick-pickled tomato halves, their cut sides revealing juicy interiors. Interspersed are delicate, finely shredded pieces of smoked chicken, adding subtle color variation. Thin, irregular shavings of Parmesan cheese are elegantly draped over the top. The components are arranged with natural spacing, ensuring each ingredient is visible. A light, glistening vinaigrette coats the leaves and tomatoes. The setting features a light reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural lighting, emphasizing the dish's fresh, sustainable essence.

ingredients.name: Fresh dill sprigs (or other herb stems)
Mixed seasonal salad greens, washed and dried
Parmesan cheese, shaved or finely grated
Black pepper, freshly ground, to taste

instructions: Prepare quick-pickled tomatoes: Combine vinegar, water, sugar, salt, and dill in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat.
Place halved tomatoes in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over tomatoes. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Shred smoked chicken: Use a fork or fingers to shred the smoked chicken breast into very fine pieces.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, reserved pickling liquid, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until emulsified.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, gently combine mixed greens, quick-pickled tomatoes, and shredded smoked chicken.
Dress and serve: Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to coat. Divide among four plates. Garnish each serving with Parmesan shavings.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing pickling liquid in the dressing and can use herb stems for infusing the pickling liquid.
Adjust sweetness and acidity of pickling liquid to your preference.
Ensure smoked chicken is shredded very finely to act as a flavor accent rather than a main protein.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Pickled Red Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: A refreshing, vibrant green and white salad is presented in a shallow, handcrafted, matte off-white ceramic bowl, reflecting traditional rustic pottery. Thinly sliced fresh cucumbers and delicate mixed salad greens form the base, artfully arranged with a natural, flowing composition. Scattered throughout are thin, translucent rings of quick-pickled red onion, their pale pink edges providing a subtle contrast. The salad is lightly coated with a glossy, golden vinaigrette, allowing the natural colors of the vegetables to shine. A generous scattering of fresh, finely chopped dill adds a verdant pop and aromatic appeal. The overall presentation is clean and minimalist, emphasizing the freshness and simplicity of the ingredients. The bowl rests on a light reclaimed wood table, illuminated by soft natural light, with an undyed linen napkin draped nearby and a simple wooden spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with slices of dark rye bread.
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion. Place it in a small bowl.
Add white vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt to the onion. Let it quick-pickle for 15 minutes.
Thinly slice the cucumbers.
In a small bowl, whisk together minced garlic, mustard, olive oil, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine the salad greens, sliced cucumbers, and the drained quick-pickled red onions.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Add the chopped fresh dill.
Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb Roasted Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest serving of Herb Roasted Chicken and Vegetables sits on an off-white, rustic ceramic plate. One roasted chicken thigh, with crispy golden-brown skin, is positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent to the chicken is a generous, natural pile of roasted potato wedges, carrot chunks, and soft onion wedges. The vegetables exhibit varied golden-brown and caramelized edges, showcasing their tender texture. Scattered among the vegetables are a few fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves. A small amount of rich, glossy pan juices collects at the bottom of the plate, mingling with the roasted elements. The plate is placed on a well-worn, light wooden dining table. A simple, casually folded cloth napkin and a clear glass of water are visible in the background, out of focus. Warm, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the comforting home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Cut carrots into 3 cm chunks. Cut onion into 2 cm wedges.
Peel and smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, carrot chunks, onion wedges, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Pour chicken broth into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Smoked Chicken Salad with Fermented Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a vibrant, fresh salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, showcasing a minimalistic, natural aesthetic. A bed of mixed salad greens, featuring diverse textures from crisp rocket to tender butter lettuce, forms the base. Irregularly halved, jewel-toned fermented cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout, their glossy skins reflecting light. Small, rustic chunks of smoked chicken, with a subtle golden-brown exterior, are nestled among the greens, not fanned. Delicate, translucent curls of shaved parmesan cheese are artfully draped over the top, adding a creamy contrast. A light sheen of vinaigrette coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural colors. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting the fresh textures and organic composition.
instructions: Wash cherry tomatoes. Pierce each tomato once with a skewer or knife.
Slice red onion thinly. Lightly smash garlic cloves.
In a clean jar, layer tomatoes, red onion slices, garlic, and fresh dill/parsley.
Dissolve sea salt in filtered water to make a 3% brine (15g salt per 500ml water).
Pour brine over ingredients in the jar, ensuring everything is submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Seal the jar loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp the jar daily if not using an airlock.
Once fermented, store in the refrigerator.
Wash and dry salad greens. Tear larger leaves into bite-sized pieces.
Dice smoked chicken breast into small, irregular chunks.
Halve the fermented cherry tomatoes. Reserve 15ml of brine for the dressing.
Shave parmesan cheese using a vegetable peeler.
In a small bowl, whisk together extra virgin olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, and honey/maple syrup (if using).
Add the reserved fermented tomato brine to the dressing. Season with black pepper. Whisk until emulsified.
In a large mixing bowl, gently combine salad greens and fermented tomatoes.
Add diced smoked chicken.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.

Divide salad among four individual plates. Arrange ingredients artfully, ensuring all components are visible. Top each serving with shaved parmesan. Garnish with a few fresh dill sprigs or parsley leaves if desired.
notes: Fermentation time for tomatoes can vary based on room temperature and desired tanginess; taste daily.
Adjust dressing sweetness and tanginess to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Beef Tomato Pot
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic chicken and beef tomato pot is presented in a deep, slightly imperfect ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy finish. Thick, browned chunks of beef and chicken are nestled within a rich, deep red tomato sauce, speckled with soft, diced carrots, celery, and onion. The sauce has a hearty, slightly viscous texture. A scattering of roughly chopped fresh green parsley rests on top. The bowl is placed on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, revealing natural grain. Beside the bowl, a simple, silver spoon rests on a casually draped off-white cloth napkin. A thick slice of crusty, golden-brown bread with an open crumb is placed nearby. Warm, soft light emanates from an unseen kitchen fixture, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the comforting textures of the dish. The background suggests a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches until well seared on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chicken chunks to the same pot. Brown chicken until golden. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onion, diced carrots, and diced celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape bottom of pot to loosen browned bits.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, dried oregano, and bay leaf.
Return browned beef and chicken to the pot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover.
Cook for 1.5 - 2 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: This dish is excellent served over pasta, polenta, or mashed potatoes for a complete meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Carne (Beef and Rice)
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of Arroz con Carne fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Tender, irregularly shaped beef chunks are naturally mixed with plump long-grain rice and soft, stewed diced tomato pieces. The dish boasts a warm, reddish-brown hue. Visible throughout are small pieces of diced onion and bell pepper, adding subtle color and texture. A generous sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh green parsley garnishes the top, providing a vibrant contrast. The bowl rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, everyday ceramic plate and a loosely folded off-white cloth napkin are casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, hinting at a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot directly from the pot or in individual bowls.
Offer crusty bread on the side for dipping.
instructions: Cut beef into 2.5 cm cubes. Pat beef dry. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Dice onions. Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic. Dice bell pepper. Add minced garlic and diced bell pepper to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in smoked paprika and cumin. Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot. Add chopped tomatoes and beef broth.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is tender.
Stir in rice. Bring back to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes off heat.
Fluff with a fork. Roughly chop fresh parsley. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Adjust liquid if rice absorbs too quickly; add a splash of hot water or broth if needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Chicken, Ricotta, and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of baked rigatoni is presented in a shallow, round white porcelain bowl. The top crust is a rich golden-brown, showing bubbling, melted mozzarella and hints of browned ricotta. Visible rigatoni tubes, diced chicken pieces, and a vibrant red-orange tomato sauce peek through the cheese. A light scattering of fresh, finely chopped rosemary adds a touch of green. The dish is placed on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the bowl, with standard silver cutlery. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft, appealing shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting, clean and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the food. The chicken is diced into 1.5 cm cubes, and the onion is finely diced, showcasing refined knife work. The composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space around the hearty portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot directly from the oven.
Accompanied by a simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in any leftover sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Dice chicken breast into 1.5 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Sear until golden and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and milk. Bring to a simmer. Add cooked chicken. Stir to combine. Season sauce with salt, pepper, and a few rosemary leaves, finely chopped.
In a separate bowl, combine ricotta cheese, egg, 25g of grated Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spread a thin layer of chicken and tomato sauce on the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Arrange half of the cooked rigatoni over the sauce layer.
Dollop half of the ricotta mixture over the pasta. Sprinkle with half of the shredded mozzarella.
Add the remaining rigatoni. Top with the remaining chicken and tomato sauce.
Dollop the remaining ricotta mixture. Sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella and the remaining 25g of grated Parmesan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chickpea & Pickled Mushroom Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Chickpea & Pickled Mushroom Salad is presented in a handcrafted, shallow ceramic bowl with an earthy cream glaze. A generous bed of vibrant mixed seasonal greens forms the base. Artfully scattered over the greens are tender, whole chickpeas, their light beige contrasting with the thinly sliced, subtly pink pickled red onions and the firm, thinly sliced pickled cremini mushrooms. The ingredients are loosely arranged, allowing natural negative space around each component. A light drizzle of the lemon-herb vinaigrette is visible, glistening on the surfaces. Fresh, finely chopped parsley and dill are sprinkled throughout, adding flecks of bright green. The overall presentation is clean, minimalist, and ingredient-focused, celebrating natural textures and colors. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the freshness of the ingredients.
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat.
Place thinly sliced mushrooms and thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar or bowl. Pour hot pickling liquid over them. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Rinse and drain cooked chickpeas well.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, aquafaba, minced garlic, salt, and pepper until emulsified.
In a large mixing bowl, combine rinsed chickpeas, drained pickled mushrooms, and drained pickled red onion. Add chopped parsley and chopped dill.
Add mixed greens to the bowl. Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately.
notes: The leftover pickling liquid can be reused for other vegetables.
Aquafaba from canned chickpeas can be saved for other vegan recipes like meringues or mayonnaise.

recipes.recipe_name: Tex-Mex Beef and Potato Hash
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Tex-Mex Beef and Potato Hash is centrally mounded on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The hash showcases golden-brown, pan-fried 1.5 cm potato cubes, tender 2-3 cm seared beef chunks, and vibrant 1.5 cm diced red and green bell peppers, interspersed with diced onion and sliced pickled jalapenos. The ingredients are well-mixed, creating a rich tapestry of color and texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh cilantro garnishes the top, and two fresh lime wedges are placed alongside. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
A dollop of sour cream or crema
A side of salsa verde

ingredients.name: Beef sirloin or chuck, cut into 2-3 cm cubes
Potatoes (Russet or Yukon Gold), diced into 1.5 cm cubes
Bell peppers (mixed colors), diced into 1.5 cm cubes
Pickled jalapeno chilies, sliced or roughly chopped

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat half of the olive oil in a large, heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Brown beef cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Remove beef from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining olive oil to the skillet. Add diced potatoes. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden-brown and tender.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the skillet with the potatoes. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, ground cumin, chili powder, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return browned beef to the skillet. Add pickled jalapeno chilies. Stir to combine all ingredients.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. If the mixture appears too dry, add a splash of beef broth.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot and Carrot Salad with Coffee-Chocolate Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with ample negative space. A vibrant bed of deep green mixed greens forms the base. Scattered artistically atop are rich purple 2 cm beetroot wedges and bright orange 2 cm carrot slices, both exhibiting a slight caramelization from roasting. Thinly sliced, delicate red onion rings are interspersed throughout, adding a subtle pop of color and sharpness. Roughly chopped, toasted walnuts are sprinkled generously, providing a textural contrast. The entire salad is glistening with a dark, glossy coffee-chocolate vinaigrette, which is evenly distributed and visually integrated with the ingredients, reflecting the natural light. The colors are balanced and appealing, with the deep tones of the roasted vegetables and dressing contrasting with the fresh greens. The arrangement is organic and flowing, not overly structured, giving a professional yet approachable feel. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Peel beetroots and carrots. Cut beetroots into 2 cm wedges. Cut carrots into 2 cm thick slices.
Toss beetroots and carrots with 60ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
While vegetables roast, toast walnuts. Spread walnuts on a separate baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until fragrant. Let cool, then roughly chop.
For the dressing, combine coffee, milk, and sugar in a small saucepan. Heat gently over medium-low heat until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Add finely chopped dark chocolate. Stir until melted and smooth.
Let the coffee-chocolate mixture cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Whisk in balsamic vinegar and Dijon mustard.
Slowly drizzle in 100ml olive oil while whisking constantly until the dressing is emulsified. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Thinly slice the red onion.
In a large bowl, combine cooled roasted beetroots, carrots, mixed greens, chopped walnuts, and thinly sliced red onion.
Pour the coffee-chocolate vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Divide the salad among four plates. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Rojo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo Rojo is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The main focus is a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its skin crisp and glistening, resting atop a generous mound of vibrant reddish-orange rice. The rice is moist and tender, with visible diced carrots and flecks of herbs providing textural and color contrast. A light scattering of freshly chopped green cilantro garnishes the chicken and rice. The plating is clean and inviting, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. A small stack of warm corn tortillas and a lime wedge are placed nearby, enhancing the authentic Mexican presentation. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Accompany with a simple salsa fresca or pickled jalapeños.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast rice for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly translucent.
In a blender, combine Roma tomatoes, chicken broth, tomato paste, chili powder, cumin, and oregano. Blend until smooth.
Pour tomato mixture into the pot with the rice and vegetables. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove bay leaf. Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chipotle Chicken with Roasted Corn and Bell Pepper
recipes.visual_description: A single, home-style portion of Skillet Chipotle Chicken with Roasted Corn and Bell Pepper is presented on an earthy-toned ceramic plate. A bed of fresh, vibrant green salad leaves forms the base. Warm, seared chicken chunks, roasted bell pepper strips showing slight charring, bright yellow corn kernels, and halved red cherry tomatoes are piled naturally and casually atop the greens. The colors are rich and natural: deep browns from seared chicken, varied reds and yellows from bell peppers and tomatoes, and bright greens from salad and cilantro garnish. A few fresh cilantro leaves are scattered over the top. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A stack of warm corn tortillas, a small bowl of lime wedges, and simple, rustic flatware are casually arranged nearby. Warm, inviting natural light fills the scene, reflecting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for wrapping.
Offer extra lime wedges for squeezing.
A side of simple rice or black beans complements the meal.

ingredients.name: Salad greens (e.g., romaine or mixed greens)

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Pat dry.
Season chicken chunks with salt, black pepper, chipotle powder, cumin, and oregano. Toss to coat.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
While chicken cooks, cut bell peppers into 2 cm strips. Halve cherry tomatoes. Mince garlic.
Add bell pepper strips and corn kernels to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp and lightly charred. Add minced garlic during the last minute of cooking. Stir well.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with the vegetables. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Stir to combine and warm through, about 1-2 minutes.
Divide salad greens among four plates. Top each with an equal portion of the warm chicken and vegetable mixture.
Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and serve immediately with lime wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Kopytka z Sosem Śmietanowo-Cebulowym
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of Kopytka z Sosem Śmietanowo-Cebulowym is presented in an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic bowl. The Kopytka, which are irregular, diamond-shaped potato dumplings, are piled casually in the center. They have a soft, pale yellow-white color. A creamy, off-white sauce, generously spooned over the dumplings, pools slightly at the bottom of the bowl. Visible within the sauce are translucent, finely diced onion pieces and vibrant green specks of fresh dill. The dish is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple fork and spoon rest casually beside the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, comfortable family dining atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the hearty, comforting food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with a side of pickled cucumbers (ogórki kiszone).
instructions: Boil potatoes until very tender. Drain well. Mash thoroughly. Let cool completely.
On a clean surface, combine mashed potatoes, egg, and a pinch of salt. Gradually add flour. Mix until a soft, pliable dough forms. Do not overmix.
Divide dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion into a long cylinder, about 2 cm thick.
Cut cylinders diagonally into 2-3 cm pieces. These are kopytka.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add kopytka in batches.
Cook kopytka until they float to the surface, then cook for 1-2 more minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well.
For the sauce, melt butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onions. Sauté until very soft and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Pour in vegetable broth and cream. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Season sauce with salt and pepper. Stir in chopped dill.
Add cooked kopytka to the sauce. Toss gently to coat. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure potatoes are completely cool before mixing with flour to avoid a sticky dough.
Do not overwork the dough to keep kopytka tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Roasted Chicken with Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, left whole, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Around the chicken, a scattering of roasted small potato halves or quarters, their skins slightly blistered and interiors tender, display varying shades of golden-brown. Interspersed among the potatoes are vibrant, burst red cherry tomato halves, some caramelized at the edges. Several smashed garlic cloves, soft and sweet, are visible. Fresh green sprigs of rosemary and thyme are artfully placed for color and aroma. A light sheen of pan juices coats the elements, reflecting the natural light. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a neatly folded light cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are arranged. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere, with natural, even lighting illuminating the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add potatoes, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme.
Season potatoes with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast potatoes in the oven for 20 minutes.
Remove skillet from oven. Stir potatoes. Nestle chicken thighs back into the skillet among the potatoes.
Add halved cherry tomatoes around chicken and potatoes.
Pour white wine (or chicken broth) into the skillet.
Return skillet to oven. Roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden. Ensure chicken is cooked through.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken & Potato Ragout with Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Chicken & Potato Ragout is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The central focus is a whole, deeply seared chicken thigh, coated in a rich, reddish-orange tomato and hot sauce. Plump, glossy orzo pasta, infused with the braising liquid, is nestled around the chicken. Scattered artfully over the dish are golden, irregularly cut crispy potato wedges, some with subtly charred edges, adding textural contrast. A vibrant sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, indicative of a modern bistro setting. Beside the main plate, a small, separate white rice bowl holds fluffy white steamed basmati rice. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed alongside. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its varied textures and warm colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, hot sauce, and dried oregano. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and crispy.
Stir orzo pasta into the braising liquid with the chicken. Cook uncovered for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until orzo is al dente and most liquid is absorbed.
Cook basmati rice according to package instructions.
Ladle braised chicken and orzo onto individual plates. Top each serving with crispy roasted potato wedges. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with a side of steamed basmati rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mozzarella Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Mozzarella Penne is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. Al dente penne pasta, coated in a rich, creamy white sauce, forms the base. Succulent, golden-brown chicken chunks, approximately 3 cm, are nestled among the pasta. Vibrant green spinach leaves are wilted throughout the dish. Melted mozzarella cheese creates delicate, stringy strands. The dish is garnished with a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese and a few fresh, bright green basil leaves. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook penne according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserve 60 ml pasta water.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, reaching 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add finely diced onion to the same pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in milk.
Reduce heat to low. Add shredded mozzarella. Stir until cheese melts and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked penne, cooked chicken, and fresh spinach to the sauce. Toss to combine. Spinach will wilt quickly.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmesan and fresh basil, if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency with reserved pasta water as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle al Ragu di Manzo
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Pappardelle al Ragu di Manzo is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain pasta bowl. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are thoroughly coated in the rich, deep reddish-brown ragu sauce. Tender, fork-shredded beef chunks are visibly intertwined with the pasta and sauce. Sliced mushrooms and finely diced vegetables from the slow-cooked sauce add subtle texture and color variation. The dish is garnished with a generous mound of freshly grated pale yellow Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese and a sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A classic silver fork and spoon are neatly placed to the right of the bowl, and a folded cotton napkin lies to the left. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer extra Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a full-bodied red wine.

ingredients.name: Fresh flat-leaf parsley
ingredients.quantity: a small bunch, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Do in batches if needed. Remove beef from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Bring to a simmer. Cook until wine reduces by half, about 5 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove beef from pot. Shred beef using two forks. Discard herb sprigs and bay leaf from sauce.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well. Season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly.
Serve immediately in bowls. Garnish generously with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Slow cooking the ragu allows the flavors to deepen and the beef to become incredibly tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Olive-Garlic Confit and Basil Stem Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken sits on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate, possibly off-white or light grey, with ample negative space. The chicken, a golden-brown thigh or drumstick, is presented as a whole, succulent piece. Alongside are thick chunks of roasted seasonal root vegetables, like caramelized carrots and potatoes, their edges slightly browned. Glistening, unpeeled confit garlic cloves and plump, unpitted olives are generously spooned over and around the chicken, reflecting the soft natural light. A vibrant sprinkle of green basil stem gremolata adds a fresh, textural contrast. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood or stone surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is gently folded beside the plate. The background is minimalist and clean, with soft natural light illuminating the scene, highlighting the dish's natural colors and textures.

ingredients.name: Whole chicken
ingredients.quantity: 1 (approx. 1.5 kg), cut into 4-6 pieces, or 4-6 chicken thighs/drumsticks

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1 large bunch (leaves for gremolata, stems for gremolata or stock)

ingredients.name: Seasonal root vegetables
ingredients.quantity: 500 g (e.g., carrots, parsnips, small potatoes), cut into thick chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
For the confit, combine unpeeled garlic cloves and olives in a small oven-safe dish. Pour 250 ml olive oil over them. Ensure garlic and olives are submerged. If not, add more oil.
Place chicken pieces and root vegetable chunks in a large roasting pan. Drizzle lightly with olive oil. Add the confit dish to the roasting pan or place it on a separate rack in the oven.

Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden brown. Vegetables should be tender and caramelized. Baste chicken and vegetables occasionally with pan juices.
While chicken roasts, prepare gremolata. Roughly chop basil leaves. Finely mince basil stems. Combine chopped basil leaves, minced basil stems, and lemon zest. Season with a pinch of salt.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and roasted vegetables with generous spoonfuls of the warm olive-garlic confit. Sprinkle basil stem gremolata over the dish before serving.
notes: The olive oil from the confit can be strained and reused for cooking or dressings. It will be infused with garlic and olive flavor.
Basil stems are often discarded but add peppery flavor and texture to the gremolata, reducing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato-Onion Conserve
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, golden-brown with a crisp exterior, rests on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, unsliced. Beside it, a vibrant mound of deep red and orange tomato-onion conserve, rich in color and texture, provides a visual counterpoint. A small, concentrated dollop of off-white fermented garlic paste is positioned thoughtfully near the chicken. A neat cluster of deep green, gently wilted Swiss chard leaves adds a fresh, earthy element. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the ingredients, emphasizing their natural forms and colors. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting textures. The background is uncluttered, subtly featuring a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare tomato-onion conserve: Dice tomatoes into 1.5cm cubes. Thinly slice then dice red onion. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add diced tomatoes, thyme sprigs, apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened into a jam-like consistency. Remove thyme sprigs.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken thighs thoroughly dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.

Sear chicken: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Once oil shimmers, carefully place chicken thighs in the pan. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, undisturbed, until golden brown and a crisp crust forms. Continue cooking until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Cook greens: In the same pan used for chicken, add 50ml water. Add seasonal greens. Sauté briefly over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until just wilted. Season with a pinch of salt.

Plate the dish: Place one seared chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon a generous portion of the tomato-onion conserve beside the chicken. Add a small dollop of fermented garlic paste next to the chicken or conserve. Arrange a neat cluster of the wilted seasonal greens on the plate. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainability through the use of fermented ingredients (fermented garlic paste), which is a preservation technique, and by encouraging the use of seasonal greens. Consider sourcing chicken and vegetables from local farms to further reduce environmental impact.

To make your own fermented garlic paste: Peel garlic cloves and place in a clean jar. Cover completely with a 2% brine solution (20g salt per 1 liter water). Seal loosely to allow gas release. Ferment at room temperature for 1-2 weeks until desired tanginess is achieved, then blend into a paste.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents seared boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into generous 5cm chunks, coated in a rich, creamy sauce. The golden-brown chicken pieces are nestled amongst vibrant green wilted spinach and ruby-red sun-dried tomato halves. The sauce, a harmonious blend of cream and Parmesan, gently clings to all components, showcasing a velvety texture. Garnished with fresh chopped Italian parsley, the dish offers a delightful contrast of colors and textures. It is served in a clean, white porcelain dinner plate on a simple wooden table, accompanied by classic Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting, rustic elegance. A single portion is thoughtfully arranged with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve alongside a simple green salad.
Serve over pasta, such as tagliatelle or penne.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut each thigh into 2-3 large chunks (approx. 5cm pieces). Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Stir in heavy cream and dried oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Return cooked chicken pieces to the pan. Toss to coat them in the creamy sauce. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Mole Poblano served on a clean white porcelain plate. The centerpiece is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh completely coated in a thick, velvety, dark reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce appears glossy and rich with visible texture from ground seeds and spices. Toasted white sesame seeds are sprinkled evenly over the chicken. Three small sprigs of fresh cilantro and four thin rings of raw red onion provide a vibrant color contrast. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy Mexican red rice is positioned. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small basket of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a colorful woven cloth and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas served in a traditional cloth-lined basket
Mexican red rice (arroz rojo)
Refried beans topped with crumbled queso fresco
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from all dried chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl of hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Toast almonds, 15g of sesame seeds, and the cinnamon stick in a dry pan until golden.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic in a dry pan until blackened in spots.
Drain chilies and place in a blender with toasted nuts, spices, and charred vegetables.
Add 100ml of chicken stock and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil in a large pot. Add the mole paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the remaining chicken stock and chopped dark chocolate. Simmer on low heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear in a separate pan until the skin is golden brown.
Transfer chicken to the mole sauce. Simmer until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Adjust seasoning with salt if necessary.
notes: Do not burn the chilies during toasting or the sauce will become bitter.
The mole sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C at the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Avocado Pasta with Roasted Tomatoes and Soft-Boiled Eggs
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy avocado pasta is served in a rustic, off-white ceramic bowl, centered on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. The spaghetti is loosely twirled, coated in a pale green, smooth avocado sauce. Scattered amongst the pasta are vibrant, slightly shriveled roasted cherry tomato halves, their reds contrasting with the pasta's green. Perched naturally on top of the pasta is a halved soft-boiled egg, revealing a bright, jammy yellow yolk surrounded by firm white. Fresh, whole basil leaves are casually scattered over the dish, adding pops of deep green. A simple silver fork rests beside the bowl on a casually draped, cream-colored cloth napkin. The scene is lit with soft, warm light, creating a cozy and inviting home kitchen atmosphere with minimal, natural background elements.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until softened and slightly browned.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, prepare avocado sauce. Halve and pit avocados. Scoop flesh into a food processor. Add peeled garlic cloves, remaining 45 ml olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Process until smooth and creamy. Add a splash of pasta water if needed to reach desired consistency.
For soft-boiled eggs, carefully lower eggs into boiling water for 6-7 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Peel gently.

Drain cooked pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water. Return pasta to the pot. Add avocado sauce and roasted tomatoes. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water as needed to create a smooth sauce that coats the pasta.
Divide pasta among 4 bowls. Halve each soft-boiled egg. Place one egg half on top of each pasta serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and optional grated Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Southwestern Seared Chicken and Corn Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Southwestern Chicken and Corn Salad presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. Thick chunks of golden-brown seared chicken are arranged atop a bed of crisp, verdant mixed salad greens. Interspersed are bright red and yellow diced bell peppers, plump golden corn kernels, and halved ruby-red cherry tomatoes. Freshly chopped green cilantro is generously sprinkled over the dish, with a few lime wedges placed strategically on the side. The chicken shows a perfectly caramelized crust. The overall composition is fresh, colorful, and inviting. The bowl rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant hues, with a subtle, blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crispy tortilla chips.
Offer sliced avocado or a dollop of fresh salsa as an accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Cut into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken evenly with salt, black pepper, chili powder, smoked paprika, and ground cumin.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C), about 6-8 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice bell peppers into 1 cm pieces. Halve cherry tomatoes. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced bell peppers and corn kernels. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute more until fragrant.
In a large bowl, combine cooked chicken chunks, sautéed bell peppers and corn, halved cherry tomatoes, and chopped cilantro. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the mixture. Toss gently to combine.
Arrange mixed salad greens on individual serving plates. Spoon the chicken and corn mixture generously over the greens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Spaghetti
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of Chicken Cacciatore with Spaghetti is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. A mound of golden spaghetti forms the base, topped with two whole, braised chicken thighs. The chicken is coated in a rich, chunky tomato sauce, flecked with visible diced red and green bell peppers and onions. The sauce has a deep red hue, contrasting with the tender, golden-brown chicken skin. Fresh, roughly chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the dish, adding a touch of green. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, sturdy silver fork rests casually beside the plate. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper to the skillet. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened, creating a soffritto base.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine (or chicken broth). Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and is very tender.
While chicken simmers, cook spaghetti according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
Taste cacciatore sauce and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve chicken cacciatore over a bed of spaghetti. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Garlic Mushrooms and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken fillet, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously topped with a creamy, rich sauce of tender, earthy brown sliced cremini mushrooms and minced garlic. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of crispy, golden-brown roasted potato wedges, approximately 2 cm thick, is arranged. Flecks of dark green chopped fresh parsley and tiny rosemary needles are scattered over the dish, adding vibrant color. The plate sits on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and appealing colors, with a subtle, blurred bistro-style background creating a casual dining atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm thick wedges. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, 1 sprig chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crispy.
Pat chicken fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken fillets. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic. Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer for 1 minute until wine is reduced by half.
Stir in heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley. Return chicken to the skillet with the creamy mushroom sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken. Garnish with chopped parsley and a fresh rosemary sprig.
Serve chicken immediately with roasted rosemary potatoes on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown roasted chicken, a bone-in, skin-on thigh, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are quartered roasted baby potatoes, their skins lightly crisped and interiors tender. Halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes and whole, glossy Kalamata olives are interspersed among the potatoes, adding bursts of color and texture. Fresh sprigs of oregano and thyme are artfully placed over and around the chicken, providing a verdant contrast. A few thin lemon wedges are nestled on the side, ready for squeezing. The dish exhibits a natural, rustic elegance, with ingredients scattered organically rather than rigidly arranged. The colors are warm and inviting, showcasing the chicken's crispy skin and the rich hues of the vegetables. The plate has appropriate negative space, presented on a simple wooden surface with natural, soft lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Halve or quarter baby potatoes, depending on size. Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice one lemon into thin wedges. Juice the second lemon.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, halved tomatoes, Kalamata olives, minced garlic, oregano sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Add chicken thighs to the pan. Drizzle all ingredients with olive oil. Toss gently to coat everything.
Pour chicken broth and lemon juice into the pan.
Arrange lemon wedges among the ingredients.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be tender.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Simple Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of pan-seared chicken breast is plated centrally on an off-white, everyday ceramic dinner plate with subtle natural imperfections. The chicken is a whole, thick piece, deeply golden-brown from searing, with visible crust. It rests slightly off-center. Alongside, a generous scattering of halved, roasted new potatoes, their skins slightly crisped and golden, showing tender interiors. Vibrant green blanched green beans are casually arranged beside the potatoes, their natural shape maintained. A glossy, light pan sauce, infused with garlic and lemon, is spooned generously over the chicken. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, roughly chopped green parsley. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Standard metal flatware (fork and knife) is casually placed next to the plate. Lighting is soft, warm, and inviting, creating a homely atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.

ingredients.name: New potatoes or small red potatoes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and halve potatoes. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread evenly on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until vibrant green. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again thoroughly.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside on a plate. Keep warm.
Add butter and minced garlic to the same skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Pour in chicken broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the sauce slightly reduces.
Add blanched green beans to the skillet. Toss to coat them in the pan sauce.
Serve each chicken breast with a portion of roasted potatoes and green beans. Spoon the pan sauce over the chicken. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot and Walnut Salad with Fermented Plum Dressing and Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic plate, showcasing a minimalistic and natural composition. Diced ruby-red beetroot forms a vibrant base, interspersed with golden-brown diced chicken pieces, ensuring a vegetable-forward focus with a small protein accent. Translucent, thinly sliced pickled red onions add a contrasting purple hue and crisp texture. Fresh, finely chopped cilantro and parsley are scattered generously. The salad is artfully arranged with natural spacing, allowing each component to be distinctly visible. A rich, reddish-brown fermented plum dressing is drizzled elegantly over the top. The dish is garnished with toasted, roughly chopped walnuts and glistening ruby-red pomegranate seeds, adding crunch and color. The entire plate is visible with ample negative space. It sits on a light reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin and simple rustic utensils, creating an eco-conscious and authentic Georgian dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a traditional Georgian 'supra' (feast).
Accompanied by freshly baked Georgian puri bread.
Can be served family-style for sharing.

ingredients.name: Red onion, small, thinly sliced (for pickling)

instructions: Prepare Pickled Onions: In a small pot, combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve. Pour hot liquid over thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Roast Beetroot: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wrap washed beetroots individually in foil. Roast for 45-60 minutes, or until tender. Let cool. Peel and dice into 1.5cm cubes.

Prepare Chicken: Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest for 5 minutes. Dice into 1.5cm cubes.
Toast Walnuts: Place walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast for 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant. Let cool. Roughly chop.
Make Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together fermented sour plum paste, walnut oil, minced garlic, and water until smooth. Season with salt.
Assemble Salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine diced beetroot, diced chicken, chopped cilantro, chopped parsley, minced garlic, and drained pickled red onions.
Dress and Serve: Add dressing to the salad mixture. Gently toss to combine. Transfer to serving plates. Garnish with toasted walnuts and pomegranate seeds.
notes: If available, use beetroot greens by sautéing them lightly and adding to the salad for a zero-waste approach.
For deeper flavor, prepare pickled red onions at least 24 hours in advance.
traditional_techniques: Fermentation (for plum paste and pickled onions)

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Garlic Herb Chicken with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Tuscan Garlic Herb Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, seared boneless chicken thighs, cooked whole, are positioned centrally. They are surrounded by a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables: bright red and yellow bell pepper strips, tender green zucchini rounds, caramelized red onion wedges, and burst cherry tomatoes. The vegetables show slight charring on their edges, indicating proper roasting. A glossy, dark balsamic glaze is artfully drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered lightly across the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plating is organized but natural, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a polished fork and knife are neatly placed. A crumpled white cotton napkin rests beside the flatware. In the soft-focused background, a small rustic bowl of assorted olives and a slice of crusty ciabatta bread evoke an authentic Italian casual dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the pan juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
Enjoy with a glass of Tuscan red wine, such as Chianti.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Cut zucchini into 2 cm thick rounds. Cut bell peppers into 3 cm wide strips. Cut red onion into 2 cm wedges.

In a large bowl, combine zucchini, bell peppers, red onion, cherry tomatoes, minced garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Drizzle with remaining 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in the skillet. Place seared chicken thighs on top of the vegetables.
Roast 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Remove skillet from oven. Transfer chicken and vegetables to a serving platter. Cover to keep warm.
Place skillet over medium heat on stovetop. Add white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly reduced.
Drizzle chicken and vegetables with balsamic glaze. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Confit Chicken with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, whole and plump, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken skin is visibly crisp, showcasing its rich, deep color. Around the chicken, an artful but uncrowded arrangement of roasted root vegetables – rustic wedges of carrots and parsnips, and halved small potatoes – display their caramelized edges and soft interiors. Translucent, tender confit garlic cloves are nestled among the vegetables. A glossy, reduced pan sauce with mashed confit garlic is drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a vibrant contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a minimal, softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful pan sauce and confit garlic oil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

For garlic confit: Place 20-25 peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with 250 ml olive oil. Heat gently over low heat. Simmer for 20-25 minutes until garlic is very tender. Do not brown. Set aside.
Prepare vegetables: In a large bowl, toss carrots, parsnips, and potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, 2 sprigs of thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Season chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken: Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.

Add vegetables and roast: Transfer skillet to oven with the baking sheet of vegetables. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender. Add rosemary sprigs to the vegetables halfway through roasting.

Make pan sauce: Remove chicken and vegetables from skillet. Set aside. Drain excess fat, leaving 1-2 tablespoons. Add minced garlic to skillet. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
